docs.title: 2D Tower Defense Maker
docs.text:
A Unity 6 toolkit for building tower defense games in 2D (URP): enemies follow authored paths, the player builds towers on fixed slots, barracks soldiers physically block enemies, a controllable hero fights on the road, and spells, status effects and an economy tie it together.

2D Tower Defense Maker is split into a deterministic, engine-independent simulation core and a Unity view/authoring layer, plus a set of editor tools for paths, waves and upgrade trees.

docs.title: Create your game first
docs.text: The Maker is the reusable runtime and authoring tools. The Samples add-on is a separate, optional reference game with its own art, balance and campaign. Install the Maker, open Welcome > New Level, and use Fresh starter assets to create independent content in Assets/TDMakerContent/. Browse the sample game only when you want an example. See the package boundaries and installation order.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
Gameplay (simulation core)

  • Fixed-tick simulation (30 Hz by default), deterministic for a given seed and input stream; command recording and replay.
  • Paths with any number of parallel sub-lanes; entry/exit markers; lane selection per spawn (fixed, round-robin, random).
  • Wave timeline model: waves → groups (per path, start delay) → spawn entries (count, interval, delays, alternating enemy types).
  • Early wave calls with a gold reward and optional spell-cooldown credit.
  • Tower families with branching upgrades (any tier can list several next tiers) and purchasable ability ranks.
  • Barracks that keep a squad of soldiers alive, respawn them and let the player move the rally point; soldiers block enemies.
  • Heroes with experience, levels, skills (auto-unlock or spend-points), respawn and click-to-move.
  • Spells (reinforcements, area strikes, lingering areas) with cooldowns, unlock waves and shared target-point validation.
  • Damage kinds: physical, magical, true, explosion, electric, poison; armor / magic resist as fractional reductions; pierce; area falloff.
  • Status effects: slows, stuns, damage over time, healing over time, shields, armor shifts, damage multipliers, range/attack/blocking/targeting modifiers; ranks, families, stacking rules, immunities.
  • Mechanic library: chain and multi-target attacks, impact payloads, damage/healing pulses, tag filters, traps and automatic mine fields, channelled beams, reflection/life steal, companions and on-site revival (same-unit returns, successors and body raising).
  • Five target priorities per tower (First, Last, Strongest, Weakest, Closest), switchable at runtime.
  • One range rule everywhere: an ellipse with horizontal radius r and vertical radius k·r, used for checks and display.
  • Extension points: custom systems, custom per-entity data, target selectors, damage hooks, ability actions, commands and events.
  • No per-tick allocation in the core after startup; fixed-capacity pools.

Unity layer

  • ScriptableObject authoring for enemies, towers, soldiers, heroes, projectiles, status effects, spells, wave sets and levels.
  • Scene authoring components for paths and build slots.
  • SimulationRunner (fixed-step clock, capacities, built-in command recording and replay, template decorators), pooled entity views with interpolation, placeholder primitive sprites (no art required to start).
  • Production TextMesh Pro/uGUI GameHud for PC mouse and keyboard, themeable with a HudTheme asset and replaceable English/Korean string tables; damage numbers, pooled VFX and audio hooks, camera controller, player settings, mechanic feedback (chain arcs, pulse rings, shield bubbles).
  • Works with the Input System package or the legacy Input Manager.

Editor tools

  • New Level wizard and Welcome window; Map Editor with painted backgrounds, curve paths, build slots, snapping and previews.
  • Unit Workshop: every unit, projectile and effect in one window – presets, animation preview, mechanic cards, bulk frame registration, computed values and a headless sandbox.
  • Wave Timeline window.
  • Upgrade Tree window.
  • Inspectors with computed stats (DPS vs. armor, effective HP, investment and refunds, range ellipse).
  • Project Validator and headless Dry Run.
  • Campaign: a world map asset with level points and unlock rules (previous level, required levels, star gates, side branches), progress with best stars and a star total, three save slots (JSON files with versioned migration, atomic writes and kept backups; an optional PlayerPrefs-backed store), and ready-made world map and save slot screens with a map editor in the inspector.
  • Permanent star-upgrade shop: six sample tracks, ordered purchases, saved ranks, Undo/Reset and deterministic battle snapshots.
  • One-click sample content generator: three sample levels and a complete playable sample flow with title, save slots, world map, pause and result screens.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text: Item Value Unity 6000.0 LTS or newer Render pipeline Universal Render Pipeline (2D renderer), URP 17.x Packages URP, 2D Sprite and uGUI 2.0 (includes TextMesh Pro). Import TMP Essential Resources once in the buyer project; they are not redistributed. Input System is optional. Platform Developed for PC (mouse and keyboard). The core has no platform dependencies.

docs.title: Folder layout
docs.text:
Assets/TDMaker/
  Runtime/Core/     TDMaker.Core   – pure C# simulation (no UnityEngine references)
  Runtime/Unity/    TDMaker.Unity  – authoring assets, scene components, runner, views, HUD
  Editor/           TDMaker.Editor – editor windows, inspectors, validator, dry run, sample generator
  Samples/Basic/    Ready-to-play sample scene and its data assets
  Samples/Crossroads/ Second level: three merging entrances, a flying route, two heroes
  Samples/WindingPass/ Third level: one long road, armored and magic-resistant waves, mortar branches, a boss
  Samples/Demo/     Playable demo flow (title, save slots, world map of the sample campaign, pause and result screens)
  Samples/Extending/ Compiled extension examples (custom system, data, selector, damage hook, action, command)
  Documentation/    Online documentation links and third-party notices

Namespaces: TDMaker.Core.*, TDMaker.Unity.*, TDMaker.Editor.*. Global menus live under Tools > 2D Tower Defense Maker, asset creation under Assets > Create > 2D Tower Defense Maker.

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text:
1. Quick Start – build your own level or explore the optional samples (or the whole demo: Samples/Demo/DemoSample.unity), then build a first level with the New Level wizard in about 5 minutes (and see how it is made by hand).
  2. Concepts – how the simulation works (ticks, ranges, targeting, damage, economy).
  3. Authoring Reference – every asset and scene component, field by field.
  4. Editor Tools – path editor, Unit Workshop, Wave Timeline, Upgrade Tree, Validator, Dry Run.
  5. Mechanic Library – the built-in mechanic library (chains, multi-target, knockback, pulses, healing, shields, combat modifiers).
  6. Presentation – HUD, themes, typography, languages, VFX/audio hooks, camera and settings. Campaigns, Progress and Saves – campaign asset and world map, level progress and stars, save slots and the permanent upgrade shop.
  7. Extending the Framework – adding your own systems, data, targeting, damage rules, abilities and commands.
  8. Determinism and Replay, Performance, FAQ, Changelog.
  9. Support and licenses – troubleshooting information, third-party notices and included font licenses.

docs.title: Authoring Reference
docs.text:
All gameplay content is authored as ScriptableObjects (Create > 2D Tower Defense Maker > …) plus a few scene components (Add Component > 2D Tower Defense Maker > …). At Play, LevelAsset.Bake() turns them into immutable core definitions.

Units: distances in world units, times in game seconds, armor/resist values as fractions (0–1).

Contents: Common data · Enemy · Tower · Soldier · Hero · Projectile · Status Effect · Spell · Wave Set · Level · Scene components

The built-in mechanic blocks (chains, multi-target attacks, impact payloads and knockback, pulses, healing, shields, combat modifiers, traps, beams, reflection, life steal, path transfers, permanent auras, mine fields, companions and on-site revival) are described in Mechanic Library; HUD, feedback, camera and audio components in Presentation.

docs.title: Identity and view (all entity assets: Enemy, Tower, Soldier, Hero)
docs.text:
Field Meaning Template Id Unique id inside a level. Blank = asset name. Two assets with the same id in one level fail the bake. Display Name Name in menus. Blank = asset name. View > View Key Lookup key for views. Blank = template id. View > Prefab Optional prefab (pooled). With no prefab, a matching ArtSet entry supplies the sprite; otherwise a primitive is generated. View > Shape / Color / Size Placeholder sprite (Square, Circle, Diamond, Triangle, Keep, Bastion, Spire, Hall, Blob, Arrowhead, Hulk, Shield, Crest, Dart, Orb, Wing). View > Show Health Bar Draw a health bar. View > Shaded Generated sprites use the outlined, shaded style (off = flat silhouettes). View > Facing None, FlipSprite or ScaleX (for multi-sprite rigs) to face the movement direction. View > Drive Animator Drive an Animator on the prefab with the standard parameters (Presentation). View > Hooks Optional VFX prefabs and audio cues for spawn, attack, hit and death (Presentation). Extensions Optional TemplateExtensionAssets (your subclasses) that decorate the baked template, for example with custom data (Extending the Framework).

Tip: add an EntityView component to custom prefabs to control sorting and which renderer is tinted; it is added automatically otherwise.

docs.title: Damage
docs.text:
Field Meaning Kind Physical, Magical, True, Explosion, Electric, Poison. See Concepts – Damage pipeline. Minimum / Maximum Roll range. Radius 0 = single target; > 0 = area damage (range ellipse). Edge Multiplier Damage factor at the edge of the area, interpolated from 1 at the centre. Falloff DistanceEndpoints (max at centre → min at edge), RolledLinear (one roll × edge factor), ConstantMaximum. Physical Pierce / Magical Pierce Armor / magic resist ignored by this hit (subtracted). Effects Status effects attached to every unit this hit damages. Experience Rate Hero experience per point of health removed (hero attacks). Impact Optional payload after each resolved hit: secondary blast, residual region, knockback and/or a path transfer (Mechanic Library). Life Steal Optional healing of the attacker from the health this hit actually removes (Mechanic Library).

Secondary blasts and region pulses use the same fields without Impact and Life Steal (BasicDamageData), so payloads cannot nest.

docs.title: Melee
docs.text: Field Meaning Enabled Off = no melee slot. Soldiers without melee cannot block. Damage Damage per strike. Cooldown Seconds between strikes. Range Contact range (range ellipse).

docs.title: Ranged attack (list; each entry is an independent channel)
docs.text: Field Meaning Range Horizontal semi-axis r of the range ellipse; vertical is r × k. Minimum Range Inner exclusion radius. Cooldown Seconds between attacks. Damage Damage per hit. Projectile Projectile asset; empty = instant hit. Targets Flying / Targets Ground Eligible target types.

docs.title: Recovery (enemy regeneration, hero recovery)
docs.text: Field Meaning Enabled Turn recovery on. Amount / Interval Health per recovery tick and seconds between ticks. Damage Grace Seconds without taking damage before recovery starts. Idle Only Only while not moving or fighting. Turn off for enemies (they are never idle).

docs.title: Stat modifier (status effects and ability passives)
docs.text: Field Meaning Speed Scale Movement multiplier (0.6 = 40% slow, 0 = rooted). Output Scale Outgoing damage multiplier. Input Scale / Magical Input Scale Incoming damage multipliers. Physical Shift / Magical Shift / Poison Shift Added armor / resist (fraction, may be negative). Stun Stops movement and attacks while active. Combat Range Scale, Disable Attacks, Ignore Blocking, Untargetable (Mechanic Library).

docs.title: Enemy
docs.text:
Create > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Enemy (EnemyAsset). Required for every unit a wave spawns.

Group Field Meaning Vitals Health Maximum hit points. Physical Armor / Magical Armor / Poison Armor Damage reductions (0–1). Speed Units per second along the lane. Reward Gold Bounty when killed. Life Cost Lives lost when it leaks. Blocking Blockable Whether soldiers/heroes can block it. Blocker Capacity How many friendly units can hold it at once. Engagement Where blockers stand. Contact Bias X is this enemy's share of the horizontal gap (usually half its drawn body width plus a small gap), Y a signed world-Y shift; Row Spacing is the world-Y offset of the 2nd and 3rd blocker rows (they stand half of it closer). Blockers stand on the side the enemy walks toward, independent of melee range. Flying Flying units ignore blocking and can only be hit by attacks with Targets Flying. Combat Melee Attack used against blocking units. Ranged Attacks Optional attacks against friendly units (they pick the closest). Abilities Regeneration Recovery (keep Idle Only off). Melee Evasion Chance to dodge each incoming melee strike. Status Immunities Effect ids or families this unit ignores (e.g. slow). Mechanics Tags Tag bits matched by Required/Rejected Tags of status effects and mechanic Targets. Behavior Always-on action channels (same fields as ability actions), for example a periodic shield cast on nearby allies. Aura Area effect emitted when the unit appears. For a permanent aura enable Until Source Lost (and Follow Source): it lasts while the unit lives and is removed with it. May be pulse-only (heal or damage pulses without a status effect). Reflection Thorns: returns a Share of the health the unit actually loses to its attacker as one hit of Kind (Mechanic Library). Death Summon Enemies released where it dies (split); they continue along the path. Death Succession Successor rules for the released enemies: Chain Budget, Rise Duration, Bounty Policy, rise protection (Mechanic Library). Revive Return on the spot: Returns, Down Delay, Rise Duration, Return Share, Invulnerable / Untargetable While Rising, Clear Effects (Mechanic Library).

Inspector extras: effective HP against each damage kind and warnings (zero speed, full immunity). The validator warns about auras without a payload and auras that do not follow their unit, returns that never happen (Returns 0, no health back) and successor rules with nothing to release.

docs.title: Tower
docs.text:
Create > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Tower (TowerAsset). Each tier is a separate asset; tiers link through Upgrades.

Group Field Meaning Economy Cost Gold to build this tier, or to upgrade into it. Tree Upgrades Next tiers. One entry = linear upgrade; two or more = branch. Combat Ranged Attacks Attack channels. Target Priority Default priority: First, Last, Strongest, Weakest, Closest. Abilities Abilities Purchasable abilities (see below), usually on final branches. Barracks Soldier Assigning a Soldier asset turns this tier into a barracks. Soldier Count Living soldiers maintained. Rally Radius Maximum distance tower → rally point (range ellipse). Respawn Time Seconds before a fallen soldier is replaced. Formation Radius Spread of the idle formation around the rally point. Companions Companions Owner-bound escorts or a flying follower kept beside the tower; they leave when it is sold (see Hero > Companions and Mechanic Library). Text Description Shown in menus.

Only towers listed in the level's Available Towers can be built; their upgrade tiers, soldiers and projectiles are collected automatically. Sale refunds come from the level's Refund Share; the old per-tower Refund Ratio field is hidden and unused.

docs.title: Abilities (tower abilities and hero skills)
docs.text:
Abilities / Skills entries (AbilityData):

Field Meaning Id Ability id; blank = display name. Display Name / Description Button text and tooltip. Reset Cooldown On Purchase Reset this ability's timers whenever a rank is bought. Ranks Ranks in purchase order. Each rank replaces the previous rank's payload.

Each rank (AbilityRankData):

Field Meaning Cost Gold (tower) or skill points (hero). Required Level Hero skills only. Passive Stat modifier active while this rank is owned. Soldier Replacement Barracks only: living and future soldiers become this Soldier asset. Actions Timed action channels (below).

Each action (AbilityActionData) runs on its own cooldown; payloads can be combined:

Field Meaning Cooldown Seconds between activations. Initial Delay Delay before a newly bought channel can fire. Skill Experience Per Rank Hero only: experience per successful activation × rank (also for actions that only carry a chain, multi-target, trap, mine, beam, transfer, raise or custom payload). Use Attack + Attack Fire an extra ranged attack. Self Effect Status effect attached to the owner. Use Summon + Summon Create units (see Summon). Area Emit an area effect region at the owner (may be pulse-only). Use Chain + Chain Chained attack jumping between nearby enemies (Mechanic Library). Use Multi Target + Multi Target One activation hitting several targets (Mechanic Library). Use Trap + Trap Place a trap that arms, then triggers on nearby units (Mechanic Library). Use Beam + Beam Channel a continuous beam with an exact damage budget (Mechanic Library). Use Transfer + Transfer Move nearby enemies to an exact path point (Mechanic Library). Use Mines + Mines Throw a mine onto a lane node in a band around the actor; it arms after flight, landing and its arm delay (Mechanic Library). Use Raise + Raise Raise new units (enemy or soldier) from nearby bodies of the fallen (Mechanic Library). Custom Action Your own AbilityActionAsset subclass (Extending the Framework).

Chain, multi-target, trap, mine, beam, transfer, raise and custom payloads run together as one custom payload; the action counts as successful when any of them succeeds (for example a trap placed, a mine thrown, a body reserved or a beam started). Only successful activations restart the cooldown and award skill experience.

Tip: the tower inspector shows DPS against several armor values, range-ellipse size, cumulative investment and the refund using the level's Refund Share (the first level whose tower trees contain this tier; otherwise the default 0.6).

docs.title: Soldier
docs.text:
Create > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Soldier (SoldierAsset). Produced by barracks, ability replacements and reinforcement spells.

Field Meaning Health Maximum hit points. Physical Armor / Magical Armor Reductions. Speed Movement speed. Intercept Radius Radius around the rally point in which it engages enemies. Engagement > Contact Bias Its share of the horizontal gap to the enemy it blocks (X, usually half its drawn body width plus a small gap) and a world-Y shift; added to the enemy's share. Melee Required to block. Ranged Attacks Optional. Tags Tag bits for effect and mechanic eligibility. Flying Only anti-air attacks reach it. Needed by flying follower companions; keep it off for barracks soldiers and ground escorts.

docs.title: Hero
docs.text:
Create > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Hero (HeroAsset). Add it to the level's Heroes.

Group Field Meaning Vitals Health, Physical Armor, Magical Armor, Speed Level-1 base values. Engage Radius Radius in which an idle hero engages enemies. Engagement > Contact Bias Same as on a Soldier: the hero's share of the horizontal gap to the enemy it blocks. Recovery Health recovery (usually idle only). Combat Melee, Ranged Attacks Attacks. Experience Per Damage Experience per point of health the hero's attacks remove. Tags Tag bits for effect and mechanic eligibility. Growth Skill Mode AutoUnlock (ranks unlock automatically by level) or SpendPoints (player spends points). Levels Growth rows; row 1 is level 1 at 0 XP. Each row: Experience (cumulative), Skill Points (total budget), Health Scale, Damage Scale, Armor Bonus, Magic Resist Bonus. Difficulty Experience Scale Experience multiplier. Skills Abilities with point costs and required levels (see Abilities). Respawn & Movement Respawn Delay Seconds dead before returning. Return Duration Seconds of invulnerable return. Use Respawn Position / Respawn Position Return at a fixed point instead of where it fell. Move Point Rule Which destinations a move order accepts (see Point rule). Companions Companions Owner-bound companions (CompanionData): Unit (Soldier asset), Slots, Mode (Ground Escort / Flying Follower), Refill Delay, Initial Delay, Formation Radius, follow distances and Acceleration (followers), Wait On Owner Death, Remove With Owner, Reconnect On Return, Rally Radius (towers without barracks), optional Point Rule (Mechanic Library).

Level, experience and skills are kept when the hero dies. Companion damage earns the hero experience; ground escorts take new places on every move order.

docs.title: Projectile
docs.text:
Create > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Projectile (ProjectileAsset).

Field Meaning Kind Instant (immediate hit, beam drawn), Straight (fixed aim point), Ballistic (fixed aim point, visual arc), Homing (follows target). Speed Units per second. Arc Height Visual arc height (ballistic). Lifetime Seconds before an unresolved projectile expires. Flight Time Fixed flight time; 0 = distance / speed. Hit Radius Fixed-aim single-target shots still hit if the target is this close to the aim point. View Key Blank = asset name. Must be unique (validator warns). Impact Area Optional region created once where the projectile arrives, also on empty ground (status effect and/or pulse). View: Prefab, Shape, Color, Size, Impact Fx Size, Beam Width, Shaded, Trail Time, Trail Width, Splash Ring Presentation. Hooks: Launch Vfx, Impact Vfx, Launch Cue, Impact Cue Optional pooled VFX and audio.

Straight and ballistic shots aim at a predicted position. Area-damage shots always explode at the aim point.

docs.title: Status Effect
docs.text:
Create > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Status Effect (StatusEffectAsset). Reference it from damage Effects, area effects, ability Self Effect or spells.

Group Field Meaning Identity Effect Id Used for duplicate checks; blank = asset name. Display Name UI name. Family Group name used by immunities and suppression (e.g. slow, poison). Rank Strength; a higher rank can replace a lower one. Duration Lifetime in seconds. Stacking Stack Equal Rank Allow separate instances at equal rank. Replace Lower Rank Replace lower-ranked instances of the same id. Refresh Equal Rank Re-applying at equal rank refreshes the lifetime (modifiers are not applied twice). Eligibility Required Tags / Rejected Tags Bit masks checked against the target's tags. Forbidden Ids / Forbidden Families Cannot attach while one of these is present. Remove Forbidden Remove existing forbidden effects instead. Payload Modifier Stat modifier while attached (slow, stun, armor shift, …). Periodic Damage over time: Kind, integer Minimum–Maximum per tick, Interval, optional First Damage on attach and Last Damage on natural expiry (negative = off). Healing Healing over time: Healing (amount + share of maximum health), Interval, Heal On Attach, Heal On Expire. Shield Damage-absorbing shield per attachment: Amount, Maximum Health Share, Channels, Refill On Refresh (Mechanic Library). View Tint, Tint Strength, Icon Body tint and icon above affected units (shields also use the tint for their bubble).

Units get their tags from the Tags field of Enemy, Soldier and Hero assets (32 bits in the Inspector). Effects with periodic damage, healing or a shield only attach to units with health.

docs.title: Spell
docs.text:
Create > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Spell (SpellAsset). Add it to the level's Spells (order = button order and number keys 1–9).

Group Field Meaning Identity Spell Id, Display Name, Description, Color Id (blank = asset name), button text, tooltip, button/preview colour. Rules Kind Reinforcement (summon friendly units), AreaStrike (scattered timed strikes), AreaEffect (region only). Cooldown Seconds; consumed only by an accepted cast. Unlock Wave First wave in which it can be cast (0 = before the first wave). Point Rule Accepted target points (below). Payload Support Summon for Reinforcement. Strikes Damage (needs a radius), Projectile, Count, Interval, Delay, Scatter Radius, Placement Attempts, Launch Offset, Targets Flying/Ground. Area Optional lingering region at the target point (any kind).

docs.title: Point rule (spells and hero movement)
docs.text:
Field Meaning Require Path Point must be near a lane; accepted points are projected onto it. Path Tolerance Maximum distance to the nearest lane (range ellipse). Use Bounds / Minimum / Maximum Restrict to a rectangle.

The same rule is used for the HUD's valid/invalid preview and by the simulation when the command arrives.

docs.title: Summon
docs.text: Field Meaning Unit Soldier asset (friendly) or Enemy asset (hostile). Count, Delay, Interval Units per activation and timing. Lifetime Seconds; 0 = permanent. Formation Radius Spread of friendly units. Cancel With Source Cancel pending units if the source dies. Population Limit Max alive + pending per source; 0 = unlimited.

docs.title: Area effect
docs.text: Field Meaning Enabled, Effect Region on/off and the status effect it attaches. Leave Effect empty for a pulse-only region. Radius, Duration, Interval Range ellipse, lifetime, seconds between scans. Until Source Lost Permanent region: ignores Duration, lasts while its source lives and is removed (with the effects it attached) when the source dies or is removed. Meant for auras; needs a living source, so spells and impacts emit nothing (the validator warns). Max Targets Recipients per scan; 0 = unlimited. Targets Enemies Enemies, otherwise friendly units. Follow Source, Remove On End Move with the source; strip effects when the region ends. Targets Flying, Targets Ground, Include Towers Recipient filters (Include Towers applies to attached effects). Pulse Direct damage and/or healing on every occupant at each scan (Mechanic Library).

docs.title: Wave Set
docs.text:
Create > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Wave Set (WaveSetAsset). Best edited in Tools > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Wave Timeline.

Wave

Field Meaning Auto Delay Seconds after the previous wave finished emitting before this wave starts by itself. Call Delay Seconds after the previous wave finished emitting before the player may call it early (clamped to Auto Delay). Early Gold Per Second Reward per rounded remaining second when called early (never for wave 1). Auto Start First Wave 1 only: start without waiting for the player. Groups Groups in this wave.

Group: Path Index (index into the level's paths), Start Delay (after the wave starts), Entries (run in order).

Spawn entry

Field Meaning Enemy Enemy asset. Entries without an enemy are skipped. Count Number of units. Interval Seconds between units (the first unit appears one interval after the entry starts). 0 = one per tick. Start Delay Extra delay relative to when this entry is reached. Lane Selection Fixed, RoundRobin (starting at Lane Index), Random. Lane Index Fixed lane or first round-robin lane. Following Gap Delay before the next entry in the group. Alternate Enemy / Same Kind Limit Alternate between two enemies every N units (0 = off), sharing Count.

docs.title: Level
docs.text:
Create > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Level (LevelAsset).

Group Field Meaning Geometry Paths Path data (centre line, Lane Count, Lane Spacing, Entry Node, Exit Node (−1 = last), per-node lane spacing, Air Route). Usually written from the scene (see Level Authoring). Build Slots Slot position and default rally point. Content Waves Wave Set asset. Available Towers Base towers buildable on empty slots. Extra Templates Additional entity assets to register (e.g. units spawned only by your scripts). Economy Starting Gold, Starting Lives Initial values. Ranges Override Range Y Scale / Range Y Scale Range ellipse ratio k for this level (otherwise the runner's value). Rules Leak Bounty Share Share of bounty still paid on a leak (default 0). Refund Share Sale refund after the first wave has started (default 0.6). Override Early Call Rate / Early Call Reward Rate Use one rate for all waves instead of each wave's own. Early Call Spell Cooldown Cut Early calls also shorten cooling spells. Early Call Cut Threshold Remaining time must exceed this for the spell cut. Victory Rating Two Star Life Ratio (default 0.5) and Three Star Life Ratio (default 1): share of starting lives (0..1) still left needed for two / three stars (inclusive). Rated by the simulation (State.VictoryStars). Player Spells Spells in button order. Heroes Heroes spawned at start. Hero Spawn Spawn point (additional heroes are offset sideways).

Inspector buttons: Validate Bake, Wave Timeline, Validate Project.

Upgrading from an earlier build: the old level field Star Rating (fractions or absolute life counts, rated by the view) is migrated into Rules > Victory Rating automatically when the asset loads; absolute counts become count / Starting Lives. Save the asset once to store the migrated values.

Nesting depth: the deepest authoring chain (ability → rank → action → attack → damage → impact payload → region → pulse → damage) is 9 levels, inside Unity's serialization limit of 10. If you add your own nested [Serializable] data below that, reference a ScriptableObject instead of nesting another class.

docs.title: Level Authoring (2D Tower Defense Maker/Level Authoring)
docs.text:
Field Meaning Level Level asset providing waves, economy, towers, spells, heroes. Paths Path components in index order; empty = all child Path Authoring in hierarchy order. Build Slots Slot components in index order; empty = all child Build Slot Authoring. Use Scene Geometry Off = use the level asset's own Paths/Build Slots.

Buttons: Write Scene Geometry To Level Asset (copies paths and slots into the asset), Validate Bake, Open Wave Timeline.

docs.title: Path Authoring (2D Tower Defense Maker/Path Authoring)
docs.text:
Field Meaning Points Centre line in local space, entry → exit. Lane Count / Lane Spacing Parallel sub-lanes generated from the centre line. Lane 0 is on the left of the travel direction. Entry Node / Exit Node Where enemies appear / leak (−1 = last point). Point Lane Spacing Optional per-point spacing override (0 = default). Air Route Presentation only: Level View draws the path as a dotted flight line instead of a road and leaves it out of the ground texture. Use it for routes that only flying enemies take (assign them in the wave groups); the simulation treats it like any path. Gizmo Color Scene gizmo colour.

Editing shortcuts: Editor Tools.

docs.title: Build Slot Authoring (2D Tower Defense Maker/Build Slot Authoring)
docs.text: Field Meaning Rally Offset Default barracks rally point, relative to the slot. The simulation projects it onto the nearest lane inside the tower's rally ellipse. Preview Tower Editor only: draws that tower's range and rally radius. Preview Range Editor only: range drawn when no preview tower is set. Preview Range Y Scale Y scale of the always-on gizmo.

docs.title: Simulation Runner (2D Tower Defense Maker/Simulation Runner)
docs.text:
Field Meaning Scene Level Level Authoring in the scene (preferred). Level Level asset used when no scene level is set. Tick Rate Ticks per second (default 30). Range Y Scale Default k (0.8) unless the level overrides it. Spawn Heroes Spawn the level's heroes at start. Seed / Randomize Seed Random seed; randomizing makes runs non-reproducible. Time Scale Game speed (0 = paused). Catch Up Ticks Per Speed Catch-up limit: at most this × speed ticks per rendered frame (default 8, via the core SimulationClock). Start On Play Start automatically; otherwise call StartSimulation(). Starting Gold Override Debug: replaces the level's starting gold when 0 or more. Capacities Entity Capacity (1024), Event Capacity (8192 – events of one whole frame, see Performance), Command Capacity (128), Effect Capacity (4096), Area Capacity (256), Schedule Capacity (1024), Chain Capacity (64). See Performance. Bodies Remains Capacity (256; 0 keeps none) and Remains Lifetime (10 s): bodies of the fallen kept for raise actions (SimConfig.WithRemains, script: SetRemains). A full store keeps its old bodies. Recording & Replay Record Commands, Recording Capacity, Recording File, Replay On Start, Replay File (Determinism and Replay).

Scripting: see Presentation (Simulation, Baked, Enqueue, Advance, SetPaused, SetSpeed, AddTemplateDecorator, recording, events SimulationStarted and EventRaised).

docs.title: Entity View Registry (2D Tower Defense Maker/Entity View Registry)

docs.title: Campaign, Progress and Saves
docs.text:
A campaign strings your levels together on a world map: levels open one after another (or by your own rules), each level keeps its best star rating, and the player's progress lives in save slots. Everything here is in TDMaker.Unity.Campaign (Runtime/Unity/Campaign). The Demo sample (Samples/Demo/DemoSample.unity) uses all of it.

Piece What it is CampaignAsset Create > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Campaign. Ordered levels, their points on a world map picture, unlock rules. CampaignProgress The rules over one save slot: level states, best stars, star total, pending victories. ProfileData What a save slot stores (JSON). ISaveStore Where slots live: JsonFileSaveStore (default), PlayerPrefsSaveStore (PlayerPrefs-backed storage), MemorySaveStore (in-memory storage). CampaignSaveSlots Slot picker logic: summaries, open (or create), save, delete. CampaignMapScreen, SaveSlotScreen Ready-made uGUI screens (TextMesh Pro, styled by your HudTheme). UpgradeShopAsset, UpgradeShopSession, UpgradeShopScreen The permanent star-upgrade shop: tracks of ranks, the purchase rules over a slot, the ready-made screen.

docs.title: The Campaign asset
docs.text:
Each entry in Levels has:

Field Meaning Key Stable id used by save files and text tables. Do not rename it after release – progress is stored by key. Level The LevelAsset to play. Title, Summary English texts of the map and the info panel. Translate them with the keys campaign.level.<key>.title / .summary. Map Position Point on the map picture, 0..1 from the bottom-left corner. Unlock Previous Level (the nearest earlier main-path level must be won; the first one is open from the start), Required Levels (every listed key must be won) or Always. Min Total Stars Optional star gate on top of the rule (earned stars, not stars left after shopping). Branch A side level. It never blocks the main path: Previous Level skips branches when looking for the previous level. A branch with Previous Level opens after the main level listed before it. Counts Toward Stars Whether its stars add to the campaign total (star gates and the upgrade shop budget). Path Points Optional bend points of the road drawn from its prerequisite.

Also: Map Image (any size; the points use 0..1 coordinates), Max Stars Per Level (normally 3) and the Map drawing group (road colours for open/locked levels, width, dash length, point size).

docs.title: Editing in the inspector
docs.text:
The Campaign inspector shows the map picture with every level point and the unlock roads (arrows from the prerequisite; dotted for branches; red when something is wrong; green points open at the start).

  • Click a point to select it; drag it to move it; click an empty spot to move the selected point there.
  • Drop Level assets from the Project window onto the map to add them at that spot (key and title come from the asset name).
  • Right-click a point: add a bend point to its road, clear its bend points, remove the level. Right-click empty map: add a bend point to the selected level's road, or add an empty level.
  • The list below sets the order; the selected level's fields follow it. Every edit is undoable.

The inspector, and Tools > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Validate Project, report: empty or duplicate keys, entries without a Level asset, the same Level asset twice, unknown required keys, unlock cycles, levels that can never open (also when a star gate asks for more stars than the levels before it can give), no level open at the start, and points outside the map.

The New Level wizard's result page has Add to Campaign: pick a campaign and the new level is appended (Previous Level rule) and the campaign is selected so you can place its point.

docs.title: Progress rules
docs.text:
A level is Locked until its save record exists, Open once it exists, and Completed after its first win. Records are created when the unlock rule holds (CampaignProgress.Refresh, also on every map visit, so a level added in an update opens for old saves too). An opened level never locks again – not when the rules change, nor when stars are spent.

Victories go through two steps, so nothing is counted twice:

  1. When a battle is won, call progress.RecordVictory(levelKey, stars) and save. The win is stored as a pending clear. Several wins before the map is shown keep the best rating; a defeat or an immediate restart does not discard it.
  2. When the map opens, call progress.ApplyPending() and save. It merges every pending clear once: best stars keep the maximum (a worse re-win changes nothing, a better one adds only the difference), the first win completes the level and raises FirstCleared(key, stars), and the next levels open. It returns a CampaignMapUpdate (changes, stars gained, newly opened keys) for the map to highlight. Calling it again does nothing.

EarnedStars is the sum of best stars of the levels that count; AvailableStars = EarnedStars − SpentStars. ProjectedStars (used by slot pickers) also counts pending wins, without counting a level twice.

var slots = new CampaignSaveSlots(campaign, SaveStoreFactory.CreateDefault(3));
var progress = slots.Open(0);                       // loads slot 1, or starts a new profile
// ... the player wins level i with `stars`:
progress.RecordVictory(campaign.levels[i].key, stars);
slots.SaveActive();
// ... back on the map:
var update = progress.ApplyPending();
if (update.HasChanges) slots.SaveActive();
mapScreen.Show(progress, update);

docs.title: Save slots
docs.text:
ProfileData holds the opened levels with best stars and win counts, pending clears, purchased permanent upgrade ranks per track key (GetUpgradeRank / SetUpgradeRank), stars spent, the earned total at the last save, and free custom key/value entries for your own data (tutorial flags, selected hero, ...). App settings – volumes and language – are not in a slot; TDGameSettings keeps them in PlayerPrefs (persistVolumes, persistLanguage).

Stores never throw; they return results and log warnings.

  • JsonFileSaveStore (default): persistentDataPath/TDMakerSaves/slot1.json, slot2.json, ... Writes go to slotN.json.tmp and then replace the slot file, so a crash mid-write keeps the previous save (a leftover complete .tmp is recovered on load).
  • PlayerPrefsSaveStore: one PlayerPrefs string per slot. SaveStoreFactory.CreateDefault chooses the platform default; you can also supply a store explicitly.
  • Unreadable data is never deleted silently. A file that is not valid JSON, not a profile, or written by a newer version is renamed to slotN.json.bak (.bak2, ... if one exists; key.bak in PlayerPrefs), a warning is logged, and the slot starts empty. SaveSlotScreen shows a note on such a slot.
  • Versions. Every file carries version. Reading an older one runs the built-in steps and then your own ProfileSerializer.Migrate += (data, fromVersion) => ... hooks, once per version step; the slot is written back in the current version. Fields a file lacks keep their defaults (JsonUtility), so new fields need no migration step – only changed meanings do.
  • Deleting a slot (CampaignSaveSlots.Delete) removes only that slot. SaveSlotScreen asks first (Delete / Cancel).

docs.title: The screens
docs.text:
Both screens are built from code under any canvas: CampaignMapScreen.Create(parent, theme) and SaveSlotScreen.Create(parent, theme) (CampaignUi.Canvas makes a canvas scaled like the HUD).

  • CampaignMapScreen.Show(progress, update): the map picture (fitted, letterboxed), dashed roads, level points (lock when locked, number when open, best stars under completed ones, pulsing "New!" on levels the update opened), the star total, a toast for first clears / stars gained / new levels, and the level info panel (title, summary, best stars, what still opens a locked level, Play). Events: PlayRequested(levelIndex), BackRequested. Keys: 1-9 select a level, Enter plays, Esc closes the panel and then goes back.
  • SaveSlotScreen.Show(slots): one row per slot (stars, levels won, last played), Continue / New Campaign and Delete with confirmation. Events: SlotChosen(slot), SlotDeleted(slot), BackRequested.

Their texts are HudTexts keys (campaign.map.*, campaign.level.*, campaign.slots.*, campaign.nav.worldMap), translated through your TextTables like the HUD; they relabel themselves when the language changes. For the in-battle buttons, the Demo calls hud.SetNavigation(false, true, null, HudTexts.NavWorldMap) so the pause menu and the result screen offer World Map.

docs.title: The Demo sample
docs.text:
Samples/Demo/Scripts/DemoFlow.cs is a complete flow in one scene: title → save slots → world map (Samples/Demo/Data/SampleCampaign.asset, painted map picture Samples/Demo/Art/world_map.png; the asset is generated by Create Sample Content) → battle (each level on its painted map, Level Grounds) → result → world map. It records each victory as a pending clear, saves immediately, and merges the result when the map opens. UseStore(...) lets you supply a storage implementation, and PreviewMap() shows a temporary in-memory profile.

The generated sample shop (Samples/Demo/Data/SampleUpgradeShop.asset) adds the Upgrades button to the map.

docs.title: The star-upgrade shop
docs.text:
Earned stars buy permanent upgrades between battles. An Upgrade Shop asset (Create > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Upgrade Shop, edited in Tools > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Upgrade Shop) holds ordered tracks (shop columns); each track is a chain of ranks bought in order, each rank has a star price and a list of effects. Assign the shop to the campaign's Upgrade Shop field: the world map then shows an Upgrades button with the unspent stars as a badge, and every battle started while a slot of that campaign is open applies the slot's purchased ranks.

Track field Meaning Key Stable id in save files (purchases are stored per key) and text key stem shop.track.<key>.name / .summary. Do not rename it after release. Display Name, Description English name and one-line summary (translated through the keys above). Icon, Color Column icon (optional) and accent colour. Ranks Price (stars), an optional English line (shop.track.<key>.rank<N>) and the effects. Higher ranks add their effects on top of the lower ranks.

docs.title: Effects
docs.text:
Each effect maps one to one to the core UpgradeEffectDef (see Runtime/Core/Upgrades.md):

  • Target: towers, soldiers, heroes or enemies (their template ids), spells (their spell ids), further ids, required tag bits and a role mask (tower, soldier, hero, spell, projectile, enemy). Filters combine with AND; the lists and the role mask are alternatives. Every matching value inside a selected template changes (all its attacks, ability ranks, damage payloads ...).
  • Stat: a field (range, damage minimum / maximum, attack interval, ability cooldown, build cost, ability prices, health, armor, magic / poison resistance, regeneration, rally range, respawn time, spell cooldown, units called and their duration, effect duration, blast radius, speed, strike count and spread) and an operation: Multiply Ceil (multiply, then round up at once - use it for damage and health), Multiply (keeps fractions - ranges, intervals), Add, Subtract, Set. Effects apply one after another in track, rank and list order; there is no "sum everything, multiply once".
  • Add Mechanic: adds an always-active timed action (the same action the units' and towers' behavior lists use: an extra attack, a self buff, a summon, an area, chain, trap, beam ...) to the selected units or towers. Give it a name for the tooltip (Mechanic Name, translated through shop.mechanic.<Mechanic Key>).
  • Swap Template: replaces a unit reference (the soldier a barracks or a reinforcement spell calls, a summon) inside the selected templates or spells. The replacement is registered for the battle automatically.

docs.title: Rules (fixed)
docs.text:
• Only the next rank of a track can be bought, and only with enough stars: Available = EarnedTotal - Spent, where Spent is the sum of the prices of every bought rank. Spending never lowers the earned total (star gates use earned stars).
  • One click on a buyable rank buys it at once - no confirmation - and the slot is saved immediately.
  • Undo Changes returns every track to the purchases the shop opened with (not just the last click) and saves.
  • Reset All clears every purchase without a confirmation, saves, and makes the empty state the new Undo baseline.
  • Done (or Esc) closes the shop; purchases are already saved. Reopening makes the current purchases the new baseline.
  • The map badge shows min(EarnedTotal, FullShopPrice) - Spent (never below zero): stars beyond the price of the whole shop are not announced. This is a display limit, not a cap on earning.

All of it comes from the core UpgradeShopRules; UpgradeShopSession applies them to a slot (Purchase, Revert, ResetAll, Available, GetState) and UpgradeShopScreen is the ready-made screen (columns of rank nodes, tooltip with price, state and an effect summary generated from the data - "Range +8%", "Cooldown -2s", "New: Sharpshot"). Its texts are HudTexts keys (campaign.shop.*, field labels campaign.shop.field.<Field>).

docs.title: Battles
docs.text:
When a run starts, SimulationRunner builds a core UpgradeSnapshot from the shop and the purchased ranks and passes the level with it (LevelDef.WithUpgrades); the core rewrites copies of the templates and spells before anything spawns, and includes the snapshot in the state hash and the command log. Where the shop and ranks come from:

Source When Runner Upgrade Shop field Used when set. Empty: the open slot's campaign shop (CampaignSession.Shop). runner.UpgradeRanks (Func<string,int>) Your own rank source, such as another save system. The open campaign slot CampaignSaveSlots.Open sets CampaignSession; used unless Use Campaign Upgrades is off. Forced Upgrade Rank Every track at this rank for the run (challenge modes); purchases are unchanged.

No shop, or nothing bought, means no snapshot: the run is exactly the run without upgrades (same hash, same log format). runner.Upgrades is the snapshot of the current run, runner.UpgradeRecord the shop name and ranks it used.

Replays. A command log stores only a fingerprint of the upgrades. When the runner saves a recording it writes the ranks next to it (<file>.upgrades.json), and a replay of that file reads them back (or set runner.ReplayUpgrades). Different ranks or a changed shop give a different fingerprint, and the replay is refused.

docs.title: The editor
docs.text:
Tools > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Upgrade Shop shows the tracks as columns and the ranks as cells (price and effect summary):

  • add, remove and move tracks; add, duplicate, remove and move ranks; every edit is undoable;
  • Price curve: fill a track's prices from its first and last price with a back-loaded curve (prices never decrease);
  • the selected rank's effects with a readable summary each (+ Stat, + Mechanic, + Swap);
  • Preview: pick a level, a tower, unit or spell and a rank (of the selected track, or of all tracks) and compare its stats before and after - computed by the core rewriter, so it is what the battle uses;
  • validation: no tracks, empty or duplicate keys, tracks without ranks, negative prices, effects without a filter, mechanics without a payload or on spells, swaps without units, Multiply Ceil on fractional fields, and effects that select nothing in the levels of the campaigns using the shop. Tools > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Validate Project runs the same checks.

The sample shop (six tracks of five ranks: archer, cannon, arcane and garrison families, Call to Arms and Starfall) is generated by Create Sample Content (SampleContentGenerator.GenerateUpgradeShopSample writes only the shop and the text tables). The three sample levels award at most 9 stars. Each track costs 0, 0, 1, 2, 3 stars (6 per track, 36 for the whole shop). The first two ranks are free purchases, still taken in order. With all 9 stars you can buy up to 19 of 30 ranks (about 63%): buy the free ranks on all six tracks, rank 3 on five tracks and rank 4 on two of those tracks. Alternatively, finish one track for 6 stars and spend the remaining 3 on other tracks. Reset All lets you try a different build.

The first version of 2D Tower Defense Maker includes:

  • A fixed-tick, engine-independent C# simulation with command recording, replay and state hashes.
  • Multi-lane paths, waves, branching towers, purchased abilities, blocking barracks, controllable heroes and player spells.
  • Damage, armor and resistance rules; status effects; chains, pulses, shields, traps, mine fields, beams, companions and on-site revival.
  • The New Level wizard, Map Editor, Unit Workshop, Wave Timeline, Upgrade Tree, Project Validator and headless Dry Run.
  • Campaign progression, best-star ratings, three save slots, a world map and permanent star-upgrade tracks.
  • Pooled Unity views, a TextMesh Pro/uGUI HUD, VFX and audio hooks, music transitions and camera framing.
  • Twin Roads, Crossroads and Winding Pass, plus a complete title-to-campaign sample flow and compiled extension examples.

docs.title: Sample presentation and onboarding
docs.text:
• Inter 4.1 Regular, Medium, SemiBold and Bold faces with static SDF atlases, explicit sample-theme assignments and bundled OFL notices. The optional dynamic Noto Sans KR fallback remains included.
  • Separate padded title and price regions on buttons and upgrade cards, larger sample small/body text and no sample text shadow.
  • English and Korean interface/content tables, language selection on the sample title screen and live relabeling of open panels and tooltips.
  • A consistent Start Wave label, more generous starting resources and gentler pacing across the three sample levels.
  • New Unit Workshop assets are selected and scrolled into view after clearing list filters. Map Editor results stay visible above its scrolling content.
  • Fresh levels include an optional starter reinforcement spell; sample audio remains an explicit opt-in.

See Quick Start for the first level, Presentation for typography and localization, and Support and licenses for notices.

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text: This page explains the rules the simulation follows. Field-level details are in Authoring Reference; code-level extension is in Extending the Framework.

docs.title: Simulation vs. view
docs.text:
ScriptableObjects (TDMaker.Unity.Authoring)
      │  LevelAsset.Bake()  →  TemplateRegistry + LevelDef  (immutable definitions)
      ▼
Simulation (TDMaker.Core)          fixed ticks · entities + components + systems
      │  reads: sim.State, sim.Entities, sim.Spells      writes: sim.Enqueue(command)
      │  outputs: sim.Events (SimEvent list)
      ▼
View (TDMaker.Unity.View / .Hud)  SimulationRunner, EntityViewRegistry, LevelView, GameHud, …
  • TDMaker.Core is plain C#. It does not reference UnityEngine, uses its own Vec2 and its own seeded random stream (SimRandom, xorshift32). Gameplay outcomes (damage, gold, lives, spawns, builds) are decided here only.
  • TDMaker.Unity bakes authoring assets into core definitions, advances the simulation every frame, and draws it. The view only reads state and sends commands; it never changes simulation state directly.

docs.title: Fixed tick
docs.text:
• The simulation advances in fixed steps: Simulation.Step(); SimConfig.TickRate defaults to 30 ticks per second (Simulation.DeltaTime = 1/30 s). All durations in assets are in game seconds.
  • SimulationRunner advances the core SimulationClock: it accumulates Time.deltaTime × TimeScale and runs as many steps as fit, up to Catch Up Ticks Per Speed × speed (default 8 × speed) per rendered frame; excess backlog is dropped so a slow frame cannot snowball. TimeScale 0 pauses; the HUD offers 1×, 2×, 3×.
  • Speeding up changes only how many ticks run per frame, not the tick length, so the outcome at 3× is the same as at 1× for the same inputs.
  • Views interpolate between Entity.PreviousPosition and Entity.Position using SimulationRunner.InterpolationAlpha.
  • SimulationClock is engine-independent, so custom hosts use the same catch-up rule (see Extending the Framework).

docs.title: System order within one tick
docs.text:
# SimStage Work 1 Commands Apply queued player commands 2 Waves Unit expiry, scheduled summons, barracks respawn, wave start and spawning 3 Effects Status effects, areas, recovery 4 Motion Path following and friendly movement 5 Blocking Pair soldiers/heroes with enemies 6 Melee Melee attack cycles 7 Ranged Target selection, ranged attacks, ability actions 8 Projectiles Projectile flight and impact 9 Damage Apply all queued damage in FIFO order 10 Death Resolve kills, pay bounties, death summons 11 Exits Resolve leaks, remove lives 12 HeroesAndSpells Hero progression, spell readiness 13 Flow Victory/defeat 14 Flush Commit spawns and removals

Entities created during a tick are committed at Flush and act from the next tick. Entities marked for removal are ignored by the rest of the tick.

docs.title: Campaign and release mechanics
docs.text:
Campaign progress and shop purchases live outside the battle. At battle start the core applies a fixed upgrade snapshot to copied definitions; the snapshot is included in replay validation and state hashes. See Campaigns, Progress and Saves.

Mine fields reserve lane sites and capacity before flight and arming. Companion slots follow their owner and refill after a child falls. Reviving enemies are not final kills until their return budget ends; pending returns and raised successors keep victory waiting. Bodies are neutral records consumed by raising actions, not extra enemy kills. See Mechanic Library.

docs.title: Templates, components and systems
docs.text:
• An EntityTemplate is an immutable definition with optional slots: Health, Armor, Motion, PathFollow, Bounty, Melee, Ranged, Tower, Barracks, Soldier, Hero, Projectile, Aura, StatusImmunity, Flying, Render, plus Rules (recovery, evasion, death summon, always-on behaviors, traits) and CustomData.
  • Templates may inherit from another template through BaseId; empty (null) slots inherit the parent's slot. Inheritance is resolved once when the TemplateRegistry is built.
  • A runtime Entity carries one runtime component per filled slot (entity.Health.Current, entity.PathFollow.RemainingDistance, entity.Tower.Priority, …). Entities come from a fixed, prewarmed pool (SimConfig.EntityCapacity, default 1024). Ids only increase and are never reused.
  • Systems implement ISimSystem.Tick(Simulation sim, float dt) and run in the fixed order above. You can insert your own; see Extending the Framework.
  • Authoring assets bake into templates: EnemyAsset, TowerAsset, SoldierAsset, HeroAsset each produce one template. Each tower tier is its own template.

docs.title: Determinism
docs.text:
• Same templates + same level + same seed + same commands at the same ticks ⇒ same result, at any game speed.
  • The core uses only its own random stream, iterates in entity-Id order, and breaks ties by the smaller Id.
  • ComputeStateHash() hashes the full authoritative state for comparison. Command recording and replay: Determinism and Replay.

docs.title: Commands and events
docs.text:
Input – the view queues immutable commands with Simulation.Enqueue(command) (or SimulationRunner.Enqueue). They are applied at the start of the next tick.

Command Effect BuildTower(slotIndex, templateId) Build an available base tower on an empty slot UpgradeTower(entityId, toTemplateId) Upgrade into one of the tower's listed next tiers SellTower(entityId) Sell (see Economy) BuyAbility(entityId, abilityIndex) Buy the next rank of a tower ability SetTargetPriority(entityId, priority) Change a tower's priority without resetting its cooldown SetRallyPoint(entityId, position) Move a barracks rally point (must be inside the rally ellipse; projected onto the nearest lane) CallNextWave() Start the next wave now MoveHero(entityId, position) Order a hero to a validated point CastSpell(spellIndex, position) Cast a ready spell at a validated point SpendHeroPoint(entityId, skillIndex) Buy a hero skill rank (SpendPoints mode)

A failed command produces a CommandRejected event with a CommandFailure reason (InsufficientGold, SlotOccupied, InvalidRallyPoint, WaveUnavailable, SpellUnavailable, …) and the command name in Key.

Output – each tick appends SimEvents (Kind, EntityId, OtherId, Value, IntValue, Position, Failure, Key) to Simulation.Events. Examples: Spawned, Removed, Damaged, Died, AttackStarted, ProjectileFired, ProjectileHit, GoldChanged, LivesChanged, WaveStarted, WaveCallable, TowerBuilt/Upgraded/Sold, EffectAttached/Removed, AbilityPurchased, HeroLevelChanged, SpellCast, Victory, Defeat, plus the mechanic events (ChainLinked, AreaPulsed, Healed, ShieldChanged, Displaced, … – see Mechanic Library). The reader calls ClearEvents() afterwards; SimulationRunner does this for you after raising EventRaised.

State – Simulation.State exposes Gold, Lives, WaveNumber, CanCallNextWave, NextWaveRemaining, NextWaveWaitDuration (the authored auto delay of the pending wave – the countdown's denominator; 0 while a wave is emitting or after the last one), VictoryStars, Phase and Tick.

Event values worth knowing – ProjectileHit.Value is the damage radius of instant (hitscan) and scheduled strikes (0 = single target; flight projectiles report 0, their radius is on the projectile). WaveStarted.Value is the early-call time credit in seconds and IntValue the one-based wave number; an early-call reward arrives as the GoldChanged event emitted just before it. Victory.IntValue is the star rating.

Previews (never duplicate a rule in the view) – read-only functions that use exactly the code the commands use. They do not change the world or emit events.

Function Use PreviewEarlyCallReward() → EarlyCallRewardPreview CanCall, WaveNumber, GoldReward (authored award), GoldGain (after the wallet limit), TimeCredit, SpellCooldownCut, SpellCooldownsAffected of calling the next wave now. PreviewEarlyCallSpellCooldownCut(spellIndex) Seconds that spell's remaining cooldown would lose if the next wave were called now. PreviewSellRefund(towerId) The refund SellTower would report (TowerSold.Value). TryResolveRallyPoint(towerId, desired, out resolved) Whether SetRallyPoint would accept the point, and the lane-projected point the soldiers would use. TryValidateSpellPoint / TryResolvePoint Spell targets and hero destinations (see Authoring Reference).

The bundled HUDs (GameHud, TDHud) use only these functions for their sell price, call-wave bonus, spell-cut tooltip and rally preview.

Commands after the end – once the game is won or lost, every queued command is rejected with GameEnded (a CommandRejected event). SimulationClock stops stepping a finished world, so SimulationRunner runs one terminal step on the next frame when commands were queued after the end; the step only processes commands (the tick counter does not advance).

docs.title: Coordinate system and the range ellipse
docs.text:
• Simulation space is the Unity XY plane in world units (scene components convert their transforms to world XY when baking). Y is "up the screen".
  • To suggest an oblique top-down view, every range is an ellipse: horizontal semi-axis r, vertical semi-axis k·r, where k is the range Y scale.
  • A point is in range when
dx² / r²  +  dy² / (k·r)²  ≤  1        (boundary included)
  • k comes from the level (LevelAsset.overrideRangeYScale / rangeYScale) or else from the runner (SimulationRunner "Range Y Scale", default 0.8). k < 1 flattens ranges vertically.
  • One formula for checks and display. The simulation uses Simulation.RangeDistanceSquared for tower ranges, melee contact, area damage, rally limits, spell scatter and aura radii. Everything drawn in the view, gizmos and editor previews uses RangeShape (Unity layer), which implements the same ellipse. What you see is exactly what is hit.
  • Authored "range" or "radius" values are the horizontal semi-axis r.

docs.title: Target priorities
docs.text:
Ranged attacks choose among eligible enemies inside the ellipse (and outside Minimum Range), respecting flying/ground filters. Ties always go to the lower entity Id.

Priority Picks First (default) Shortest remaining real path length to the exit (sum of actual segment lengths, including connected paths), not "closest to the exit point" Last Longest remaining path length Strongest Highest current health Weakest Lowest current health Closest Smallest elliptical distance to the attacker

A tower's default comes from TowerAsset.targetPriority; the player can change it at runtime (SetTargetPriority) and the choice survives upgrades. Enemies attacking friendly units use Closest. Soldiers and heroes choose melee opponents through their own blocking rules.

docs.title: Damage pipeline
docs.text:
1. Roll. Single-target hits roll ceil(lerp(min, max, random)), then multiply by the attacker's output scale (rounded up). Projectile hits deal at least 1.
  2. Area. If the damage has a Radius, every eligible unit inside the ellipse is hit. With q = distance / radius (elliptical) and edge = Edge Multiplier, the amount is ceil(base × (1 − (1 − edge)·q) × outputScale) where base depends on Falloff:
  3. DistanceEndpoints: floor(max − (max − min)·q)
  4. RolledLinear: one roll per impact
  5. ConstantMaximum: max
  6. Hooks. Registered IDamageHook.BeforeDamage may change or cancel the raw amount.
  7. Queue. Requests are applied in the Damage stage in request order (stage order × entity Id), so results do not depend on frame timing.
  8. Mitigation (per request):
  9. Immune channel (TargetTraitsDef.Immunities) or IgnoreDamage → 0.

  10. Reduction R, clamped to [0, 1]:

    Kind R Physical armor + armor shifts − physical pierce Magical magic resist + shifts − magical pierce Explosion, Electric ½ × (armor + armor shifts − physical pierce) Poison poison resist + shifts True 0

  11. Incoming multipliers (rounded half away from zero): magical damage first × MagicalIncomingMultiplier × status magical input scale, then all damage × IncomingMultiplier × status input scale.

  12. Enemies lose floor(value × (1 − R)). Friendly units (soldiers, heroes) lose round(value − floor(value × R)).
  13. Shields from status effects absorb the mitigated amount of matching channels, in attachment order (Mechanic Library).

  14. Flags: Execute removes all remaining health; NonLethal leaves SurvivalHealth; Despawn removes without reward; armor-reduction flags change defense instead of health.

  15. After. Damaged event, on-hit status effects, the damage's impact payload (secondary blast, residual region, knockback), hero experience, then IDamageHook.AfterDamage.

Armor and magic resist are fractions: 0.3 armor removes 30% of physical damage. 1.0 makes a unit immune to that kind.

docs.title: Resolution: kill vs. leak in the same tick
docs.text:
Every enemy is resolved exactly once as Killed, Leaked or Despawned. Because Damage → Death → Exits run in that order, an enemy that takes lethal damage in the same tick it reaches the exit counts as Killed: the bounty is paid and no life is lost.

  • Killed: +Bounty.Gold.
  • Leaked: −LifeCost lives and +round(Gold × LeakBountyShare) (level rule, default 0).
  • Defeat when lives reach 0. Victory when every wave has finished emitting, nothing is pending (spawns, scheduled summons) and no enemy remains. If both happen in the same tick, defeat wins. Once decided, the outcome never changes and further commands are rejected with GameEnded.
  • Star rating: on victory the core rates the result from the share of starting lives left (remaining / starting, capped at 1) against the level's Victory Rating bands (inclusive): three stars at or above the three-star share, two at or above the two-star share, otherwise one. The result is State.VictoryStars and the Victory event's IntValue; defeat leaves it at 0. Product default: two stars at half the lives, three at all of them.

docs.title: Economy
docs.text:
• Build: pay the tower tier's Cost.
  • Upgrade: pay the target tier's Cost (each tier's cost is incremental).
  • Ability rank: pay that rank's cost.
  • Total investment = build + upgrades + ability ranks bought on that tower.
  • Sell:
  • before the first wave has started (WaveNumber == 0): full refund of the investment;
  • afterwards: round(investment × RefundShare), RefundShare from the level rules (default 0.6). Rounding is half away from zero.
  • The per-tower Refund Ratio field is a hidden legacy value and does not affect the simulation; editor previews also use the level's Refund Share.
  • During play, Simulation.PreviewSellRefund(towerId) returns exactly the amount a sale would pay.
  • There is no interest.

docs.title: Waves and early calls
docs.text:
• A wave contains groups; each group belongs to one path and has a start delay; each group runs its spawn entries one after another. The first unit of an entry appears one Interval after the entry starts; an interval of 0 spawns one unit per tick.
  • After a wave finishes emitting, the next wave's timers start:
  • Call Delay: from then on the player may call it early (CanCallNextWave, WaveCallable event);
  • Auto Delay: it starts automatically.
  • The first wave waits for the player unless Auto Start First is set.
  • Early call reward: calling wave n > 1 early pays ceil(round(remaining seconds) × rate) gold, where remaining = Auto Delay − time already waited, rounded half away from zero, and rate is the wave's Early Gold Per Second (or the level's override). Calling the first wave gives no reward.
  • If the level rule Early Call Spell Cooldown Cut is on and the rounded remaining time exceeds Early Call Cut Threshold, cooling, unlocked spells are shortened by that many seconds.
  • Simulation.PreviewEarlyCallReward() and PreviewEarlyCallSpellCooldownCut(spellIndex) return both effects for the current tick; the countdown ring is NextWaveRemaining / NextWaveWaitDuration.

docs.title: Barracks, soldiers and heroes
docs.text:
• A barracks tower keeps Soldier Count soldiers alive and replaces a fallen one after Respawn Time. Soldiers stand in a formation around the rally point, which is always projected onto the nearest lane inside the tower's rally ellipse.
  • Soldiers engage enemies inside their Intercept Radius around the rally point. An engaged enemy stops walking while blocked and waits for its blocker to reach its place: beside the enemy on the side it walks toward, at the summed Engagement contact bias of the enemy and the blocker (2nd and 3rd blockers take rows above and below, by the enemy's Row Spacing). Blockers attack only once they stand in place; both face each other. Blocker Capacity on the enemy limits how many friendly units can hold it; flying or non-blockable enemies cannot be blocked.
  • Heroes are friendly units that block and fight like soldiers, gain experience from damage, level up through growth rows, unlock skills, die and return after Respawn Delay, and move by command.

docs.title: View layer
docs.text:
• SimulationRunner bakes the level (applying template decorators), creates the Simulation, spawns heroes, advances it with SimulationClock, and raises EventRaised for each event once per frame (then clears them).
  • EntityViewRegistry creates pooled EntityViews on Spawned, removes them on Removed, and reacts to damage, death, effects, upgrades, projectile and mechanic events (chain arcs, pulse rings, shield bubbles, …). A prefab is taken from the asset's View settings (or the registry's overrides by view key); otherwise a primitive sprite is generated.
  • LevelView draws a generated placeholder ground, path ribbons and slot pads.
  • GameHud is the production uGUI HUD (themeable with HudTheme); DamageNumbers, VfxPool, AudioCuePlayer, TDCameraController and TDGameSettings complete the presentation. See Presentation. TDHud is a minimal IMGUI reference HUD. Any of them can be replaced by your own UI that reads Simulation.State and sends commands.

docs.title: What is guaranteed
docs.text:
Given the same templates, level, SimConfig, seed, registered extensions, initial spawns and the same commands at the same ticks, the simulation produces the same state on the same runtime – regardless of frame rate or game speed (1×, 2×, 3×).

How the core achieves it:

  • Fixed ticks (SimConfig.TickRate, default 30); speed only changes how many ticks run per frame.
  • One seeded random stream, Simulation.Random (SimRandom, xorshift32). The seed is Simulation.Seed.
  • Stable ordering: entity Ids only increase, systems run in a fixed order, damage is applied in request order, ties break on the lower Id.
  • Commands are applied only at the start of a tick.
  • Spawns and removals are committed at the end of a tick.

What is not guaranteed: bit-identical floating-point results across different CPUs, runtimes or compiler settings. Use the state hash to check reproducibility on your target platform.

docs.title: Things that break determinism
docs.text:
• SimulationRunner with Randomize Seed enabled (by design).
  • Extension code that uses UnityEngine.Random, System.Random, wall clock time, frame time or Dictionary/HashSet iteration order in the tick.
  • Changing simulation state from outside Step() other than through Enqueue.
  • Registering extensions differently between the original run and the replay.

docs.title: State hash
docs.text:
ulong hash = sim.ComputeStateHash();   // call between ticks, never inside Step

The 64-bit FNV-1a hash covers the seed and random state, tick, phase, gold, lives, wave state, slot occupancy, every entity's authoritative state in Id order, pending spawns/removals, effects, scheduled summons, spells, queued commands and queued damage, upgrade snapshots, deployment reservations, companion slots, revival/body records, plus the state of extensions that implement IStateHashContributor. It excludes events and the render-frame accumulator.

Typical uses: compare a live run with its replay, compare 1× vs 3× runs, or detect divergence in automated checks.

docs.title: Recording commands
docs.text:
using System.IO;
using TDMaker.Core;

var log = new CommandLog(sim.Seed, capacity: 4096);
sim.StartRecording(log);        // before the first Step and before enqueueing anything

// … play: sim.Enqueue(...) / sim.Step() …

sim.StopRecording();            // between ticks; seals the log
using (var file = File.Create(path))
    log.WriteTo(file);          // pass an ICommandCodec as second argument if you use custom commands
  • Only commands enqueued from outside Step() are recorded, each with the tick at which it will execute. Commands created inside the tick by systems are regenerated by those systems during replay.
  • The log has a fixed capacity; when full, further commands are rejected with CapacityExceeded (it never grows during play).
  • Custom commands need an ICommandCodec with type ids ≥ 1024 (see Extending the Framework).

docs.title: Replaying
docs.text:
CommandLog log;
using (var file = File.OpenRead(path))
    log = CommandLog.ReadFrom(file);            // or ReadFrom(file, codec)

var replay = new Simulation(templates, level, config, log.Seed);
// register exactly the same extensions and spawn the same initial units (e.g. heroes) here
replay.StartReplay(log);

while (replay.State.Phase == GamePhase.Running)
{
    replay.Step();
    replay.ClearEvents();
}
  • During replay, live Enqueue calls from outside Step() throw.
  • With SimulationRunner, heroes are spawned by SpawnHeroes when Spawn Heroes is enabled; do the same before replaying (SimulationRunner.SpawnHeroes(sim, baked)).
  • Replay throws if the log skips an execution tick or if the input capacity differs from the recording.

A replay must use the same permanent upgrade snapshot as the recording. The runner writes purchased ranks beside a command log in <file>.upgrades.json; changing the shop or ranks changes the fingerprint and replay is refused. See Campaigns, Progress and Saves.

docs.title: Recording and replaying with SimulationRunner
docs.text:
The runner's Recording & Replay section does this for a Unity session:

Field Meaning Record Commands Record every run (started before the first step and before any input). Recording Capacity Commands one recording can hold. Recording File Where the log is written when the game ends, on restart and when the runner is disabled. Relative paths use Application.persistentDataPath. Empty = keep it in memory only (runner.CommandLog). Replay On Start / Replay File Start runs by replaying a saved log (its seed is used); live runner.Enqueue calls are ignored while IsReplaying.

From code: RecordCommands, RecordingFile, ReplayOnStart, ReplayFile, CommandLog, IsReplaying, SaveRecording(). Set runner.CommandCodec before the run if you use custom commands. Register the same extensions in the replaying scene (for example the same SimulationStarted handlers and template decorators).

docs.title: Speed-independence check
docs.text:
ulong RunAt(float speed) { /* create sim, start replay, advance with SimulationClock at 'speed' until done */ return sim.ComputeStateHash(); }
// RunAt(1) == RunAt(2) == RunAt(3)

Record one input sequence, load it into otherwise identical simulations and advance each with SimulationClock at a different speed. Compare the final state hashes on the same runtime to verify your content and extensions.
