All range ellipses drawn by the tools use the same shape as the simulation (RangeShape). The Y scale is taken from the open scene (level override, else the runner's value, else 0.8).

docs.title: Welcome
docs.text: Tools > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Welcome starts with TextMesh Pro setup, then Create your game: New Level, Unit Workshop and Map Editor. New Level defaults to fresh assets in your own folder and works without the Samples add-on. The Browse Samples button opens a separate browser for the optional complete sample game and feature examples. Missing samples are not a setup failure. Online Documentation and API Reference open the guide and C# reference. Show on startup is stored per project; the window never opens in batch mode.

docs.title: Optional sample browser
docs.text: Tools > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Samples > Browse Samples separates the complete Sample Game (title, slots, campaign, star shop and battles) from feature examples (Basic, Crossroads and Winding Pass). It also links back to New Level. Sample regeneration is available only when the add-on's editor scripts are installed and asks before resetting generated samples. These examples demonstrate choices you can replace in your own game; they are not mandatory Maker configuration.

docs.title: New Level wizard
docs.text:
Tools > 2D Tower Defense Maker > New Level makes a playable level in one step.

Use Online Quick Start in the wizard to open the first-level walkthrough in your browser.

Input Meaning Level Name Scene and asset names; fresh assets get template ids starting with the name (mylevel_walker, a number is added when the name is taken). Folder Default Assets/TDMakerContent/<Name>. Folders inside Assets/TDMaker (the package and its samples) are refused. Background Optional painted map (Sprite, or a Texture that is re-imported as a Sprite). The default path and slots are stretched to the map, it becomes the Level View ground art and the camera is clamped to it. Starter content Sample kit: the Basic sample's archer, barracks, cannon and arcane towers, its enemies, the Warden and two spells (the level refers to Samples/Basic). Fresh starter assets: new assets in <Folder>/Data from the Unit Workshop presets – Walker (standard enemy), Archer Tower with Archer Tower II, Barracks with Footman, and Captain (melee hero) when Include Hero is on. Include Starter Spell Adds a reinforcement spell to fresh starter content; enabled by default. Its soldier asset is created in the same Data folder. Waves 1–30 (default 3). Each wave is larger than the last; the waves together always send more enemies than the level has lives, so an undefended level is lost. Use Sample Sounds Fills the units' sound cues, the level music and the scene's interface sounds with the sample audio (Samples/Audio). Disabled by default; enable it when the sample audio is available and you want to use it. Off: every cue and track stays empty, so a level made from fresh starter assets does not depend on the Samples folder (assign your own clips later).

It creates <Folder>/<Name>.unity and <Folder>/Data/ (<Name>_Level, <Name>_Waves, <Name>_HudTheme, <Name>_SpriteUnlit and the fresh units). The scene is built by the same code as the sample scenes: camera, Level Authoring with one Path Authoring (two lanes, entrance at the left edge, exit at the right edge) and six Build Slot Authorings ordered from the entrance with rally points on the nearest road, and the 2D Tower Defense Maker object (Simulation Runner, Entity View Registry, Level View, VFX Pool, Audio Cue Player, Music Player, Game Settings, Game HUD with the F1 debug overlay, Damage Numbers). Afterwards the scene is open, the Level is selected, the Map Editor is open on the Paths tool and the wizard lists the next steps (with buttons for the Map Editor, Unit Workshop, Wave Timeline, Validate and Dry Run).

The result has no Validator errors or warnings and the Dry Run loses it without towers and wins it fortified and on its starting gold. Headless: NewLevelBuilder.Create(new NewLevelSettings { ... }) (it replaces the open scenes; NewLevelBuilder.Validate returns the first problem with the settings).

docs.title: Map Editor
docs.text: One window for turning a painted map into a level: background, curved paths, build slots, wave-call buttons, then Validate, Dry Run and Bake. It works in the Scene view (2D) on the scene's Level Authoring; every edit supports Undo and marks the scene dirty. Paths are drawn by hand – the editor does not try to detect roads in the image.

docs.title: Make a level from a painted map in 5 minutes
docs.text:
1. Scene. Run Tools > 2D Tower Defense Maker > New Level (pick your map as the Background) – it creates the scene with the 2D Tower Defense Maker rig (Simulation Runner, Level View, camera controller, HUD), a Level Authoring with a Level Asset, one path and six build slots, and opens this window. Or duplicate a sample scene (for example Samples/Basic/BasicSample.unity) and delete or edit its paths and build slots.
  2. Background. Open Tools > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Map Editor and drop your map Sprite (or Texture – it is re-imported as a Sprite) on the drop area. The map becomes the Level View's ground art, the game camera is clamped to the map rectangle, and the Scene view switches to 2D and frames it. Check the size line (Image 1920×1080 px · 100 px/unit · world 19.2×10.8 units).
  3. Paths. Press P (Paths tool) and N, then click along the road from the entrance to the exit: a handful of clicks at bends is enough – the path is a smooth curve through your points, sampled into simulation nodes every Node Spacing units. Drag points to fine-tune, Shift+click on the road to insert, Ctrl+click to delete. Set Lane Count / Lane Spacing until the drawn road band (lanes plus the Level View's road padding) matches the painted road; drag the white side handles of a selected point to widen or narrow the road there. Press N again for the next path; [ / ] switch paths.
  4. Build slots. Press B and click where towers may stand. Each new slot gets its rally point on the nearest point of the nearest road. Pick a Preview Tower to see its range ellipse at the cursor and around new slots. The ghost turns orange when a slot would overlap a road or another slot. Use Align X/Y, Spread X/Y, Snap, Duplicate and Delete on the selection.
  5. Wave-call buttons. Press C and drag the yellow ring of each entrance to where the HUD should show its call button (Ctrl+click resets it to just ahead of the entry).
  6. Test. Validate opens the Project Validator; Dry Run simulates the level with the scene geometry (summary in the window, full report in the Console); Bake to Level Asset writes the scene paths and slots into the Level Asset (Undo works on the asset too). Press Play.

docs.title: Background
docs.text:
Setting Effect Drop area / Map Sprite Sets the Level View's painted ground (Generated ground style). Textures are switched to Sprite import. Pixels Per Unit Re-imports the texture at a new scale; the world size follows (pixels / PPU). Pivot Position, Center On Origin Where the map sits in the world. Keep alignment (on by default) When the map is replaced by an image of another size, its pixels-per-unit changes or it is re-centred, every path point (curve controls and nodes), lane width, node spacing, build slot, rally point and wave-call offset is mapped from the old map rectangle to the new one, so everything stays on the painted roads. One Undo step reverts the geometry (the texture import setting itself is not undone). Fit camera bounds to the map Clamps the TDCameraController to the map rectangle (fixed bounds). Fit Camera Now does it once. Show map in Scene view, Opacity An edit-mode preview of the map (never saved into the scene, removed before Play). Lower the opacity to see your lanes over a busy painting. Lock map Unlock to drag the map with the Map tool (M) – for lining the painting up with existing geometry.

Recommended backgrounds. Paint at 16:9, 1920×1080 to 3840×2160 px, and choose texture compression appropriate for your target build. Keep one pixels-per-unit value per level and decide it before drawing paths – all level coordinates (paths, slots, rally points, ranges, speeds) are world units, so the PPU decides how big a tower range or an enemy step is on your painting. The window shows a non-blocking hint when the image is not 16:9, is larger than 4096 px, is down-scaled by its Max Size or is imported uncompressed (with a memory estimate).

docs.title: Paths
docs.text:
• Curve mode (default for new paths, the Smooth Curve toggle per path): you edit control points; the path is a centripetal Catmull-Rom curve that passes through every control point and is sampled into the simulation's node list at Node Spacing (each span gets round(length / spacing) equal steps). The entry is the first control point and the exit the last. Per-point lane widths are interpolated along the curve.
  • Polyline mode: the original point list, used as it is, with Entry Node / Exit Node. Existing paths stay polylines; switching a polyline to curve mode seeds the control points from its points (entry to exit), so the shape is kept. Switching back keeps the generated nodes.
  • The path list renames (type in the row), reorders (▲▼ – waves refer to paths by index) and deletes paths. Clicking another path's line in the Scene view selects it.
  • Every path shows its road band, all sub-lanes, direction arrows, ENTRY / EXIT markers and its wave-call button.

docs.title: Camera framing and larger maps
docs.text: The Camera Framing section edits the level's framing (Level Asset, or a scene override on Level Authoring): Fit Whole Map (default – the whole map on one screen, no player pan or zoom), Fit Height Scroll Horizontally, Fit Width Scroll Vertically or Fixed View Size, the Start Focus and an optional Intro Pan along the first path. With Show start screen on, the Scene view draws the first screen of the level as a green rectangle for the chosen reference aspect (16:9 by default; 16:10, 21:9, 4:3), using the same math as the game camera – so you see what fits on screen before pressing Play. For a scrolling level, paint the map wider (or taller) than 16:9 and keep the same pixels-per-unit; see Presentation for the camera inputs.

docs.title: Shortcuts (Scene view while a Map Editor tool is active)

Slots: place a slot (or select one) Shift+click Paths: insert on the road (away from it: add before the entry). Slots: add to / remove from the selection Ctrl+click (Cmd on macOS) Delete the point / slot under the cursor; Wave Call: reset the button Drag Move points, slots (the rally point follows the road when that option is on), rally squares, wave-call rings, lane width handles Delete, Ctrl+D, F Delete the selected point or slots, duplicate slots, frame the selected point

The same list is in the window's Shortcuts section. With the Map Editor's Paths/Wave Call tool active, the Path Authoring inspector only draws (the window owns the handles); with the Slots tool active, the Build Slot inspector's rally handle is hidden.

Scripting: the operations behind the window are public in MapEditing (create paths and slots, auto rally, align, remap, bake) and the curve math in PathGeometry (runtime assembly).

docs.title: Path and lane editor
docs.text:
Select an object with Path Authoring. The Scene view shows the centre line with direction arrows, all generated sub-lanes, ENTRY / EXIT markers and (optionally) build slots with their ranges.

Input (Scene view) Action Drag a point Move it Shift+click Add a point at the end; on a segment, insert a point there Ctrl+click (Cmd on macOS) Delete the hovered point (a path keeps at least two) Delete Delete the selected point Ctrl+D Duplicate the selected point F Frame the selected point Esc Deselect Drag the white side handles Override the lane width at that point (snaps back to default when equal)

Inspector:

  • Lanes: Lane Count, Lane Spacing, Entry Node, Exit At Last Node / Exit Node.
  • Scene Editing: Snap toggle and Step (stored in editor preferences).
  • Points list with per-point Lane Width, plus Reverse (swap direction) and Reset Widths.
  • Build Slots / Ranges toggles show every build slot, its rally point and tower ranges while you edit paths.

All edits support Undo.

docs.title: Build slot handles
docs.text:
Select an object with Build Slot Authoring:

  • Drag the Rally handle to set the default rally point.
  • Set Preview Tower to draw its attack range and rally radius; the inspector shows the resulting ellipse size and warns when the rally point lies outside the rally radius (the simulation would pull it back onto a lane inside the ellipse).
  • Reset Rally and Use Level Y Scale (copy the scene's Y scale to the gizmo).

docs.title: Wave Timeline
docs.text:
Open with Tools > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Wave Timeline, from the Level or Level Authoring inspector, or by double-clicking a wave issue in the Validator. Works on a Wave Set or on the Wave Set of a Level asset. Follow keeps it in sync with the Project selection; path names come from the first level that uses the wave set.

Layout

  • Left: list of waves with per-wave totals (units, total HP, gold, duration, auto delay) and +, duplicate, ▲ / ▼ (reorder), − buttons.
  • Centre: one row per group (sorted by path). Each spawn entry is a bar from its start to the end of its last interval, with a tick per spawned unit, coloured by enemy.
  • Right: inspector for the selected wave, group or entry (including Add Entry, Duplicate, Delete Group, ◀ Earlier / Later ▶, Select Enemy Asset, and warnings for missing enemies or invalid lanes).
  • Footer: totals for the whole wave set.

Mouse

Input Action Click a bar Select the entry Drag a bar Change the entry's start delay Alt+drag a bar Change the group's start delay Drag a bar's right edge Change the interval Shift+drag the right edge Change the count Click an empty row Select the group Double-click an empty row Add an entry at that time Mouse wheel Scroll rows Shift+wheel Scroll time Ctrl/Cmd+wheel Zoom time around the cursor

Keyboard

Key Action ← / → Nudge the selection by the snap step Page Up / Page Down Previous / next wave Delete Delete the selected entry (or group) Ctrl+D Duplicate the selected entry (or group) F Fit the wave to the view (also the Fit button) Esc Clear the selection

Toolbar: Snap with steps 0.1 s / 0.25 s / 0.5 s / 1 s, Fit, Ping. If a level has no wave set, the window offers Create Wave Set For …. All edits support Undo.

Timing shown on the timeline matches the simulation: the first unit of an entry appears one interval after the entry starts, and an interval of 0 means one unit per tick.

docs.title: Upgrade Tree
docs.text:
Open with Tools > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Upgrade Tree with a Tower asset selected (or from the Validator). It shows the whole tree containing that tower: build tier → levels → branches.

Each node shows: name, BUILD / LEVEL n / BRANCH, template id (and "barracks"), Cost, Invested (cumulative cost along the path from the root), Sell (after wave 1, and full refund before wave 1), and ≈DPS / Range. Cycles are highlighted. The side panel lists the selected tier's purchasable abilities with their rank costs.

Sell values use the Refund Share of the first Level asset whose tower trees contain the tier (the default 0.6 when no level contains it); the panel names the level used.

Action How Edit a tier Click the node; edit it in the side inspector Select the asset Double-click the node, or Select Asset Add next level / branch + on the node's right edge, or Add Next Level / Add Branch. A new tower asset is created next to its parent and linked. Unlink Unlink From Parent (the asset is kept) Navigate Go To Root, Follow, Refresh

docs.title: Unit Workshop
docs.text:
One window for enemies, heroes, soldiers, towers, projectiles, status effects and spells: find them, make them from presets, see them move, edit them on flat tabs, read what they are worth and try them against your towers.

Panel What it does List (left) Every 2D Tower Defense Maker unit asset, grouped by type. Search (name, display name, id, effect family), type filter, tag-bit filter, towers on/off. Click, Ctrl+click and Shift+click select; several assets of one type are edited together (numbers show "—" when they differ). * marks unsaved changes. Used by lists the levels (buildable, hero, spell), wave sets (wave numbers and counts), towers (upgrade, barracks soldier, projectile) and other assets that refer to the active asset. Toolbar New ▾ (presets, projectile, status effect, spell), Duplicate (gives the copy its own id), Rename, Delete (asks first and says how many references will be cleared), Save, Ping, Sandbox ▶. Preview (middle) Walk / Idle / Attack / Hurt / Death from the art set entry (same frame rates, hop and death hold as the game), speed and zoom, a 1-unit grid with the pivot cross and the ground line, the health bar at its real height and width. Moving right / left flips the direction; Art faces LEFT is the entry's Faces Left – the unit must look where it walks in both directions. Units without art show their generated shape; prefabs with an Animator list their clips. Projectiles fly from a tower to a target with their speed or flight time, arc, trail and impact flash; status effects show their tint and pip; spells their target ellipse. Below: quick numbers and checks. Basics Health, defenses, speed, gold, lives, flying, blocking (heroes: vitals and experience; towers: cost, targeting, upgrades, barracks). Projectiles, effects and spells show all their data as one flat form. Fields no tab claims appear under Other. Attack A melee card and one card per ranged attack (reorder, remove, add) with the damage block, target types and the projectile: pick one or press New to create it next to the unit, and edit its data in place. Mechanics Cards instead of nested foldouts. Traits (regeneration, melee evasion, reflection, aura, split on death with optional successor rules, return on the spot), on-melee-hit payloads (status effect, impact payload, life steal) and ordered timed actions (ranged attack, self buff, summon, area, chain, multi-target, trap, mine field, raise remains, beam, path transfer, custom action). + payload ▾ combines payloads in one action. Cards show computed hints: total health over all returns and time on the road, mines armed after the throw and how many lie on the road, cast plus rise time of a raise; problems (an empty placement band, a lifetime shorter than the arming, a raise without a unit) appear inside the card. Heroes and towers: a Companions card (unit, slots, escort or follower, refill) with mode/unit checks. Heroes: skills with ranks (points, level, passive stats, actions). Towers: purchasable abilities with ranks and + Mine-laying ability (a ready two-rank mine field). Effects Status immunities, tag bits, the effects each hit applies (editable in place), + New effect. Look View settings, the art set entry of this view key (created on request), frame arrays, scale, health bar placement, Art Faces LEFT, and the frame drop area (below). Hero Skill mode, respawn, move rule, growth graph (experience, health and DPS per level), growth table, Fill growth curve, skill rank summary. Audio Spawn / attack / hit / death cues with Play / Stop, VFX hooks, the launch / impact cues of the projectiles the unit fires, and the cast cue of spells that call this unit. Projectiles and spells show their own cues. Engagement Contact bias and row spacing, with a top view of the three blocker places around the enemy (rank 1 in front, ranks 2 and 3 below and above, pulled back by half the row spacing; ranks 4+ reuse them) for either walking direction. Soldiers and heroes are drawn against an enemy you pick. Stats See "Computed values" below. Sandbox See "Sandbox" below.

docs.title: Bulk frame registration
docs.text: Drop a sprite folder or several PNG files on the Look tab's drop area. Each file is sorted by its name: walk, run, move, fly → walk loop; idle, stand, breath → idle; attack, atk, shoot, cast, slash → attack; hurt, hit, take hit, damage → hurt; die, death, dead → death. The last number is the frame number (Orc_Walk_003, walk (2), 1_ATTACK_005, goblinRun07); a number right after the word is a variant (Attack2_05) and only the lowest variant is used. Files without an action word are reported as unsorted. The textures are set to Sprite, pivot bottom centre (the feet), no mip maps, compressed. Found sequences replace the entry's arrays; the idle sprite becomes the first idle (or walk) frame when the entry has none. The direction the art faces is never guessed: check Art faces LEFT in the preview.

docs.title: Presets
docs.text: Standard, Fast, Armored, Magic Resistant, Healer (permanent healing aura), Splitter (splits into a smaller enemy that is created with it), Flying, Boss, Melee Hero, Ranged Hero, Barracks Soldier, Necromancer (raises weak enemies from the bodies of the fallen; the raised enemy is created with it as _Risen), Revenant (returns once with half its health). A preset scales the project's median enemy and soldier (or built-in defaults) by ratios inside the balance bands: gold per health ×0.5–1.8 of the standard enemy, defenses in the low / medium / strong bands, hero experience steps ×3 then ×1.35. They are starting points; tune them against your towers with the Stats and Sandbox tabs.

docs.title: Computed values
docs.text:
The numbers follow the simulation's damage rules exactly for single-target hits without status effects: a hit rolls ceil(lerp(min, max)), an enemy keeps floor(hit × (1 − reduction)) (soldiers: hit − floor(hit × reduction)), and the reduction is the matching defense minus pierce (explosion and electric use half the armor). Expected values average every integer roll.

  • Enemy: effective health and hits of 10 for every damage kind; gold per 100 HP and per 100 effective HP; bounty density against the project's median enemy; for every tower tier in the project: hits of its strongest channel, seconds with every channel (and up to Blocker Capacity barracks soldiers), DPS and gold per 100 invested.
  • Hero: per level experience, step ratio, health, armor, DPS, effective health and skill points; a level-1 duel against every enemy.
  • Soldier: effective health, DPS against 0 / 50 / 90 % armor, a duel against every enemy.
  • Tower: investment, DPS by defense, time to kill every enemy.
  • Checks: defenses above 0.9, full reduction, zero speed, flying-but-blockable, bounty density outside ×0.5–1.8, experience steps outside ×1.1–1.6 (the first step up to ×3.5), units that cannot block, enemies that split into themselves.

docs.title: Sandbox
docs.text: A straight lane, the towers you list beside it (any tier, unlimited gold) and a wave of the unit (Count, Spawn interval). Heroes and soldiers (a barracks of three) face an opponent enemy instead. Run headless plays it with a fixed seed and reports the outcome, spawned / killed / leaked, lives lost, kill time from spawn (average, fastest, slowest), damage taken by enemies and by soldiers or heroes, gold, damage / hits / kills per source and the final state hash – the same inputs always give the same table. Buy tower abilities buys every rank of the listed towers' abilities before the wave (mine fields only act once bought). When they happen, mines thrown and traps triggered, companions arrived (and refills), falls and finished rises, and bodies reserved and raised are listed too; a fall of a returning unit is not counted as a kill. Play in temporary scene opens an unsaved scene with the lane, the towers, views (with the Workshop's art set) and the debug HUD and enters Play mode; stop Play mode and discard the scene when done.

docs.title: Shortcuts
docs.text: Ctrl+N new · Ctrl+D duplicate · F2 rename · Delete delete · Ctrl+S save · Ctrl+F search · ↑ / ↓ move in the list (Shift extends) · Ctrl+1…9 tabs · Space play / pause the preview · M flip the walking direction · Numpad 1–5 preview action.

docs.title: Make an enemy in 5 minutes
docs.text:
1. Create. Open Tools > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Unit Workshop, select an asset in the folder where the new one should go, then New ▾ > Enemy > Armored (or any preset). The asset gets an id from its name and numbers scaled from your project's enemies. Press F2 to rename it.
  2. Numbers. On Basics, adjust health, armor and speed. Watch the quick numbers under the preview and the Stats tab: the tower table tells you how long each of your tower tiers needs to kill it; orange rows are slow or cannot hit.
  3. Look. On Look, pick your art set (or New), press Create entry, then drop the folder with the unit's PNGs on the drop area. Play Walk / Attack / Death in the preview, press M to flip the direction and tick Art faces LEFT if the unit walks backwards. Set the scale and the health bar height.
  4. Special. On Mechanics, + Add mechanic ▾ > Trait > Aura (or a timed action) and fill in the card. On Audio, assign the hit and death cues and press Play.
  5. Try it. On Sandbox, Pick ▾ two or three tower tiers, set the count and press Run headless: killed / leaked and the kill times show whether the enemy fits the wave you have in mind; Play in temporary scene shows it in motion. Then add it to a wave in the Wave Timeline and press Ctrl+S.

docs.title: Inspectors with computed stats
docs.text:
Enemy, Tower and other template inspectors group fields in foldouts and show any extra fields under "Other". The identity header shows the resolved id and warns about duplicate ids.

Inspector Computed Enemy Effective HP (hits needed) against each damage kind; warnings for zero speed and full physical+magical reduction. Mechanics fields (Tags, Behavior, Aura) have their own group Tower Cumulative investment, sell value (after/before wave 1) and the refund share used (from the tower's level), range ellipse size at the scene's Y scale, garrison size and HP, DPS table for ranged attacks and for soldiers against several defense values; warnings for towers that do nothing and soldiers that cannot block Level / Level Authoring Validate Bake, Wave Timeline, Validate Project, Write Scene Geometry To Level Asset

DPS and effective-HP values are approximations (averages; no rounding, status effects or incoming multipliers), marked with "≈".

docs.title: Project Validator
docs.text:
Tools > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Validate Project scans every 2D Tower Defense Maker asset and the open scenes.

  • Filter by Errors / Warnings / Info; click to select the asset, double-click (or Enter) to open the right tool (Wave Timeline for waves, Upgrade Tree for upgrade issues).
  • F5 re-runs; arrow keys move the selection.
  • Checks include: missing references; duplicate template ids and projectile view keys; enemies with zero speed or full immunity; towers that do nothing, list themselves, have empty or duplicate upgrade slots, upgrade cycles, or are not buildable in any level; soldiers that cannot block; zero rally radius; attacks with zero range or no target types; waves without groups or enemies; entries without an enemy; path/lane indices that do not exist; invalid paths (fewer than two points, entry not before exit, coincident points, overlapping lanes); levels without waves, towers, paths or slots; failed bakes; rally points outside the rally radius; mechanics: enabled auras or pulses without a payload, auras that do not follow their unit, chains that cannot jump, multi-target health budgets with area damage.

Headless: TDMaker.Editor.ValidatorWindow.RunBatch logs every issue (for -executeMethod).

docs.title: Dry Run
docs.text:
Tools > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Dry Run Level runs the level headlessly and logs a report. It uses the selected Level asset, or the first Level Authoring in the open scene.

Three passes:

  • Undefended: no towers, every wave called as early as possible – shows the total threat (a sound level is lost here).
  • Fortified: unlimited gold; builds and upgrades towers on every slot (branch choice rotates by slot so each branch is also built near the entry; the report lists the final tiers reached), buys every ability, spawns heroes, moves them, spends skill points and casts ready spells.
  • Budget: the level's real starting gold, spent by a simple greedy player – start the first wave after three seconds, let later waves arrive on their timers, build the next empty slot (slots in list order, buildable towers cycled per slot) until half the slots hold a tower, then buy the cheapest of the next build (counted double), upgrades and ability ranks; hero and spells assist as in the fortified pass. The line adds lives left, gold left and spent, final tiers and the lives at the start of every wave. A budget-pass victory provides one reproducible winning strategy; use playtesting to assess how clear and forgiving that strategy is for your players. Order your build slots from most to least important – the budget pass builds them in that order.

The report lists the outcome and time, waves, enemies (killed, lives lost), towers built and upgraded, soldiers, shots, damage, abilities, spells, summons, effects, a mechanics line (chains and links, multi-target hits, region pulses, shields raised and damage absorbed, impact payloads, displacements and knockback payloads), an advanced line (traps placed/armed/triggered and how they ended, beams with pulses, budget and end reasons, path transfers, reflections, life steal), ballistic accuracy per source (fired, landed, damaging, target already gone before landing, landed beside a live target with the average miss distance), heroes, any remaining enemies, and rejected commands by type. Release-mechanic counters list thrown mines, companions, temporary falls/finished rises and reserved/raised bodies; a temporary fall is not a final kill. Rejected commands point to content problems (for example a barracks whose rally point cannot reach a lane).

The range Y scale is the level's override when set, otherwise the open scene's Simulation Runner value (0.8 when there is none). Headless: -executeMethod TDMaker.Editor.LevelDryRun.RunSample runs every sample level (Basic, Crossroads, Winding Pass); add -dryRunLevel <asset path> for one level asset. From code: LevelDryRun.Report(levelAsset, out PassResult[] results) returns the report and each pass' phase, stars, lives, time and waves.

docs.title: Permanent upgrade shop
docs.text: Tools > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Upgrade Shop edits ordered track/rank columns, a back-loaded star-price curve and stat/mechanic/template-swap effects, with validation and before/after stat previews. Link the shop on the Campaign asset; the world map then offers Upgrades. See Campaigns, Progress and Saves for purchases, Undo Changes, Reset All, save integration and battle snapshots.

docs.title: Sample generator
docs.text: Tools > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Samples > Regenerate Sample Content (re)creates every generated sample: Samples/Basic (data assets and BasicSample.unity), Samples/Crossroads and Samples/WindingPass (their own data plus references to the Basic towers, enemies, hero and spells) and Samples/Demo/DemoSample.unity (title, save slots, world map and result flow over the three levels, with the sample campaign Samples/Demo/Data/SampleCampaign.asset and its painted map picture Samples/Demo/Art/world_map.png; the scripts in Samples/Demo/Scripts are not generated). Re-running updates generated assets in place, including customized sample data. Keep your own game content outside the package folder. Headless: TDMaker.Editor.SampleContentGenerator.Generate().

docs.title: Sample screenshot
docs.text: Tools > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Capture Sample Screenshot plays the Basic sample with a scripted run and saves a PNG of the camera and HUD. Batch: -batchmode -executeMethod TDMaker.Editor.SampleScreenshot.Capture (without -quit and without -nographics). Details and options: Sample screenshots.

docs.title: Creating and checking content
docs.text:
• New Unit Workshop assets clear the active list filters and are selected and scrolled into view. When a user-created level is open, its Data folder is the first save-folder suggestion; packaged sample folders are not the default.
  • A Wave Timeline group's + opens an enemy picker before adding the entry. Count and Interval are copied from the previous entry, and the operation supports Undo. Double-clicking an empty group row uses the existing copy-entry workflow.
  • Map Editor keeps Validate/Dry Run controls and their latest summaries at the top of the window. Click the error/warning summary to open the Validator. The separate all-slot Auto Rally action asks for confirmation and supports a single Undo step.
  • Sample kit refers to existing sample units. Disabling Use Sample Sounds does not remove audio references already stored on those shared units. For content independent of Samples, choose Fresh starter assets and leave sample sounds off.

docs.title: Extending 2D Tower Defense Maker
docs.text:
The simulation core (TDMaker.Core) exposes extension points so you can add mechanics without editing package code. Before writing code, check the built-in mechanic library (chains, multi-target attacks, knockback, pulses, healing, shields, combat modifiers, mines, companions and on-site revival) – it covers many common needs with data only.

Extension point API Use it for Custom system ISimSystem, Simulation.RegisterSystem(system, SimStage, after) New per-tick rules (hazards, weather, objectives) Custom template data EntityTemplate.WithCustomData<T>(value), template.CustomData.Get<T>() Immutable per-template configuration Custom runtime component ICustomComponent, Simulation.RegisterComponent<T>(factory), entity.CustomData.Get<T>() Mutable per-entity state Target selector ITargetSelector, Simulation.RegisterTargetSelector Custom targeting for all ranged attacks Damage hook IDamageHook, Simulation.RegisterDamageHook Damage caps, reactions, custom absorbs Ability action IAbilityAction, new AbilityActionDef(action, cooldown), AbilityActionAsset Custom timed actions on abilities, skills and behaviors Command ICommand, ICommandHandler<T>, Simulation.RegisterCommandHandler<T> New player inputs Event Simulation.PublishEvent(SimEvent) with kinds ≥ SimEventKind.CustomStart Notify the view Spatial query Simulation.QueryEnemies(center, range, buffer) Find enemies in a range ellipse State hash IStateHashContributor Include your state in ComputeStateHash() Unity: template decorator SimulationRunner.AddTemplateDecorator, TemplateExtensionAsset Add custom data / rules to templates baked from assets

docs.title: The Extending sample
docs.text:
Every code block on this page is taken from Assets/TDMaker/Samples/Extending/ (assembly TDMaker.Samples.Extending), which is compiled with the package:

File Shows Scripts/HazardZoneSystem.cs Custom system + custom event Scripts/Barrier.cs Custom template data (BarrierDef) + runtime component (BarrierState) Scripts/LowestBarrierSelector.cs Target selector Scripts/BarrierDamageHook.cs Damage hook Scripts/RechargeBarrier.cs, Scripts/RechargeBarrierAction.cs Ability action, and its ScriptableObject wrapper for the Inspector Scripts/BarrierData.cs TemplateExtensionAsset adding custom data from the Inspector Scripts/Stance.cs Command, handler, custom event and replay codec Scripts/ExtendingSample.cs A MonoBehaviour that registers all of the above with a SimulationRunner Scripts/ExtendingSnippets.cs The short fragments of sections 5 and "Hosting the simulation" Scripts/MechanicDefinitionsExample.cs The code example of Mechanic Library

To try it, open the Basic sample scene, add 2D Tower Defense Maker > Samples > Extending Sample to the 2D Tower Defense Maker object and press Play: Brutes get a 40-point barrier that recharges, towers aim at the weakest barrier, and a hazard zone burns enemies near the map centre.

The sample uses the name barrier for its custom absorb so it does not clash with the built-in ShieldDef (shields on status effects, see Mechanic Library). Prefer the built-in shield for content; the barrier exists to demonstrate the extension points.

docs.title: Rules for extension code
docs.text:
• Register before the first Step(). All Register* calls throw once the simulation has stepped.
  • Do not allocate in Tick. Allocate buffers and objects up front. Use SpatialQueryBuffer instances you keep.
  • Keep shared definitions immutable. Template data, ability actions and command objects are shared; put mutable state in custom components or in your system object.
  • Stay deterministic. Use sim.Random, sim.Time / sim.State.Tick, and iterate in a stable order. Never use UnityEngine.Random, wall clock time or unordered dictionaries in the tick path.
  • Change state through the simulation. Health is changed through RequestDamage; positions through SetEntityPosition; effects through sim.Effects.TryAttach / EmitArea; gold, lives and builds through commands.
  • Hash your state by implementing IStateHashContributor on systems, components, commands, selectors and hooks (systems, command handlers, selectors and hooks that implement it are picked up automatically; others use RegisterStateHashContributor).

docs.title: Registering extensions in a Unity scene
docs.text:
SimulationRunner offers two hooks:

  • AddTemplateDecorator(decorator) – called for every baked template on each (re)start, before the simulation is created. Return a changed template (for example with WithCustomData or WithRules); the id must stay the same. Register it in Awake/OnEnable.
  • SimulationStarted – raised right after the simulation is created and before its first step, also after Restart. Register systems, components, hooks, selectors and command handlers here. The level's heroes are already queued; components registered now are also prepared for them.

From ExtendingSample.cs:

// OnEnable runs before the runner's Start(), so the decorator and the hook are in place for the first simulation.
private void OnEnable()
{
    if (runner == null) return;
    runner.AddTemplateDecorator(Decorate);
    runner.SimulationStarted += Configure;
    runner.EventRaised += OnSimEvent;
    runner.CommandCodec = new StanceCodec();
    if (runner.Simulation != null) Debug.LogWarning("[2D Tower Defense Maker] ExtendingSample was enabled after the simulation started; restart to apply it.", this);
}

private void OnDisable()
{
    if (runner == null) return;
    runner.RemoveTemplateDecorator(Decorate);
    runner.SimulationStarted -= Configure;
    runner.EventRaised -= OnSimEvent;
}

/// <summary>Template decorator: custom data plus an always-on custom ability action.</summary>
private EntityTemplate Decorate(EntityTemplate template, EntityAssetBase asset)
{
    if (!barrierTemplates.Contains(template.Id)) return template;
    var recharge = new AbilityActionDef(new RechargeBarrier(rechargeAmount), cooldown: 2f, initialDelay: 1f);
    return template.WithCustomData(new BarrierDef(barrierAmount)).WithRules(AddBehavior(template.Rules, recharge));
}

/// <summary>Runs for every new simulation (start and restart) before its first step.</summary>
private void Configure(SimulationRunner source)
{
    Simulation sim = source.Simulation;
    sim.RegisterComponent(() => new BarrierState());
    sim.RegisterComponent(() => new StanceState());
    sim.RegisterDamageHook(new BarrierDamageHook());
    sim.RegisterSystem(new HazardZoneSystem(new Vec2(hazardCenter.x, hazardCenter.y), hazardRadius), SimStage.Damage, after: false);
    if (useBarrierSelector) sim.RegisterTargetSelector(new LowestBarrierSelector());
    sim.RegisterCommandHandler(new SetStanceHandler());
}

WithRules replaces the whole rules bundle, so the sample's AddBehavior helper copies the template's existing recovery, evasion, death summon, traits and behavior actions before appending its own action.

Without code: list a TemplateExtensionAsset (your subclass) in any entity asset's Extensions field and it decorates that template during the level bake. Custom ability actions can be picked in an action's Custom Action field through an AbilityActionAsset subclass (see sections 2 and 5).

docs.title: 1. Custom system
docs.text:
A system receives the simulation and the fixed dt once per tick at its position in the stage order. Systems registered at the same anchor run in registration order; after: false inserts before the built-in stage.

using TDMaker.Core;
using TDMaker.Core.Defs;
using TDMaker.Core.Systems;

namespace TDMaker.Samples.Extending
{
    /// <summary>Deals true damage every second to enemies standing in a zone, and tells the view.</summary>
    public sealed class HazardZoneSystem : ISimSystem, IStateHashContributor
    {
        /// <summary>Custom event published on every pulse; Position is the zone centre and Value its radius.</summary>
        public const SimEventKind HazardPulse = SimEventKind.CustomStart + 1;
        private static readonly DamageDef Burn = new DamageDef(DamageKind.True, 3, 3);

        private readonly SpatialQueryBuffer hits = new SpatialQueryBuffer(1024); // allocated once
        private readonly Vec2 center;
        private readonly float radius;
        private double nextPulse;

        /// <summary>Creates a zone at <paramref name="center"/> with a range-ellipse <paramref name="radius"/>.</summary>
        public HazardZoneSystem(Vec2 center, float radius) { this.center = center; this.radius = radius; }

        /// <inheritdoc />
        public void Tick(Simulation sim, float dt)
        {
            if (sim.Time < nextPulse) return;
            nextPulse = sim.Time + 1.0;
            sim.QueryEnemies(center, radius, hits);            // same range ellipse as towers; ascending Id order
            for (int i = 0; i < hits.Count; i++)
                sim.RequestDamage(new DamageContext(0, hits[i].Id, Burn.Maximum, Burn));
            sim.PublishEvent(new SimEvent(HazardPulse, position: center, value: radius));
        }

        /// <inheritdoc />
        public void AppendStateHash(ref StateHasher hash) => hash.Add(nextPulse);
    }
}

Registered before the built-in Damage stage, so the damage is applied in the same tick:

sim.RegisterSystem(new HazardZoneSystem(new Vec2(hazardCenter.x, hazardCenter.y), hazardRadius), SimStage.Damage, after: false);

RequestDamage goes through the same pipeline as built-in attacks: damage hooks, the FIFO queue, armor and resist, shields, on-hit effects and experience.

docs.title: 2. Custom data: template definition + runtime component
docs.text:
Immutable configuration lives on the template; mutable state lives in a prewarmed component that every entity bundle owns.

using TDMaker.Core;
using TDMaker.Core.Defs;

namespace TDMaker.Samples.Extending
{
    /// <summary>Immutable barrier configuration, shared by every entity of a template.</summary>
    public sealed class BarrierDef
    {
        /// <summary>Barrier capacity.</summary>
        public readonly float Maximum;
        /// <summary>Creates the configuration.</summary>
        public BarrierDef(float maximum) { Maximum = maximum; }
    }

    /// <summary>Mutable per-entity barrier state, prewarmed for every entity bundle.</summary>
    public sealed class BarrierState : ICustomComponent, IStateHashContributor
    {
        /// <summary>Remaining and maximum capacity.</summary>
        public float Charge, Maximum;

        /// <summary>Runs on spawn and on template change (upgrade). template == null marks an unused pool bundle. Must not allocate.</summary>
        public void Reset(EntityTemplate template)
        {
            Maximum = template?.CustomData.Get<BarrierDef>()?.Maximum ?? 0;
            Charge = Maximum;
        }

        /// <inheritdoc />
        public void AppendStateHash(ref StateHasher hash) { hash.Add(Charge); hash.Add(Maximum); }
    }
}

Attaching the data:

// In code (a SimulationRunner template decorator, or templates you build yourself):
return template.WithCustomData(new BarrierDef(barrierAmount)).WithRules(AddBehavior(template.Rules, recharge));

// Runtime side (before the first Step):
sim.RegisterComponent(() => new BarrierState());   // the factory must return a new instance each call

// Anywhere in the tick:
var barrier = actor.CustomData.Get<BarrierState>(); // null if the type was not registered

From the Inspector, a TemplateExtensionAsset does the same for one asset (create it with Create > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Samples > Barrier Data and add it to a unit's Extensions list):

using TDMaker.Core.Defs;
using TDMaker.Unity.Authoring;
using UnityEngine;

namespace TDMaker.Samples.Extending
{
    /// <summary>Lets designers add <see cref="BarrierDef"/> to a unit through its Extensions list.</summary>
    [CreateAssetMenu(menuName = "2D Tower Defense Maker/Samples/Barrier Data", fileName = "BarrierData")]
    public sealed class BarrierData : TemplateExtensionAsset
    {
        /// <summary>Barrier capacity.</summary>
        [Min(0)] public float maximum = 40;

        /// <inheritdoc />
        public override EntityTemplate Apply(EntityTemplate template) => template.WithCustomData(new BarrierDef(maximum));
    }
}

CustomData slots are inherited through BaseId; a child template's value of the same type replaces the parent's.

docs.title: 3. Target selector
docs.text:
One selector replaces the default scoring for every ranged attack in the world (towers, soldiers, heroes, enemies). Candidates are an ephemeral, Id-ordered buffer from the spatial index; always filter with IsEligibleTarget. Return null to skip the attack.

using TDMaker.Core;

namespace TDMaker.Samples.Extending
{
    /// <summary>Towers prefer the target with the weakest barrier; everything else uses "lowest health".</summary>
    public sealed class LowestBarrierSelector : ITargetSelector
    {
        /// <inheritdoc />
        public Entity Select(Simulation sim, in TargetQuery query, SpatialQueryBuffer candidates)
        {
            Entity best = null;
            float bestScore = float.MaxValue;
            for (int i = 0; i < candidates.Count; i++)
            {
                Entity target = candidates[i];
                if (!sim.IsEligibleTarget(target, query)) continue;    // lifecycle, faction, flying/ground, range ellipse
                float score = query.Actor.Tower != null
                    ? target.CustomData.Get<BarrierState>()?.Charge ?? 0
                    : target.Health.Current;
                if (best == null || score < bestScore || (score == bestScore && target.Id < best.Id))
                { best = target; bestScore = score; }
            }
            return best;
        }
    }
}

query.Priority carries the tower's current priority if you want to honour it. To fall back to the built-in choice for some actors, return sim.FindDefaultTarget(query); – it is safe to call from a selector. Do not call FindTarget from inside a selector (re-entry throws).

docs.title: 4. Damage hook
docs.text:
BeforeDamage runs when a request is queued and may change Amount (finite, ≥ 0) or set Cancelled. AfterDamage observes every accepted request after mitigation, including those that applied zero. Hooks run in registration order and must not request damage from BeforeDamage.

using TDMaker.Core;

namespace TDMaker.Samples.Extending
{
    /// <summary>Absorbs raw damage with the target's barrier before armor and resistance.</summary>
    public sealed class BarrierDamageHook : IDamageHook
    {
        /// <inheritdoc />
        public void BeforeDamage(Simulation sim, ref DamageContext hit)
        {
            var barrier = sim.Entities.Get(hit.TargetId)?.CustomData.Get<BarrierState>();
            if (barrier == null || barrier.Charge <= 0) return;
            float absorbed = System.Math.Min(hit.Amount, barrier.Charge);
            barrier.Charge -= absorbed;
            hit.Amount -= absorbed;                     // raw amount, before armor and resist
        }

        /// <inheritdoc />
        public void AfterDamage(Simulation sim, in DamageResult result)
        {
            // result.AppliedAmount is the health actually lost.
        }
    }
}

sim.RegisterDamageHook(new BarrierDamageHook());

Built-in shields (status effect Shield) absorb after armor and resistance; a BeforeDamage hook sees the raw amount before both.

docs.title: 5. Ability action
docs.text:
An IAbilityAction runs on an action channel's cooldown. Returning true consumes the cooldown; false retries next tick. Keep the action object immutable and store state in a custom component.

using TDMaker.Core;

namespace TDMaker.Samples.Extending
{
    /// <summary>Custom ability action: refills the actor's barrier.</summary>
    public sealed class RechargeBarrier : IAbilityAction
    {
        private readonly float amount;

        /// <summary>Creates the action.</summary>
        public RechargeBarrier(float amount) { this.amount = amount; }

        /// <inheritdoc />
        public bool TryExecute(Simulation sim, Entity actor, int slotIndex, int actionIndex)
        {
            var barrier = actor.CustomData.Get<BarrierState>();
            if (barrier == null || barrier.Charge >= barrier.Maximum) return false;
            barrier.Charge = System.Math.Min(barrier.Maximum, barrier.Charge + amount);
            return true;
        }
    }
}

Using it from code:

var recharge = new AbilityActionDef(new RechargeBarrier(rechargeAmount), cooldown: 2f, initialDelay: 1f);

// a) Always-on behavior of a unit template (ExtendingSample appends it to the existing rules):
EntityTemplate unit = template.WithRules(new EntityRulesDef(behavior: new AbilityRankDef(new[] { recharge })));

// b) Rank 1 of a purchasable tower ability (costs must match the rank count):
var ability = new AbilityDef(new AbilityExecutionDef(new[] { new AbilityRankDef(new[] { recharge }) }), "barrier_battery", 150);

// c) Add a custom payload to an existing built-in action:
AbilityActionDef combined = existingAction.WithCustomAction(new RechargeBarrier(5));

Using it from the Inspector: wrap it in an AbilityActionAsset and pick the asset in any action's Custom Action field (tower abilities, hero skills, enemy behaviors). It runs together with the action's other payloads.

using TDMaker.Core;
using TDMaker.Unity.Authoring;
using UnityEngine;

namespace TDMaker.Samples.Extending
{
    /// <summary>Lets designers pick <see cref="RechargeBarrier"/> in an ability action's Custom Action field.</summary>
    [CreateAssetMenu(menuName = "2D Tower Defense Maker/Samples/Recharge Barrier Action", fileName = "RechargeBarrierAction")]
    public sealed class RechargeBarrierAction : AbilityActionAsset
    {
        /// <summary>Barrier restored per activation.</summary>
        [Min(0)] public float amount = 5;

        /// <inheritdoc />
        public override IAbilityAction CreateAction() => new RechargeBarrier(amount);
    }
}

The built-in ChainAttackDef and MultiTargetAttackDef are ability actions too; when an action uses several of chain, multi-target and a custom action, they are combined with CompositeAbilityAction.

docs.title: 6. Command and event
docs.text:
using System.IO;
using TDMaker.Core;
using TDMaker.Core.Commands;

namespace TDMaker.Samples.Extending
{
    /// <summary>A tower stance chosen by the player.</summary>
    public enum Stance
    {
        /// <summary>Default behavior.</summary>
        Normal,
        /// <summary>Alternative behavior.</summary>
        Defensive
    }

    /// <summary>Custom player command: changes a tower's stance.</summary>
    public sealed class SetStance : ICommand, IStateHashContributor   // immutable
    {
        /// <summary>Tower entity.</summary>
        public int EntityId { get; }
        /// <summary>Requested stance.</summary>
        public Stance Stance { get; }
        /// <summary>Creates the command.</summary>
        public SetStance(int entityId, Stance stance) { EntityId = entityId; Stance = stance; }
        /// <inheritdoc />
        public void AppendStateHash(ref StateHasher hash) { hash.Add(EntityId); hash.Add((int)Stance); }
    }

    /// <summary>Per-entity stance state.</summary>
    public sealed class StanceState : ICustomComponent, IStateHashContributor
    {
        /// <summary>Current stance.</summary>
        public Stance Value;
        /// <inheritdoc />
        public void Reset(TDMaker.Core.Defs.EntityTemplate template) { Value = Stance.Normal; }
        /// <inheritdoc />
        public void AppendStateHash(ref StateHasher hash) => hash.Add((int)Value);
    }

    /// <summary>Applies <see cref="SetStance"/> and publishes a custom event.</summary>
    public sealed class SetStanceHandler : ICommandHandler<SetStance>
    {
        /// <summary>Custom event; EntityId is the tower and IntValue the new stance.</summary>
        public const SimEventKind StanceChanged = SimEventKind.CustomStart + 2;

        /// <inheritdoc />
        public CommandFailure Handle(Simulation sim, SetStance command)
        {
            Entity tower = sim.Entities.Get(command.EntityId);
            var state = tower?.CustomData.Get<StanceState>();
            if (state == null || tower.Tower == null) return CommandFailure.InvalidEntity;  // emits CommandRejected
            state.Value = command.Stance;
            sim.PublishEvent(new SimEvent(StanceChanged, tower.Id, intValue: (int)command.Stance, position: tower.Position));
            return CommandFailure.None;
        }
    }

    /// <summary>Optional: persists <see cref="SetStance"/> in replays (type ids ≥ 1024 are yours).</summary>
    public sealed class StanceCodec : ICommandCodec
    {
        /// <inheritdoc />
        public int GetTypeId(ICommand command) => command is SetStance ? 1024 : 0;
        /// <inheritdoc />
        public void WritePayload(BinaryWriter writer, ICommand command)
        { var c = (SetStance)command; writer.Write(c.EntityId); writer.Write((int)c.Stance); }
        /// <inheritdoc />
        public ICommand ReadPayload(int typeId, BinaryReader reader)
            => typeId == 1024 ? new SetStance(reader.ReadInt32(), (Stance)reader.ReadInt32()) : throw new InvalidDataException();
    }
}

Setup (before the first Step) and use:

sim.RegisterComponent(() => new StanceState());
sim.RegisterCommandHandler(new SetStanceHandler());
runner.CommandCodec = new StanceCodec();          // lets the runner save and load replays containing SetStance

// From UI:
public void SetTowerStance(int towerId, Stance stance) => runner.Enqueue(new SetStance(towerId, stance));

Built-in command types cannot be replaced. A command type without a handler is rejected with InvalidCommand.

docs.title: How the view consumes events
docs.text:
SimulationRunner.EventRaised delivers every event in emission order once per frame, after the frame's ticks (the runner clears them afterwards). Subscribe from any MonoBehaviour – ExtendingSample does:

private void OnSimEvent(in SimEvent e)
{
    switch (e.Kind)
    {
        case HazardZoneSystem.HazardPulse:
            if (hazardVfx != null && vfxPool != null) vfxPool.Spawn(hazardVfx, new Vector3(e.Position.X, e.Position.Y, 0));
            break;
        case SetStanceHandler.StanceChanged:
            Debug.Log($"[2D Tower Defense Maker] Tower #{e.EntityId} stance: {(Stance)e.IntValue}", this);
            break;
    }
}

Guidelines:

  • Treat events as notifications; read current values from runner.Simulation.State and runner.Simulation.Entities.
  • Several ticks can run in one frame; avoid expensive work per event (pool your effects with VfxPool).
  • Look up authoring assets for an entity with runner.Baked.TryGetAsset(entity.Template.Id, out var asset), GetTower, GetHero, GetSpell(index), TryGetProjectile(viewKey, …), TryGetEffect(effectId, …) or TryGetMechanicVisual(key, …) (chain, multi-target and pulse looks).
  • For a custom HUD, read Simulation.State (gold, lives, wave, CanCallNextWave, NextWaveRemaining, NextWaveWaitDuration, VictoryStars) and Simulation.Spells, validate targets with TryValidateSpellPoint / TryResolvePoint / TryResolveRallyPoint, and show prices with PreviewSellRefund, PreviewEarlyCallReward and PreviewEarlyCallSpellCooldownCut – the same code the commands use (Concepts).

docs.title: Hosting the simulation without SimulationRunner
docs.text:
BakedLevel baked = levelAsset.Bake();
var sim = new Simulation(baked.Templates, baked.Level, new SimConfig(tickRate: 30, rangeYScale: 0.8f), seed: 1234);
// register extensions here
var clock = new SimulationClock(sim);           // catch-up limit = 8 × speed ticks per frame
// per frame:
clock.Advance(Time.deltaTime, speed: 1f);
for (int i = 0; i < sim.Events.Count; i++) { SimEvent e = sim.Events[i]; /* … */ }
sim.ClearEvents();
// interpolate views with clock.Interpolation

This is what SimulationRunner does internally. To decorate templates in your own host, build a new TemplateRegistry from baked.Templates.Templates (changed as you like) and use baked.WithTemplates(registry) so the view lookups stay valid. SimulationClock.Advance may run several ticks per call; if you need events per tick, call sim.Step() yourself and drain events after each step.

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text:
The range circle I see does not look like a circle. By design. Ranges are ellipses with horizontal radius r and vertical radius k·r (range Y scale k, default 0.8) to match an oblique top-down view. The drawn ellipse is exactly the area the simulation tests. Set the level's Range Y Scale to 1 for true circles.

Which enemy does a tower shoot first? With the default priority First, the enemy with the shortest remaining path length to the exit – not the one nearest to the exit point. Players can switch a tower to Last, Strongest, Weakest or Closest at runtime.

An enemy died on the exit line. Did I lose a life? No. Damage and death are resolved before exits in each tick, so a unit that takes lethal damage in the tick it reaches the exit counts as killed: bounty paid, no life lost.

Why did selling refund everything? Before the first wave starts, selling refunds the full investment. After that the refund is investment × Refund Share (level rules, default 0.6). The tower asset's old Refund Ratio field is hidden and unused; the Upgrade Tree and Tower inspector also show the level's share.

How much does an upgrade cost? The Cost of the tier you upgrade into. Each tier's cost is incremental.

The first wave does not start. Wave 1 waits for the player (the HUD's Start Wave button or CallNextWave) unless Auto Start First is enabled on it.

I called a wave early but got no gold. Calling wave 1 never pays. For later waves, the reward is based on the rounded remaining seconds of Auto Delay; if the wave was about to start anyway, the reward can be 0. Check Early Gold Per Second or the level's early-call override.

My barracks soldiers do not block anything. Check that the Soldier has Melee enabled, the enemy is Blockable and not Flying, its Blocker Capacity is above 0, and the rally point can reach a lane inside the tower's Rally Radius. The Validator and the Build Slot inspector warn about most of these.

Building a barracks is rejected with InvalidRallyPoint. No lane passes through the tower's rally ellipse at that slot. Move the slot closer to the path or increase Rally Radius.

Enemy regeneration never triggers. Turn off Idle Only in the enemy's Regeneration; walking enemies are never idle.

My new enemy is ignored by waves. Entries without an Enemy are skipped when baking. The Wave Timeline and Validator flag them.

"Template id '…' is used by both …" Two assets in the same level resolve to the same id (blank ids use the asset name). Give one a unique Template Id.

Does 3× speed change the outcome? No. Speed only changes how many fixed ticks run per frame. See Determinism and Replay.

Can I restyle the HUD or use my own UI? Restyle the Game HUD with a HUD Theme asset (TextMesh Pro font, sprites, colours, sizes) and change its words with string tables. For a completely different UI, read Simulation.State and Simulation.Entities, send commands with SimulationRunner.Enqueue, listen to SimulationRunner.EventRaised, and remove the Game HUD (and TD Hud) components. See Presentation and Extending the Framework.

How do I make a healer, a shielded unit or a knockback tower? Use the built-in mechanic blocks: pulse-only healing auras, status effects with Shield, and damage Impact payloads with displacement. See Mechanic Library; the Basic sample's Mender, Storm Spire and Cannon III use them.

The HUD has no text, or text shows as boxes. No text at all: the TextMesh Pro Essential Resources are not imported – use Tools > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Import TMP Essential Resources. Boxes: the font has no glyphs for that language (for example Korean with the default LiberationSans); add a dynamic CJK font asset as a fallback. See Presentation.

How do I translate the HUD or add a language? Duplicate Samples/Text/Text_English, set its language code, translate, add it to TDGameSettings > Text Tables and select the language (TDGameSettings.Current.SetLanguage("de")). Missing texts fall back to English. See Presentation.

Can I use my own sprites and animations? Use an ArtSet entry keyed by the asset's View Key for sprites and animation frames (the Unit Workshop supports bulk frame registration), or assign a prefab in the asset's View section (or in the Entity View Registry's Overrides by view key). Add an EntityView component to the prefab to control the body renderer and sorting.

Input System or legacy Input Manager? Both work. The HUD reads input through PointerInput, which uses the Input System package when it is installed and enabled, and the legacy Input Manager otherwise.

Where do stars and permanent upgrades go? Win a campaign level, return to its world map and open Upgrades. The sample campaign awards at most nine stars; each shop track costs 0 / 0 / 1 / 2 / 3 stars, so take its free starter ranks first. Purchases are saved in the active slot and apply when the next battle starts. See Campaigns, Progress and Saves.

Mobile / touch? This release is PC only (mouse and keyboard; touch UI not yet). The core is platform-independent; other platforms require your own input/UI and target-device testing.

Can I add a new mechanic without editing package code? Yes: custom systems, per-entity data, target selectors, damage hooks, ability actions and commands. See Extending the Framework and the compiled examples in Samples/Extending.

Where are the logs from Dry Run and the Validator? The Map Editor shows Validate, Dry Run and the latest results above its scrolling content. Click the error/warning summary to open the full Validator list. The complete Dry Run report and ValidatorWindow.RunBatch results are also written to the Console.

Why is the interface still English after I set the Inspector language to ko? In the Editor, enable Ignore Saved Language In Editor and set Language to ko. If that option is disabled, the saved PlayerPrefs language takes precedence. You can also select Korean from the sample title screen. Keep the Korean text table and the sample theme's fallback font assigned together.

Why is there no spell button in my fresh level? Enable Include Starter Spell in the New Level wizard. For an existing level, create a Spell in Unit Workshop and add it to the Level asset's Spells list. Audio is a separate choice: Use Sample Sounds is off by default for fresh content.

Why does clicking a tower not open its panel? If you are aiming a hero move, spell or rally point, right-click to cancel first. By default, both the tower body sprite and its pad are clickable. If Custom Area is enabled, only the authored rectangle is used.

Which time zone do save-slot timestamps use? Saves record the operating system's UTC time in ISO 8601 format. The slot screen displays local time using the Gregorian yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm format. Existing timestamps are preserved; correcting the system clock does not rewrite older save dates.

Does a colored Wave Set icon mean there is an error? 2D Tower Defense Maker does not assign a special red warning icon to Wave Sets. Check the Validator's error/warning counts and Inspector messages rather than judging an asset by its icon color.

docs.title: Mechanic Library
docs.text:
Ready-made building blocks for common tower defense mechanics. Each one is a core definition (TDMaker.Core.Defs) with a matching serializable authoring block (TDMaker.Unity.Authoring), so designers can attach it to towers, tower abilities, enemies, hero skills, spells and projectiles without code. The view draws every one of them out of the box.

Mechanic Core definition Authoring block Where you attach it Chain attack ChainAttackDef ChainAttackData Ability / skill / behavior action: Use Chain + Chain Multi-target attack MultiTargetAttackDef MultiTargetAttackData Action: Use Multi Target + Multi Target Recipient filter MechanicTargetDef MechanicTargetData Targets of chains, multi-target attacks, impact payloads and pulses Impact payload ImpactPayloadDef ImpactPayloadData Any attack damage: Damage > Impact Path displacement (knockback / pull) PathDisplacementDef ImpactPayloadData.useDisplacement + displacement Inside an impact payload Region pulse AreaPulseDef AreaPulseData Any area effect: Area > Pulse (an area without a status effect becomes pulse-only) Healing HealingDef HealingData Pulses and periodic healing Periodic healing PeriodicHealingDef PeriodicHealingData Status effect: Healing Shield ShieldDef ShieldData Status effect: Shield Combat modifier CombatModifierDef CombatModifierData Stat modifier: Combat (status effects, ability passives) Trap (mine, snare) TrapDef TrapData Action: Use Trap + Trap Beam (channel) BeamDef BeamData Action: Use Beam + Beam Reflection (thorns) ReflectionDef ReflectionData Enemy: Reflection Life steal LifeStealDef LifeStealData Any attack damage: Damage > Life Steal Path destination PathDestinationDef PathDestinationData Inside a transfer action or an impact payload Path transfer PathTransferDef PathTransferData Action: Use Transfer + Transfer; hits: Impact > Use Transfer Permanent aura AreaEffectDef.WithOwnerLifetime / CreateOwned AreaEffectData.untilSourceLost Enemy Aura: Until Source Lost Mine field (automatic mine laying) DeploymentPlanDef (+ TrapDef) MineFieldData Action: Use Mines + Mines Companions (escorts, followers) CompanionDef CompanionData Hero / Tower: Companions Return on the spot ReviveDef ReviveData Enemy: Revive Successor rules SummonDef.WithDeathSuccession DeathSuccessionData Enemy: Death Succession (with Death Summon) Raising the fallen RaiseRemainsDef RaiseRemainsData Action: Use Raise + Raise

Projectiles can additionally leave a region where they land: ProjectileAsset > Impact Area (core: ProjectileDef.WithImpactArea).

docs.title: Chain attack
docs.text:
One activation hits a first target near the actor, then jumps from victim to victim. Each victim is hit at most once per chain.

Field Meaning Id Event key; also selects the arc colour in the view. Use one id per look. Damage Damage at each link (may carry status effects and an impact payload). Range Range of the first link from the actor (scaled by the actor's range modifier). Link Range Range from one victim to the next. Max Targets Distinct victims including the first. Link Delay Game seconds between links (0 still waits for the next tick). Link Scale Damage multiplier applied after each link (0.8 = every jump deals 20% less). Chance One roll per activation; a failed roll still uses the cooldown. Targets, Targets Flying, Targets Ground Victim eligibility. Cancel With Source Remaining links stop if the actor dies, disappears, is stunned, disarmed or ordered to rally. Color, Vfx Arc colour and an optional pooled VFX spawned on each victim.

Each link picks the nearest eligible enemy (ties: lower Id). Chains run from a fixed pool (SimConfig.ChainCapacity, runner field Chain Capacity, default 64); unfinished chains count as pending work, so the level does not end while one is running.

Events: ChainStarted (IntValue = chain id), ChainLinked per victim, ChainEnded (Value = victims), MechanicMissed on a failed roll.

docs.title: Multi-target attack
docs.text:
One activation hits several distinct targets at once.

Field Meaning Id Event key and beam colour key. Damage Independent hit per target. Range, Max Targets Search ellipse and number of targets. Health Budget Optional: the chosen targets' summed current health cannot exceed this (0 = no budget). Requires single-target damage. Useful for "finish off several weak enemies". Chance, Targets, Targets Flying, Targets Ground As for chains. Color, Vfx Beam colour and optional VFX per target.

Towers order targets by their current target priority; other actors take the nearest first. Events: MechanicTargeted per target, then MechanicActivated (IntValue = targets hit).

docs.title: Recipient filter (Targets)
docs.text:
Field Meaning Required Tags / Rejected Tags Bit masks matched against the recipient's Tags (Enemy, Soldier and Hero assets have a Tags field). Allow Heroes Heroes may be chosen. Maximum Health Ratio Only recipients at or below this share of their maximum health (1 = any). Maximum Health Only recipients at or below this current health (0 = off).

Tags are your own convention: decide what each bit means (the Basic sample uses bit 0 = support, bit 1 = heavy).

docs.title: Impact payload (Damage > Impact)
docs.text:
Extra work after a resolved hit, rolled once per hit:

Field Meaning Enabled, Chance Turn on; probability per eligible hit. Trigger On Zero Damage Also trigger on hits that removed no health (control-only attacks). Immune targets never trigger. Targets Extra victim eligibility, checked before the damage is applied. Use Secondary Damage + Secondary Damage An independent extra hit centred on the victim (give it a radius for a blast). Area A residual region left at the impact point, even if the victim died (status effect and/or pulse). Use Displacement + Displacement Moves a surviving victim along its own path and lane: negative = back toward the entry (knockback), positive = toward the exit. Clamped to the path; blockers are released. Use Transfer + Destination Moves a surviving victim to an exact path point (after any displacement); see Path destination and transfer. A payload with only a transfer needs no dummy damage.

Events: ImpactPayloadTriggered (IntValue bits: secondary damage 1, area 2, displacement 4, path transfer 8), Displaced, PathTransferred.

docs.title: Region pulses, pulse-only regions and healing
docs.text:
Every area effect (AreaEffectData: tower/skill actions, spells, enemy auras, impact payloads, projectile impact areas) can carry a Pulse:

Field Meaning Enabled, Id Turn on; event key (also the ring colour key). Use Damage + Damage Single-target hit on every occupant per scan (the region is the area; the damage radius is ignored). Use Healing + Healing Amount + Maximum Health Share restored to every occupant per scan (never above maximum health; not affected by damage multipliers). Targets Extra occupant eligibility. Color, Vfx Ring colour and optional VFX per pulse.

Occupants are re-scanned every Interval; nothing lingers after a unit leaves. Leave Effect empty for a pulse-only region – no dummy status effect is needed. Targets Enemies selects the enemy faction (so an enemy aura with Targets Enemies on heals other enemies). Event: AreaPulsed (Value = radius, IntValue = occupants affected, Key = pulse id).

Periodic healing on a status effect (Healing): Healing, Interval, Heal On Attach, Heal On Expire (natural expiry only). Refreshing the effect does not reset its cadence. Event: Healed.

docs.title: Shields
docs.text:
A status effect with Shield enabled gives each accepted attachment its own shield:

Field Meaning Amount + Maximum Health Share Capacity, snapshotted when attached. Channels Damage kinds absorbed (after armor and resistance). Execute and despawn hits bypass shields. Refill On Refresh Re-applying at equal rank refills the shield; otherwise the remaining capacity is kept.

Several shields absorb in attachment order; removing the effect discards unused capacity. Events: ShieldChanged (Value = capacity, 0 when gone), ShieldAbsorbed. The view draws a bubble that fades with the remaining capacity.

docs.title: Combat modifier (Modifier > Combat)
docs.text:
Field Meaning Range Scale Multiplies attack ranges, including melee contact (area sizes are not scaled). Tower range support or "nearsighted" debuffs. Disable Attacks No attacks or ability actions; movement and recovery continue (for example a tower jam). Ignore Blocking Cannot be blocked; current blockers are released (dashes). Untargetable Attacks cannot select the unit (concealment); status effects keep their own rules.

Stacked flags are reference-counted and fully reversed on removal. Events: CombatControlChanged (IntValue bits: attacks disabled 1, ignores blocking 2, untargetable 4), AttackRangeChanged. The view greys out disarmed units and draws untargetable units translucent.

docs.title: Traps (Action > Use Trap)
docs.text:
A fixed-position deployment (mine, snare, glyph). It arms after a delay, then hits the nearest eligible unit inside its detection radius until its triggers or lifetime run out.

Field Meaning Id Event key and marker colour key; also the population-limit key (per source). Damage Hit on trigger. An area packet (Radius > 0) is centred on the trap; a single-target packet hits the triggering unit. May carry effects, an impact payload and life steal. Trigger Radius Detection ellipse, independent of the damage radius. Lifetime, Arm Delay Total lifetime (including arming) and the delay before it can trigger. A trap never acts in the tick it was placed. Max Triggers, Trigger Cooldown Activations before it is used up, and the delay between them (at most one per tick). Population Limit Live traps with this id per source (0 = unlimited). When full, the action does not succeed and its cooldown does not restart. Area Optional region left at the trap on every trigger (status effect and/or pulse). Targets Enemies, Targets Flying, Targets Ground, Targets Who triggers it. Area victims use normal damage eligibility. Cancel With Source Off (default): the trap outlives its source with the damage multiplier and hero credit captured at placement. On: removed when the source dies. Placement, Placement Range, Offset Source (actor position), Rally (barracks/hero rally point, else the actor) or Opponent (nearest eligible unit within the range). The offset is added before validation. Use Custom Point Rule + Point Rule Placement validation; by default the point is snapped onto the nearest lane. A rejected point cancels the activation. Color, Vfx Marker colour and optional VFX per trigger.

Traps come from a fixed pool (SimConfig.WithAdvancedCapacity, default 128). Remaining friendly traps do not delay victory. Code can also place one at an explicit point: Simulation.PlaceTrap(def, point, sourceId) / RemoveTrap(id).

Events: TrapPlaced (IntValue = trap id, Value = lifetime), TrapArmed (Value = detection radius), TrapTriggered (OtherId = triggering unit, Value = damage radius), TrapRemoved (Value = MechanicEndReason: Completed, Expired, SourceLost, Cancelled). The view draws a dim pulsing marker while arming, a solid marker with a detection ring once armed, a flash and blast ring per trigger, and fades the marker out on removal.

Spells cannot place traps yet (a spell has no action payload); use a hero skill or a tower ability.

docs.title: Mine fields (Action > Use Mines)
docs.text:
Automatic mine laying for towers, hero skills and enemy behaviors (core: DeploymentPlanDef with a TrapDef payload). Each activation picks one lane node of a level path inside a distance band around the producer – a seeded, deterministic pick among the valid nodes, not the spot under an enemy – reserves it together with a trap slot, throws the mine (flight, landing, then the arming delay) and leaves a trap that bursts under the first eligible unit.

Field Meaning Id Event key: marker colour, keyed audio cue, mine limit key. An art set entry with this key replaces the generated marker. Damage, Trigger Radius, Max Triggers, Area, Targets … As for traps: an area packet re-searches its victims around the mine; a single-target packet hits the triggering unit. A detection radius of about a quarter to a third of the blast radius reads well. Lifetime Counted from the throw: flight, landing and arming use it up. An unused mine fades out without exploding. Arm Delay After the landing preparation. Keep When Source Lost On (default): mines already laid stay when the producer is sold or dies, with their damage multiplier and hero credit captured at the throw. Minimum Distance, Maximum Distance The placement band (range ellipses around the producer). Only lane nodes inside it are candidates; denser node runs are picked more often. Side Clearance Minimum horizontal offset of a site from the producer. Minimum Spacing, Spacing Scope Distance to other mines, including those still in flight; Owner checks this producer's mines, Global every deployment (spell traps too). Max Mines Mines of this id alive or in flight per producer. A full field rejects the throw (old mines are never replaced); the action then does not succeed and its cooldown does not restart. Transit Duration, Settle Duration Flight time and landing preparation (the mine cannot trigger before transit + settle + arm delay). Use Custom Point Rule + Point Rule Terrain check for every candidate node; a node the rule would move is skipped.

No candidate means no throw – there is no fallback spot. A mine whose lifetime ends in the same tick an enemy reaches it explodes (detection wins); expiry itself never explodes. Events: TrapPlaced and DeploymentReserved (IntValue = trap id, Position = site), DeploymentInTransit, DeploymentLanded, then the trap events TrapArmed, TrapTriggered, TrapRemoved (Value = MechanicEndReason). The view throws the marker along an arc from the producer, flashes the landing spot, shows the detection ring once armed with a short fuse blink, draws the blast and lets an expired mine sink and fade slowly. The Workshop's tower Mechanics tab has + Mine-laying ability for a ready two-rank ability.

docs.title: Companions (Hero / Tower > Companions)
docs.text:
Owner-bound slots (core: CompanionDef, template custom data). Each slot keeps one child alive; a fallen child is replaced Refill Delay seconds after its death. Child damage earns the owner experience.

Field Meaning Unit A Soldier asset. Ground escorts: not flying, with melee to block. Flying followers: Flying on (Soldier asset), usually with a ranged attack. Slots, Mode Ground Escort walks, blocks and fights like a soldier and takes new places around the owner on every hero move order or rally point. Flying Follower flies after the owner and never blocks; it attacks from where it is. Refill Delay, Initial Delay Refill after a loss; first arrival after the owner appears. Formation Radius Ground escorts' places around the owner's last move / rally point. Follow Start Distance, Follow Stop Distance, Acceleration Flying followers: start moving beyond the start distance, stop at the stop distance (start must be larger). Wait On Owner Death On (default): children return to the dead owner and stop fighting; they reconnect when it comes back. Remove With Owner, Reconnect On Return On (default): children leave when a tower is sold; waiting children rejoin a returning hero (off: they leave instead). Remove With Owner off: they stay on as independent units. Rally Radius Towers without barracks: how far a SetRallyPoint command may move the escorts (Simulation.TryResolveRallyPoint).
