The sample HUD offers the rally button on barracks only; on a barracks the escorts follow its rally point. Use Custom Point Rule + Point Rule Ground spawn / reposition points (default: on a lane). An invalid point leaves the slot empty.

Empty friendly slots never hold victory. Events: CompanionSpawned (EntityId = child, OtherId = owner, IntValue = slot, Key = child template), CompanionWaiting, CompanionReconnected, CompanionRetired, CompanionDetached. The view draws a short tether and a ring where a child arrives, dims waiting children and fades retiring ones out. The Validator reports flying mismatches as errors (the level would not start).

docs.title: Return on the spot (Enemy > Revive)
docs.text:
The same unit lies down when killed, gets Return Share of its maximum health back after Down Delay, rises for Rise Duration and walks on with the same identity (core: ReviveDef). Returns counts over its lifetime; the death after the last one is final. While down it neither moves nor fights; while rising it may ignore damage (Invulnerable While Rising) and be skipped by attacks (Untargetable While Rising), independently. Clear Effects removes its status effects when it falls.

Its bounty is paid once (on the first death) and a split on death (Death Summon) happens only after the last return. Pending returns hold victory. Events: Died, then UnitDowned (IntValue = returns used), UnitRising (Value = rise time), UnitRevived. The view keeps the unit (no death fade), turns it onto its side and darkens it, hides its health bar, and tweens it upright while it rises. The Sandbox counts falls separately from kills.

docs.title: Successor rules (Enemy > Death Succession)
docs.text: Extra rules for the enemies released by Death Summon (core: SummonDef.WithDeathSuccession): Chain Budget – death releases the whole lineage may make (one release can hold several siblings; 1 = successors do not release again), Rise Duration – successors rise before they act (optionally invulnerable / untargetable), Bounty Policy – Once Per Lineage (a lineage never pays twice) or Suppress Successor. A lineage leaks one life cost at most once, whichever member gets through. Successors inherit the dead unit's path position and travel direction.

docs.title: Raising the fallen (Action > Use Raise)
docs.text:
Killed units leave a body (a neutral record: position, path position, side, kind, tags, cause). A raise action reserves the closest eligible bodies (ties by body order), casts for Cast Delay, then consumes each body and creates Unit there (core: RaiseRemainsDef). An Enemy result is hostile and continues the body's path; a Soldier result fights for the player.

Field Meaning Id, Color, Vfx Event key, cast colour, optional VFX where a body is raised. Unit Created from each body; the body's own stats are not copied. Range, Max Count Body search radius around the caster and bodies per activation. Cast Delay, Rise Duration, Reservation Timeout Reservation to consumption; the result's rise time; the time-out (0 = cast delay + 1 s). Bodies, From Enemies / Soldiers / Heroes, Required Tags Whose bodies qualify. Hostile results need a body that was on a path. Skip Suppressed Deaths, Skip Executed, Minimum Age, Maximum Age Cause and age filters (maximum 0 = until the body decays). Population Limit, Chain Budget Raised units of this caster at once (reservations included); raises a lineage may make (1 = a raised unit's body cannot be raised again). Invulnerable While Rising, Untargetable While Rising Protection of the raised unit while it rises.

A caster that moves, is stunned or dies releases its reservations; a body that decays is not extended by a reservation. The body is consumed only after the new unit is created, so a full entity pool releases the reservation instead. Raised enemies share the body's lineage, so they pay no second bounty. Bodies are kept by the Simulation Runner (Remains Capacity, default 256, 0 keeps none; Remains Lifetime, default 10 s; core: SimConfig.WithRemains); a full store does not push old bodies out. Reserved bodies hold victory; unreserved ones do not.

Events: RemainsCreated (EntityId = dead unit, IntValue = body id), RemainsReserved (EntityId = caster, Value = cast delay), RemainsReleased, RemainsConsumed (OtherId = new unit). In levels where something raises bodies the view draws a small body marker for each available body (art set key remains replaces it), makes a reserved body glow, draws a tether from the caster for the cast time and flashes where the unit rises (the new unit starts lying and gets up).

docs.title: Beams (Action > Use Beam)
docs.text:
A continuous single-target channel with an exact total damage budget split over pulses.

Field Meaning Id Event key; beam colour and width key. Damage Channel (Kind), pierce, on-hit effects, impact payload and life steal. Minimum/Maximum and Radius are ignored – the budget decides the amount. Total Damage Raw damage of one channel before defenses, multiplied once by the source's damage multiplier and rounded up. Pulse Count, Interval, First Delay The budget is split evenly; earlier pulses take the remainder (100 over 3 pulses = 34, 33, 33). Range Targeting range and tracking limit; the beam ends when the target leaves it. The target is never switched. Targets, Targets Flying, Targets Ground Rechecked on every pulse. Cancel With Source On (default): ends when the source dies, is stunned or disarmed, or is ordered to move. Off: continues from the source's last position. Color, Width, Vfx Line look and optional VFX on the target per pulse.

The budget is counted before armor, shields and hooks: mitigated, absorbed or rejected slices are not refunded, and an interrupted beam does not deal its remainder. Unfinished beams count as pending work. Pool: SimConfig.WithAdvancedCapacity (default 64); code can stop one with Simulation.CancelBeam(id).

Events: BeamStarted (IntValue = beam id, OtherId = target, Value = captured budget), BeamPulsed (Value = raw slice), BeamEnded (Value = MechanicEndReason: Completed, TargetLost, OutOfRange, SourceLost, Interrupted, Cancelled). The view keeps one pooled line per beam from start to end, following the source and target views, widening on every pulse and fading out at the end.

docs.title: Reflection (Enemy > Reflection)
docs.text:
Thorns: when the unit loses health, a Share of the actual loss (shield absorption and overkill excluded, rounded up) is returned to the attacker as one single-target hit of Kind (with optional pierce).

  • Reflected hits never reflect again and never steal life, so two reflecting units cannot loop.
  • Dead attackers, attackers without health (towers) and self-damage are skipped; a unit that dies from the hit still reflects it.

Event: DamageReflected (EntityId = reflecting unit, OtherId = attacker, Value = returned raw amount, Key = Id). The view draws a short line from the reflecting unit to the attacker and a flash on the attacker in the reflection Color.

docs.title: Life steal (Damage > Life Steal)
docs.text:
The attacker recovers Health Share × the health this packet actually removed, plus Flat Healing per qualifying hit, up to its missing health.

Field Meaning Id, Color Event key and feedback colour. Health Share, Flat Healing Healing formula. Include Periodic Also steal from the damage-over-time ticks of effects carried by this packet. Heal Credit Owner Heal the hero credited with the hit instead of the immediate source (for example a hero's trap or summon).

Units without health (towers) cannot be healed. Events: LifeStolen (EntityId = healed unit, OtherId = victim, Value = restored health) and the usual Healed (heal numbers). The view draws a thin line from the victim to the healed unit.

docs.title: Path destination and transfer
docs.text:
A path destination (Path Index, Node Index, Lane Index, Progress, Clear Effects) is an exact point on a level path: the segment starting at Node Index, Progress of the way to the next node. Lane Index -1 keeps the unit's lane (modulo the destination's lane count). It is checked against the level when used: a path, lane or node outside the path's entry..exit range moves nothing (the validator reports it as an error for the level's towers and heroes).

A transfer action (Use Transfer + Transfer: Id, Destination, Range, Max Targets, Targets) moves up to Max Targets path-following enemies within Range, nearest first. Hits can do the same through Impact > Use Transfer.

A moved unit is released from blockers, its attack cycles restart, its own cancellable chains and beams end, and with Clear Effects its effects are removed. Event: PathTransferred (EntityId = unit, OtherId = source, IntValue = path index, Value = progress, Position = destination). The view snaps the unit (no sliding across the map), draws a trail from where it was and replays its appear pop; the trail colour is the registry's Transfer Color.

docs.title: Permanent auras (Area > Until Source Lost)
docs.text:
An area with Until Source Lost has no timed expiry: it lasts while its source is alive and is removed – together with the effects it attached – when the source dies or is removed. Heroes re-emit their permanent auras when they return. Attached effects still follow their own duration and refresh rules; only the region's lifetime is permanent.

Use it for enemy Auras. A spell or impact area has no living source and emits nothing; on an ability action every activation would add another permanent region, so the validator warns in both cases.

docs.title: Combining in actions
docs.text:
An ability, hero skill or enemy behavior action can combine its built-in payloads (Attack, Self Effect, Summon, Area) with Use Chain, Use Multi Target, Use Trap, Use Mines, Use Beam, Use Transfer, Use Raise and a Custom Action asset (Extending the Framework). They run together on the action's cooldown. The action succeeds when any payload succeeds; only then does the cooldown restart and a hero earn Skill Experience Per Rank × rank (core: new AbilityActionDef(action, cooldown, initialDelay, skillExperiencePerRank)).

The enemy Mechanics fields include:

  • Tags – their tag bits.
  • Behavior – always-on action channels (for example "every 7 s, shield nearby allies").
  • Aura – a region emitted when the unit appears. For a permanent aura enable Until Source Lost (and Follow Source).
  • Reflection – thorns.
  • Death Summon + Death Succession – split on death and the successor rules.
  • Revive – return on the spot.

docs.title: Projectile accuracy
docs.text: Ballistic and straight shots aim where the target will be along its actual path when the shot lands, with the same flight time used for aiming and for the flight (fixed Flight Time, or solved from distance and speed). Blocked, stunned or stopped targets are not led. Homing shots track; instant shots hit at once. The Dry Run reports, per source, ballistic shots fired, landed, damaging, landed after the target was already gone, and landed beside a live target (with the average miss distance).

docs.title: In the Basic sample
docs.text:
Content Mechanics used Storm Spire › Arc Lightning Chain attack (4 → 6 victims, 20% weaker per jump) Volley Nest › Split Volley Multi-target attack Cannon III › Concussion Shell, Warden › Shield Bash Impact payload with knockback; Targets rejects the heavy tag (Brutes) Void Spire › Null Lance Beam: 140 → 200 magic damage over 8 → 10 pulses Void Spire › Rift Path transfer: the two nearest light enemies go back to the north road's second node Garrison III › Caltrops Trap at the rally point: arms after 1 s, area burst plus a short chill region, up to 2 → 3 live Warden › Snare Trap placed under the nearest enemy; trap-only action that still awards skill experience Warden blade Life steal (25% of health removed) Brute enemy Reflection: 25% of the health it loses goes back to its attacker as physical damage Mender enemy Behavior action casting the Ward shield effect on nearby allies; permanent pulse-only healing aura (Effect empty, Until Source Lost) Ward status effect Shield with refill on refresh

The mine field, companion and revival samples are prepared by SampleContentGenerator.GenerateReleaseMechanicSamples (also callable with -executeMethod): Volley Nest › Barbed Mines (mine field, venom blast, 3 → 5 mines), Warden › Hound (ground-escort companion, refilled 10 s after it falls), Revenant (returns once with half its health) and Gravecaller (raises up to two Husks from nearby enemy bodies). The full sample generator already connects Revenants and Gravecallers to later waves in all three sample levels, gives the Warden its Hound, and adds Barbed Mines to Volley Nest. The standalone method updates only those mechanic assets.

docs.title: Coding against the definitions
docs.text:
using TDMaker.Core.Defs;

var arc = new ChainAttackDef("arc", new DamageDef(DamageKind.Electric, 20, 30), range: 3, linkRange: 1.6f, maxTargets: 4, linkScale: 0.8f);
var chainAction = new AbilityActionDef(arc, cooldown: 5);                     // a chain is an IAbilityAction

var knockback = new DamageDef(DamageKind.Physical, 10, 15)
    .WithImpact(new ImpactPayloadDef(displacement: new PathDisplacementDef(-1.2f)));

var heal = AreaEffectDef.CreatePulse(new AreaPulseDef("mend", healing: new HealingDef(5)), radius: 1.6f, duration: 1, interval: 1.5f,
    followSource: true).WithOwnerLifetime();                                     // permanent pulse-only region
var aura = new AuraDef(heal);

var caltrops = new TrapDef("caltrops", new DamageDef(DamageKind.Explosion, 20, 30, radius: 0.9f), triggerRadius: 0.6f, lifetime: 20,
    armDelay: 1, populationLimit: 2, placement: TrapPlacement.Rally);
var lance = new BeamDef("lance", new DamageDef(DamageKind.Magical, 1, 1), totalDamage: 140, pulseCount: 8, interval: 0.2f, range: 3.6f);
var snare = new AbilityActionDef(caltrops, cooldown: 9, initialDelay: 1, skillExperiencePerRank: 3);  // hero skill XP on a trap-only action

var drain = new DamageDef(DamageKind.Physical, 10, 16).WithLifeSteal(new LifeStealDef("drain", healthShare: 0.25f));
var thorns = new EntityRulesDef().WithReflection(new ReflectionDef("thorns", 0.25f, new DamageDef(DamageKind.Physical, 1, 1)));
var rift = new PathTransferDef("rift", new PathDestinationDef(pathIndex: 0, nodeIndex: 1), range: 3, maxTargets: 2);

var mines = new DeploymentPlanDef(new TrapDef("mines", new DamageDef(DamageKind.Explosion, 30, 45, radius: 1), triggerRadius: 0.3f, lifetime: 30, armDelay: 0.5f),
    minimumDistance: 0.6f, maximumDistance: 3, minimumSpacing: 0.6f, populationLimit: 4, transitDuration: 0.6f, settleDuration: 0.2f);
var mineAction = new AbilityActionDef(mines, cooldown: 5);                      // a deployment plan is an IAbilityAction
var withHound = heroTemplate.WithCustomData(new CompanionDef("hound", slots: 1, refillDelay: 10));
var revenant = enemyTemplate.WithCustomData(new ReviveDef(returns: 1, downDelay: 1.5f, riseDuration: 1, returnShare: 0.5f));
var raise = new RaiseRemainsDef("raise", "husk", range: 2.4f, maxCount: 2, castDelay: 1.2f, riseDuration: 1, populationLimit: 4);
var config = new SimConfig(30, 0.8f).WithRemains(capacity: 256, lifetime: 10);

var ward = new StatusEffectDef("ward", duration: 5).WithShield(new ShieldDef(amount: 30, refillOnRefresh: true));
var jam = new StatusEffectDef("jam", duration: 3, modifier: new StatModifierDef().WithCombat(new CombatModifierDef(disableAttacks: true)));

docs.title: Maker and Samples
docs.text: 2D Tower Defense Maker is a reusable runtime framework and a set of authoring tools. You create and own the content of your game. The complete sample game is an optional reference implementation.

docs.title: Install the Maker
docs.text:
1. Import 2D-Tower-Defense-Maker-0.1.0.unitypackage into a Unity 6 URP 2D project.
  2. Import TMP Essential Resources once when prompted.
  3. Open Tools > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Welcome, then New Level.
  4. Keep Fresh starter assets selected and Use Sample Sounds off. Create the level in your own folder, such as Assets/TDMakerContent/MyLevel.
  5. Edit the paths, build slots, units and waves, then play. Follow Quick Start.

The Maker package works on its own. The default New Level flow does not load the sample game's scene generator, string tables, artwork, audio, campaign or balance assets. It creates a Level, Wave Set, HUD Theme, units, material and scene inside your chosen folder. A fresh HUD uses the project's TMP default font until you assign your own font in its theme.

docs.title: Add optional examples
docs.text:
Import 2D-Tower-Defense-Maker-Samples-0.1.0.unitypackage after the Maker package. Then open Tools > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Samples > Browse Samples.

Part Purpose Location Maker runtime Simulation, authoring components, views, configurable HUD, campaign/save/shop systems Assets/TDMaker/Runtime/ Maker tools New Level, Workshop, Map Editor, Wave Timeline, Upgrade Tree, Validator and Dry Run Assets/TDMaker/Editor/ except Editor/Samples/ Your game Your own scenes, units, waves, settings and chosen presentation Assets/TDMakerContent/ by default, or your own folder Complete sample game Example title, slots, world map, star shop and three battles Assets/TDMaker/Samples/Demo/ Feature examples Basic, Crossroads, Winding Pass and compiled extension examples Assets/TDMaker/Samples/ Sample presentation Original art, audio, Inter, Korean fallback and example text tables Assets/TDMaker/Samples/ Sample authoring utilities Optional generator, sample art importer and screenshot driver Assets/TDMaker/Editor/Samples/

The sample add-on uses the same Maker runtime. It does not contain a second copy of the engine. Existing sample paths, asset GUIDs and TDMaker.* namespaces are preserved.

Fresh starter assets is the default and creates independent content. Reuse sample kit and Use Sample Sounds deliberately reference the optional add-on. If you choose them, keep the referenced sample assets or replace those references with your own assets before removing the add-on. Regenerating sample content resets generated example files; it does not regenerate your own New Level folder.

docs.title: Features are choices, samples are examples
docs.text:
• Campaigns, saving and the permanent star shop are reusable Maker features. The sample's map, track prices, unlock sequence and title menu are example content.
  • The engine supports both automatic hero skill unlocking and explicit skill-point purchases. The compact sample HUD shows portraits and health bars, so its heroes use automatic skill growth. To use SpendPoints in your own game, enable Hero Skill Buttons on Game HUD or supply a skill-allocation UI. Combat skill points are separate from the campaign's saved star-upgrade shop.
  • The sample game starts in English and has no title-screen language buttons. String tables, Korean fallback fonts and the language API remain available for your own game.
  • The compact sample battle HUD displays spell buttons without a large background panel. Hero portraits and health bars sit at the bottom left. You may restyle or replace the HUD through HudTheme and the runtime API.

Use the examples to learn the authoring model. Start production content with New Level and keep it in your own folder.

docs.title: Performance
docs.text: Measure simulation work, views, UI and rendering separately on your target devices. Content density, effect concurrency and the selected game speed all affect the work performed in a rendered frame. Warm pools and shaders before measuring steady-state behavior, and include pool growth when measuring startup and new concurrency peaks.

docs.title: Profiler markers
docs.text:
In the Editor and in development players the runner wraps the simulation in Unity Profiler markers, so the CPU Usage module shows where a tick goes:

  • TDMaker.Runner.Advance → TDMaker.Sim.Step → one marker per stage: TDMaker.Sim.Commands, Waves, Effects, Motion, Blocking, Melee, Ranged, Projectiles, Damage, Death, Exits, HeroesAndSpells, Flow, Flush. Custom systems appear as TDMaker.Sim.<anchor stage>#<index>.
  • TDMaker.Runner.Dispatch → TDMaker.Views.OnEvent, TDMaker.Hud.OnEvent, TDMaker.DamageNumbers.OnEvent (the event handlers of the frame).

Turn the stage markers off with Profiler Markers on the Simulation Runner (they compile away in non-development players anyway). To time stages yourself, implement ISimProfiler (preallocate, do not allocate in callbacks) and assign it to SimulationRunner.Profiler; it is chained behind the markers.

docs.title: How the core stays cheap
docs.text:
• Fixed pools. All entity bundles, components, event and damage buffers are allocated when the simulation is created (SimConfig.EntityCapacity default 1024, EventCapacity 8192, CommandCapacity 128; SimConfig.WithLimits(new SimLimits(effects, areas, schedules)) for effects, areas and scheduled summons).
  • No allocation in the tick path, no LINQ, lists are reused.
  • Spatial grid for enemy range queries (Simulation.ConfigureSpatialIndex(cellSize: 4) before the first step; enabled: false switches to an Id-ordered linear scan with identical results).
  • Per-role entity lists (Enemies, Towers, Soldiers, Projectiles, Heroes) avoid scanning everything.

docs.title: Capacity limits
docs.text:
When a pool or buffer is full, the simulation degrades instead of allocating:

Situation Behavior Counter No free entity (spawns, projectiles, soldiers) Spawn waits or fails Simulation.CapacityFailureCount Too many damage requests in one tick (limit = EventCapacity) Request dropped Simulation.DroppedDamageCount Event buffer full (events not cleared) New events are dropped Simulation.DroppedEventCount Command queue full Command rejected with CapacityExceeded —

Except for a full event buffer, each case also emits a CapacityExceeded event whose Key names the pool (for example Entities, Damage, Commands).

Event capacity and game speed. SimulationRunner delivers events once per frame, so the buffer must hold every tick a frame catches up – at most Catch Up Ticks Per Speed × speed ticks (24 at 3× with the default 8). The default Event Capacity of 8192 therefore covers about 340 events per tick at 3× in the worst catch-up frame (at a steady 60 fps a 3× frame runs only 1–2 ticks). If a denser level drops events, the runner logs one warning per run and Simulation.DroppedEventCount rises; raise Event Capacity (it also sizes the per-tick damage queue). The Dry Run report prints the peak per tick and per 24 ticks for your own levels.

If you see these counters rise, raise the capacities in the Simulation Runner Inspector (Capacities: entities, events, commands, effects, areas, schedules, chains; SimulationRunner.CreateConfig() builds the SimConfig) or reduce content density. Chains run from their own pool (Chain Capacity, default 64); each chain job preallocates one visited-target array of Entity Capacity.

docs.title: View-side tips
docs.text:
• Views and projectile visuals are pooled by EntityViewRegistry (Prewarm Primitives); primitive entries prepare trails, status pips and shields before the fight, so switching a former projectile view to a unit does not add those components mid-fight. Use prefabs with few renderers; avoid per-frame allocations in custom EventRaised handlers.
  • At high speed several ticks run per frame; keep event handlers light.
  • Catch Up Ticks Per Speed on the runner limits catch-up work after a slow frame (value × speed ticks per frame).
  • GameHud (uGUI) is the production HUD. The IMGUI TDHud is a reference/debug overlay; keep it disabled in shipping builds.
  • VFX hooks go through VfxPool (Max Active caps live instances) and mechanic feedback (arcs, rings, flashes) is pooled by EntityViewRegistry (Prewarm Feedback Fx, Max Feedback Fx per kind; extra effects are skipped rather than growing the pool).
  • The built-in views and HUD allocate nothing per frame once their pools have grown to the level's peak. Pools still grow (and allocate once) when a new peak of simultaneous units, projectiles or traps appears; raise Prewarm Primitives for very dense levels.

docs.title: Measuring your own content
docs.text:
• Use the Unity Profiler on a development player build; the simulation runs inside SimulationRunner.Update (see the markers above).
  • Tools > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Dry Run Level runs a whole level headlessly in the Editor and is a quick sanity check for content, not a benchmark.

docs.title: Presentation: HUD, Feedback, Camera and Audio
docs.text:
Everything on this page lives in the Unity layer (TDMaker.Unity.View, TDMaker.Unity.Hud). It only reads simulation state and events and sends commands; you can replace any piece without touching the core. The Basic sample scene wires all of them on the 2D Tower Defense Maker object (see SampleContentGenerator).

Component (Add Component > 2D Tower Defense Maker > …) Class Role Simulation Runner SimulationRunner Owns and advances the simulation; event source for everything below Entity View Registry EntityViewRegistry Pooled unit, tower and projectile views; built-in hit, death, spell and mechanic feedback Level View LevelView Generated placeholder ground with decorations, path ribbons and slot pads Game HUD GameHud Production uGUI HUD for mouse and keyboard, styled by a HudTheme Damage Numbers DamageNumbers Pooled floating damage and heal numbers VFX Pool VfxPool Pools VFX prefabs from presentation hooks Audio Cue Player AudioCuePlayer Pools AudioSources; plays global, mechanic and per-template cues Music Player MusicPlayer Menu / battle / intense loops with crossfade, victory and defeat stingers Camera Controller TDCameraController Frames the level (whole map by default; optional scrolling framings with pan and zoom) Game Settings TDGameSettings Player-facing toggles read by the camera, HUD and feedback Ellipse Renderer EllipseRenderer Draws a range ellipse (fill + outline) with the simulation's shape TD Hud TDHud Minimal IMGUI HUD, used by the sample as an F1 debug overlay

docs.title: SimulationRunner (scripting)
docs.text: Member Meaning Simulation, Baked The running world and its baked level (authoring lookups: TryGetAsset, GetTower, GetHero, GetSpell, TryGetProjectile, TryGetEffect, TryGetMechanicVisual). StartSimulation() / Restart() Bake and create a fresh world. Enqueue(command) Queue a player command (ignored while replaying). After victory/defeat the command is rejected with GameEnded on the next frame. Advance(realDeltaTime) Advance the clock and dispatch events. Called from Update; tools may call it directly (edit-mode captures, replays). Uses the core SimulationClock: at most Catch Up Ticks Per Speed × speed ticks per call. TimeScale, SetPaused(bool), IsPaused, SetSpeed(scale), ResumeScale Game speed; pause remembers the last non-zero speed. InterpolationAlpha Fraction of a tick for render interpolation. RangeYScale, DefaultRangeYScale Effective k of the running level, and the runner's own setting. StartingGoldOverride Debug: replaces the level's starting gold (≥ 0) on the next start. CreateConfig() The SimConfig built from the Inspector (tick rate, k, capacities). AddTemplateDecorator / RemoveTemplateDecorator Change baked templates before each start (Extending the Framework). RecordCommands, RecordingFile, ReplayOnStart, ReplayFile, CommandLog, IsReplaying, CommandCodec, SaveRecording() Built-in recording and replay (Determinism and Replay). SimulationStarted, EventRaised Events: new world created (register extensions); every simulation event, once per frame in emission order (the frame's events must fit Event Capacity; a warning is logged once per run if any are dropped).

docs.title: GameHud
docs.text:
Add Component > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Game HUD (TDMaker.Unity.Hud.GameHud). Built in uGUI from code at runtime – no prefabs to maintain – and styled by a HudTheme asset.

Contents: top bar (gold, lives, wave, pause, 1×/2×/3×), wave-call indicators at path entrances (countdown ring, early-call bonus), radial build menu, tower panel (upgrade/branch choices, ability ranks, target priority, rally, sell), compact hero portraits with health bars (manual skill buttons are an opt-in on Game HUD), spell bar with cooldowns and hotkeys, unit info, pause and victory/defeat screens with star rating, tooltips, toasts for rejected commands, and world feedback (range ellipses, slot highlight, placement ghost, rally/move markers, spell aim valid/invalid).

docs.title: Controls (PC mouse and keyboard)
docs.text:
One thing is selected or aimed at a time. A battlefield left click acts where the button is released (press and release must both be on the battlefield, not on HUD panels or buttons).

Situation Input Result Nothing selected, or a menu/info is open Left click an empty build slot / a tower Opens its build menu / tower panel (clicking the same one again keeps it open) Left click a soldier or an enemy Shows its info panel (not an attack order) Left click a hero, its portrait, or H Selects the hero for moving Left click empty ground or road Clears the selection Build menu / tower panel One click on a build, upgrade or branch item Buys it and closes the menu (hovering previews range, ghost and price; there is no second confirmation click) One click on an ability Buys one rank; the panel stays open One click on Sell Sells immediately (no confirmation by default) Click on Set Rally Hides the panel and starts rally aiming Hero selected Left click anywhere on the battlefield (ground, road, slot, tower, unit, the hero itself) Moves the hero to that point; a valid point ends the selection, an invalid one shows a marker and keeps the hero selected The same portrait again or H (after the last hero) Deselects Another hero's portrait Selects that hero Rally aiming Left click anywhere on the battlefield Sets the rally point when it is inside the ring and on an allowed lane spot (then back to browsing); otherwise a marker and aiming continues Spell aiming (spell button or 1–9) Left click anywhere on the battlefield, including empty ground Casts at that point when it is valid for the spell (then back to browsing and the cooldown starts); otherwise a marker and aiming continues, no cooldown is used The same spell button or key again Cancels aiming A locked or recharging spell button or key Nothing is selected Any selection or aim Right click (anywhere) or Esc Cancels everything and returns to browsing; never moves a hero; a cancelled rally keeps the old rally point Nothing selected Right click Nothing (it never pauses) Esc Opens the pause menu Pause menu Esc or Resume Closes it; the battle continues with nothing selected Result screen Esc Leaves the battle like the Quit button (when a Quit listener exists) Wave call One click on an entrance's call button, or N Calls the whole next wave at once (every entrance); hovering shows what comes through that entrance

Keys: Esc cancel / pause, Space or P pause, 1–9 spells, H hero, N next wave, F1 debug overlay. Product additions that a buyer can turn off: the 1× / 2× / 3× speed buttons (TDGameSettings.speedControls), the early-call gold preview on wave buttons and tooltips (showEarlyCallBonus, off by default), the tower panel's target-priority buttons and close button, and an optional sell confirmation (confirmSell, off). Camera pan and zoom exist only in levels whose Camera Framing scrolls; with left-drag pan on (leftDragPan, off by default) a press that turns into a drag pans the camera and is not also a click.

Click targets are world rectangles around each unit (the border itself is outside): heroes are roughly square, soldiers and enemies taller than wide, towers slightly wider than tall and empty build slots clearly wider than tall. Where rectangles overlap, a hero wins; otherwise the target whose position is lower on the map wins. Per content, View > Click Area on an entity asset replaces the rectangle (Custom Area, Size, Offset) and raises or lowers its priority (Priority Bonus).

The same entry points are public for tutorials, tests and other input devices: BattlefieldClick(worldPoint), SecondaryClick(), PressEscape(), PressSpellKey(index), PressHeroKey(), ClickHeroPortrait(heroId), CancelAll().

Field Meaning Runner, Registry, World Camera Dependencies (empty camera = Camera.main). Theme HudTheme asset (empty = built-in defaults). Debug Hud Optional TDHud toggled with F1. Audio Player Optional; plays the interface cues (click, build menu open/close, rally set, wave called). Pause Volume Sliders Master / Music / Effects / Interface sliders in the pause menu (on). Hero / Unit / Tower / Slot Click Size, … Click Offset Default click rectangles in world units (size, centre offset from the position). On Continue, On Quit UnityEvents for the result screen buttons and the pause menu's Quit (hidden when nothing is assigned in the Inspector; see SetNavigation for listeners added from code).

Text: Texts (the scene's TDGameSettings.Texts), static Describe(texts, failure) (the text of a rejected command).

Scripting: Configure(runner, registry, camera, theme, debugHud), Connect(), Refresh(), SelectTower(entityId), SelectBuildSlot(index), ClearSelection(), CancelAll(), CurrentMode (Browsing, BuildMenu, TowerMenu, RallyAiming, HeroSelected, UnitSelected), AimingSpell, SelectedHero, SelectedTower, SelectedUnit, HasSelection, the input entry points above, Theme, Canvas, Runner, SetPauseMenu(open), IsPauseMenuOpen, static EnsureEventSystem().

Hero skill UI is optional. The compact default shows a portrait and health bar per hero. HeroSkillButtons (Inspector: Hero Skill Buttons) enables small skill-purchase buttons when your hero uses SpendPoints; you can also supply your own allocation UI. The sample heroes use AutoUnlock, so they need no purchase buttons. Spell buttons retain cooldowns, hotkeys and aiming without a large background panel. Short feedback appears under the top bar. Early wave-call rewards update the gold counter and call button; WaveCalledEarly(int gold) is available for a custom notification.

Game flow from code. A menu script that adds onContinue/onQuit listeners at runtime calls SetNavigation(showContinue, showQuit, continueText, quitText) to choose which buttons show and their labels – text keys or literal texts (for example "Next Battle" only when a next level exists, and "Main Menu"); with both shown the result screen places them side by side. ClearNavigation() returns to the Inspector rule. The pause button in the top bar opens the same pause menu as Space/P/Esc. The campaign screens (world map, save slots) are described in Campaign. See the Demo sample (Samples/Demo/Scripts/DemoFlow.cs): one scene, one runner, levels swapped with SimulationRunner.Configure(null, levelAsset) + StartSimulation() (set StartOnPlay off so nothing starts behind the title screen).

Every value the HUD shows is read back from the simulation; failed or cancelled aims never send commands. Rules are never recomputed in the view: the sell price uses Simulation.PreviewSellRefund, the call-wave bonus and tooltip use PreviewEarlyCallReward, spell tooltips show PreviewEarlyCallSpellCooldownCut, the countdown ring is NextWaveRemaining / NextWaveWaitDuration, the rally cursor is drawn at the point TryResolveRallyPoint resolves (invalid points are refused before a command is sent), early-call feedback uses the GoldChanged delta that precedes WaveStarted, and the result screen shows the core's Victory star rating. Splash rings use ProjectileHit.Value for instant hits. Text is TextMesh Pro with the theme's font, and every string comes from the string tables (Text, fonts and languages).

docs.title: HudTheme
docs.text:
Create > 2D Tower Defense Maker > HUD Theme (HudTheme). All fields are optional; empty sprites use generated defaults (HudSprites).

Group Fields Canvas Reference Resolution, Match Width Or Height, Sorting Order Text Font (TMP_FontAsset; empty = the TMP Settings default), Font Material (optional preset), Fallback Fonts (for characters the font lacks, for example CJK), Body Font Weight, Button Font Weight, Small Font Size, Font Size, Large Font Size, Title Font Size, Text Shadow (underlay) Sprites Panel, Button, Circle, Ring, Bar (9-sliced where useful), icons for gold, lives, wave, incoming, star, pause, play, lock, damage Colours panel/button states, text, accent, gold, lives, wave, positive/negative, health, experience, cooldown shade, stars, overlay Controls Button Frame Color, Button Frame Sprite, Selected Text Color, Primary Button Color, Primary Text Color, Tooltip Color, Inset Color, Section Color; HudButton.SetPrimary marks the main action Layout Top Bar Height, Padding (spacing), Panel Padding (sample: 30), Screen Padding (24), Button Text Padding (18 horizontal / 10 vertical), radial menu radius and button size, spell button, portrait, wave indicator, tower panel width, button height World feedback range/preview/rally/hero/valid/invalid/slot-hover/unit-select colours, Range Fill Alpha, Outline Width, Ghost Alpha Damage numbers Damage Number Color, Heal Number Color, Damage Number Size

HudTheme.Default is the in-memory default; ResolveFont() returns the configured font or the TMP Settings default (null when the TMP Essential Resources are missing), or a runtime copy of it when Fallback Fonts are set (see below).

docs.title: DamageNumbers
docs.text: Add Component > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Damage Numbers. Pooled floating TextMesh Pro numbers (outlined) on a screen-space canvas, merged per target for a short window; digits are cached strings and the fade uses the canvas renderer alpha, so they do not allocate per frame. Fields: Runner, World Camera, Theme, Merge Window, Lifetime, Rise, Minimum Value, Max Numbers, Show Heals. Disabled when TDGameSettings.damageNumbers is off. Configure(runner, camera, theme).

docs.title: Text, fonts and languages
docs.text: All runtime text – GameHud, DamageNumbers and the sample menus – is TextMesh Pro (TextMeshProUGUI, built from code by HudUi.Label). TextMesh Pro is part of the uGUI package in Unity 6 (com.unity.ugui 2.0), so there is no extra dependency; the 2D Tower Defense Maker assemblies reference Unity.TextMeshPro.

docs.title: TMP Essential Resources
docs.text:
TextMesh Pro needs its Essential Resources (TMP Settings, the default LiberationSans SDF font asset and the SDF shaders) in the project once. 2D Tower Defense Maker does not ship them. When they are missing:

  • the editor logs one message per session and offers Import in a dialog;
  • Tools > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Import TMP Essential Resources (or Unity's Window > TextMeshPro > Import TMP Essential Resources) imports them into Assets/TextMesh Pro;
  • Validate reports an error in the Text category;
  • the HUD still builds and plays, but text stays invisible until the resources exist.

Batch: -batchmode -executeMethod TDMaker.Editor.TextMeshProSetup.ImportEssentials without -quit (the editor exits when the import finishes). Scripts can ask TextMeshProSetup.EssentialsImported.

docs.title: Fonts
docs.text:
Included sample typography. Both sample HUD themes explicitly use Inter 4.1 from Samples/Fonts/Inter/. Regular (400), Medium (500), SemiBold (600) and Bold (700) have separate static SDF atlases and real weight-face links: body text uses Regular, button titles SemiBold, button prices Medium and headings Bold. Small/body sizes are 20/24 and the sample text shadow is disabled. Button titles and prices use separate padded regions; long text fits or truncates inside its region. The original four TTF files and their SIL Open Font License 1.1 are included alongside the generated assets (ThirdPartyNotices.txt).

The static atlases use 80 pt sampling, 8 px padding and a 2048-square texture per face. They include the shipped English table and common Latin UI characters. If you add characters outside that set, regenerate the atlas or add a licensed fallback. Re-running Create Sample Content preserves existing Inter assets and their GUIDs.

HudTheme > Font takes a TMP_FontAsset; empty uses the default font asset of your TMP Settings. Font Material is an optional material preset (outline, glow ...); empty uses the font's own material, and Text Shadow adds a drop shadow through a generated underlay material (HudUi.TextMaterial, shared and cached per font, so labels keep batching). Damage numbers add an outline the same way; HudUi.SetOutline(label, theme, color, width) does it for your own labels.

To make a font asset: select a .ttf/.otf and use Assets > Create > TextMeshPro > Font Asset (or Window > TextMeshPro > Font Asset Creator for a static atlas).

docs.title: Chinese, Japanese and Korean (CJK) fonts
docs.text:
The bundled Inter faces and the TMP default LiberationSans font do not cover CJK scripts; without a CJK font those characters render as boxes (and TMP logs which characters are missing). Add one font that covers the language, as a dynamic fallback so only the glyphs you use are rasterized.

Sample Korean font. The samples include Noto Sans KR Regular (Samples/Fonts/NotoSansKR-Regular.otf, about 4.4 MB, SIL Open Font License 1.1 – Samples/Fonts/OFL.txt, see ThirdPartyNotices.txt) and a dynamic font asset made from it by the sample generator, Samples/Fonts/NotoSansKR-Regular SDF.asset (48 pt sampling, 1024 atlas pages, multi atlas, dynamic data cleared on build). Both sample HUD themes list it in HudTheme > Fallback Fonts, so the Korean sample table renders out of the box (switch TDGameSettings > Language to ko, or call the language API in your own UI; the optional sample title has no language buttons). The fallback is applied to a runtime copy of the HUD font, so your TMP Settings and the TMP default font asset are not changed. Keep the font and its license file together if you ship it; if Korean is not required, remove only the Noto Sans KR font and its theme fallback entries; keep the Inter folder and its license.

Adding a font for another language (Japanese, Chinese, another Korean typeface):

  1. Import a font file you are licensed to ship (for example Noto Sans JP / SC / TC, SIL Open Font License).
  2. Select it, Assets > Create > TextMeshPro > Font Asset > SDF. In the new asset set Atlas Population Mode = Dynamic, an atlas of 1024 (or 2048), Multi Atlas Textures on and Clear Dynamic Data On Build on.
  3. Add it to your theme's HudTheme > Fallback Fonts (tried in order after the HUD font's own fallbacks). Alternatives: the HUD font asset's own Fallback Font Assets list (required when HudTheme > Font is itself a dynamic font – Fallback Fonts only applies to static fonts and logs a warning otherwise), Project Settings > TextMesh Pro > Settings > Fallback Font Assets (every TMP text in the project), or the font directly as HudTheme > Font for a single-language build.
  4. Play the scene in that language once and check the console for missing-character warnings.

Keep Latin text in the primary font and CJK in the fallback: the HUD's numbers and the English fallback texts keep the primary font's metrics (CJK fonts have taller line metrics, so multi-line panels grow a little). Dynamic atlases fill while the game runs; in the editor the glyphs are written into the font asset (re-run Create Sample Content to reset the sample one). For a shipped static atlas, use the Font Asset Creator with your table's characters (Characters from File).

docs.title: String tables
docs.text:
Every user-visible HUD string is a key (HudTexts lists them, for example hud.pause.title, hud.tower.sell = Sell +{0}). Texts come from TDGameSettings.Texts (a TextResolver):

Order Source 1 TextResolver.Provider – an optional ITextProvider set from code (an adapter to the Unity Localization package, a spreadsheet import ...) 2 TDGameSettings > Text Tables whose language matches TDGameSettings > Language (later tables override earlier ones) 3 the English tables in the same list (en) 4 the built-in English texts (HudTexts.English) 5 the caller's fallback (Get(key, fallback)), then the key itself

A Text Table (Create > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Text Table, TextTable) has a Language Code (en, ko, de, zh-Hans ...; matched ignoring case, and ko serves ko-KR), a Language Name for menus and key → text entries. Empty texts count as missing, so a partly translated table works. Texts may use rich text (<b>, <color=#ff7766>) and {0}, {1} placeholders for numbers and names; preserve the placeholder indices, although translations may reorder them. A broken placeholder shows the text unformatted instead of throwing, and Validate reports placeholders the HUD does not fill.

The samples include Samples/Text/Text_English.asset and Samples/Text/Text_Korean.asset; the sample generator updates both. Sample scenes assign both tables and use en as their default language. Sample menu keys start with demo.*, campaign screen keys with campaign.*, and level titles and summaries use campaign.level.<key>.title and .summary. Content names and descriptions use the content.* keys below; missing translations display the asset's authored text.

Adding a language

  1. Duplicate Text_English (or create a Text Table), set Language Code and Language Name, translate the texts (leave a text empty to keep English).
  2. Add the table to TDGameSettings > Text Tables in your scenes (keep the English table in the list for keys you add yourself).
  3. Make sure the HUD font or its fallbacks cover the script (see CJK above).
  4. Select the language: TDGameSettings > Language in the Inspector, or TDGameSettings.Current.SetLanguage("de") from an options menu (GetLanguages(list) lists the codes of the assigned tables; LanguageChanged fires). Open HUDs and the sample menus relabel themselves on the next frame. With Persist Language on (default), the choice is saved in PlayerPrefs (Language Prefs Key, default TDMaker.Language) and loaded when play starts in a build (LoadLanguage()). In the Editor, Ignore Saved Language In Editor is enabled by default so the Inspector value takes precedence. Like volumes, the language is an app setting kept outside save slots.

Scripting: Texts.Get(key), Texts.Get(key, fallback), Texts.Format(key, a[, b[, c]]), Texts.FormatText(text, a), Texts.Has(key), Texts.Version (changes when the language, the tables or the provider change), Texts.Invalidate(); TextTable.TryGetText, Set, Remove, Clear, Entries; CachedText caches the formatted text of a key per number and language. HUD labels are updated only when their value changes, and the strings are cached per value (NumberText.Get(int) shares one string per integer; CachedNumber and CachedText keep the text of every value they have shown), so the HUD adds no per-frame allocation at any game speed – a count, timer or health value that comes back costs nothing; a language switch rebuilds the labels once. Top bar values and hero hints shrink (TMP auto size) instead of running past their panel in longer languages.

docs.title: Translating content names and descriptions
docs.text:
The game HUD uses ContentTexts to resolve names and descriptions for units, towers, heroes, spells, status effects, purchased abilities and hero skills. Keys follow content.<category>.<id>.<field>. Categories are unit, spell, effect and ability; fields are name and description. General units and status effects have no description field, so only their names are translated.

For example, content.unit.garrison_1.name, content.unit.militia.name and content.ability.piercing_shot.name translate Garrison, Militia and Piercing Shot. Both sample tables include content names and descriptions. Add keys following the same pattern for your own content. When a translation is absent, the original authored name or description is used.

Changing the display language preserves TemplateId and the authored DisplayName; it does not change core definitions, saves or command replay. Open tower panels, hero names and tooltips update when the language changes. Authoring tools such as Unit Workshop continue to show asset filenames and authored text.

docs.title: Presentation hooks, VFX and audio
docs.text:
Each entity asset's View has Hooks (PresentationHooks): Spawn / Attack / Hit / Death Vfx prefabs and Spawn / Attack / Hit / Death Cue audio cues. Projectiles have Launch Vfx, Impact Vfx, Launch Cue, Impact Cue; spells have Cast Vfx and Cast Cue. Every slot is optional.

AudioCue: Clips (one picked at random), Volume, Pitch Min/Max, Min Interval (prevents stacking), Spatial Blend. HasClips tells whether anything would play.

VfxPool (2D Tower Defense Maker > VFX Pool): Spawn(prefab, position, lifetime = -1) places a pooled instance; particle systems are restarted on reuse and the instance returns after its particle duration (or Default Lifetime). Max Active caps live instances. Implement IPooledVfx.OnSpawned() on a prefab component to reset custom state. Clear() returns everything.

docs.title: Audio
docs.text: Three components play sound: AudioCuePlayer (one-shot cues), MusicPlayer (loops and stingers) and TDGameSettings (volumes and mixer routing). All of them are optional and every cue or clip slot may stay empty (silent).

docs.title: Cues (AudioCuePlayer)
docs.text:
2D Tower Defense Maker > Audio Cue Player. Plays cues through a pool of AudioSources.

Field Meaning Voices Pool size = global voice limit. When every voice is busy the oldest one is reused. Max Voices Per Cue Copies of one cue that may sound at once (default 3, 0 = no limit). Together with each cue's Min Interval this keeps dense fights from stacking. Master Volume Extra volume of this player (multiplied with the Game Settings volumes). Cues Global events: wave started, wave callable, wave called (button/N, played by the HUD instead of the click), tower built / upgraded / sold, ability purchased, life lost, coin gained (an enemy with a bounty died; throttle with Min Interval), command rejected, spell ready, spell cast (fallback for spells without their own Cast Cue), hero moved (order approved), hero level-up, rally set, victory, defeat, UI click, build menu opened / closed. Mechanic Cues Built-in mechanic events: chain started, trap placed, trap triggered, beam started, healed (give it a long Min Interval), shield applied (an effect with a shield was attached), damage reflected, knockback (displacement), path transferred. Keyed Cues Key + Cue: replaces the mechanic default for one mechanic id (chain, trap, beam, pulse, reflection or transfer id) or plays on attach of one status effect id. SetKeyedCue(key, cue) from code. Ensure Listener On Start, adds an AudioListener to the main camera when the scene has none.

Per-template cues are on the assets (see above) and are routed by the EntityViewRegistry. Cues on the UI channel: UI click, build menu, command rejected; everything else is SFX.

Scripting: Play(cue), Play(cue, position), Play(cue, position, AudioChannel), PlayUi(cue), PlayUi(preferred, fallback), Keyed(key, fallback), StopAll(), ActiveVoices, static EnsureListener().

docs.title: Music (MusicPlayer)
docs.text:
2D Tower Defense Maker > Music Player. Two pooled loop sources crossfade (Crossfade, real seconds) and a third plays stingers.

  • Level music: Level Asset > Audio > Music (LevelMusicData): Battle loop, Intense loop, Victory / Defeat stingers, Volume. The intense loop is crossfaded in when a wave starts that matches a rule: Intense On Last Wave, Intense On Boss Waves (waves with Boss Wave ticked in the Wave Set – a presentation hint that is not baked into the core) or Intense From Wave (one-based, 0 = off).
  • Defaults on the Music Player (Menu Music, Battle Music, Intense Music, Victory Stinger, Defeat Stinger) are used for every slot a level leaves empty.
  • Menu music: plays while no simulation runs, or while the optional Battle Root object is inactive (assign the HUD a menu flow hides, as the Demo sample does). Follow Battle Root switches back to the battle loop when it shows again.
  • Stingers: Stinger Mode Stop Loop (default: the loop fades out) or Duck Loop (lowered to Duck Volume while the stinger plays). Paused Volume lowers the loop while the game is paused.

Scripting: PlayMenu(), PlayBattle(intense), PlayOutcome(victory), Stop(), CrossfadeTo(clip, volume), Current (Silent, Menu, Battle, Intense, Outcome), CurrentClip, IsPlaying, IsIntenseWave(wave), Configure(runner, battleRoot, menu, battle, intense, victory, defeat).

docs.title: Volume and mixer (TDGameSettings)
docs.text:
Master Volume, Music Volume, Sfx Volume, Ui Volume (0..1). A sound plays at cue volume × player volume × Master × its channel. With Persist Volumes on (default) the four values are loaded from PlayerPrefs on enable and written when they change (keys Prefs Key Prefix + Master/Music/Sfx/Ui; PlayerPrefs failures only log a warning).

Mixer routing is optional: assign Music Group, Sfx Group, Ui Group (AudioMixerGroup) to route each channel through your mixer for effects or snapshots. Volumes are applied on the AudioSources either way, so everything works without a mixer.

Options menu API: GetVolume(AudioChannel), SetVolume(AudioChannel, value), EffectiveVolume(channel), MixerGroup(channel), LoadVolumes(), SaveVolumes() (flushes PlayerPrefs), event VolumeChanged. The sample pause menu shows Master / Music / Effects / Interface sliders bound to these (GameHud > Pause Volume Sliders, on by default); closing the pause menu saves them.

docs.title: Sample audio
docs.text: The samples use the sound effects and music in Samples/Audio (Sfx/<key>.ogg, Music/<key>.ogg, generated with Stable Audio, see ThirdPartyNotices.txt). The sample generator assigns them by key (TDMaker.Editor.SampleAudio): tower families get shot sounds (tower_arrow_shot, tower_cannon_fire, tower_magic_cast), projectiles impact sounds (arrow_hit, cannon_explosion, magic_impact), enemies enemy_hit and enemy_death_small / enemy_death_big by size, soldiers sword_clash / soldier_death, spells their cast sounds, the audio player the global and mechanic cues, levels music_battle / music_battle_intense / music_victory / music_defeat, and the Demo scene music_menu. A missing file leaves its cue empty, so generation works (and stays deterministic) without the folder.

docs.title: Editor preview
docs.text: TDMaker.Editor.AudioCuePreview plays cues in the editor (edit or play mode): Play(cue), PlayClip(clip, volume, pitch), Stop(), IsPlaying, FromProperty(serializedCue), DrawCueRow(label, cue) and DrawSection(expanded, title, cues) (an "Audio" foldout with each cue's field and Play/Stop buttons) for custom inspectors and windows.

docs.title: Art sets
docs.text:
An ArtSet (Create › 2D Tower Defense Maker › Art Set) maps template view keys to sprites so a whole look can be swapped without code. Assign it on the EntityViewRegistry; keys without an entry fall back to the asset's prefab or a generated primitive. All three samples use BasicArtSet: original vector units, towers and separate painted maps. The Hound, Revenant, Gravecaller and Husk have their own entries. Imported sprites remain available even when external authoring tools are absent.

Per entry: View Key, Sprite, optional frame loops (Walk, Idle, Attack, Hurt, Death frames with their frames-per-second), Death Sprite + Death Hold (e.g. a grave shown briefly), Icon (menus and portraits), Scale, health-bar height/width, Walk Bob, and for projectiles Rotate To Flight, Impact Sprite / Impact Frames, Impact Size. Set-wide: build-slot sprite and scale, Draw Build Slots, health-bar back/fill/low sprites.

Facing direction – draw or import unit art facing either way. Right-facing art needs nothing; for art drawn facing left, tick Faces Left on its entry. Units face their movement direction; in a melee engagement (and when an attack starts) they use the simulation's latched facing (Entity.FacingX), so a blocker and its enemy face each other. Left- and right-facing sheets can be mixed in one set. (Requires the template's Facing to be FlipSprite or ScaleX.)

docs.title: Entity views
docs.text:
EntityViewRegistry pools one EntityView per entity (prefab from the asset's View, the registry's Overrides, or a generated primitive). View settings: Shape/Color/Size, Shaded (outlined style), Facing (None, FlipSprite, ScaleX), Show Health Bar, Drive Animator, Hooks.

Animator parameters – with Drive Animator on, an Animator on the prefab receives the parameters it declares (others are skipped):

EntityView.AnimatorParameters Type Set when Move Bool The unit moved this frame Speed Float Movement speed (units per second) Attack Trigger An attack starts Hit Trigger Positive damage is taken Die Trigger Death fade begins

Animator speed follows the game speed. Built-in feedback: hit flash, death fade, status-effect tint and icons, tower tier pips, projectile trails, impact flashes, splash rings, instant-hit beams, spell cast flash.

Mechanic feedback (see Mechanic Library): jagged arcs between chain victims, beams for multi-target attacks, rings for every region pulse (including pulse-only regions) and projectile impact areas, heal glows, a shield bubble that fades with the remaining capacity, dust rings on displacement, greyed disarmed units and translucent untargetable units, trap markers (dim while arming, detection ring once armed, trigger flash), pooled continuous beam lines that follow source and target, reflection and life-steal lines, and path-transfer trails. Colours come from each mechanic's Color (or the effect tint; transfers use the registry's Transfer Color); optional Vfx prefabs go through VfxPool. Registry toggles: Mechanic Arcs, Pulse Rings, Heal Glows, Trap Markers, Channel Beams, Reaction Lines.

docs.title: Camera, settings and ellipses
docs.text:
TDCameraController (on the orthographic camera) frames the level on start for any aspect ratio. Its bounds are the level geometry plus Padding and the HUD reserve (Hud Reserve Top/Bottom), or a fixed rectangle (Use Fixed Bounds, set by the Map Editor to the painted map). How the level is framed comes from the level's Camera Framing (LevelAsset.cameraFraming, or a scene override on Level Authoring):

Framing (mode) View Player camera Fit Whole Map (default) The whole map on one screen; other aspect ratios show the camera background at the sides or top/bottom None – no pan, no zoom Fit Height Scroll Horizontally View height = map height Pan left/right, zoom in Fit Width Scroll Vertically View width = map width Pan up/down, zoom in Fixed View Size viewHeight world units (capped to the map) Pan both ways, zoom in

startFocus picks the first view (Center, FirstEntrance, FirstExit of path 0) and introPan (introPanSeconds) pans along the first path from its entrance to its exit when the level starts, then settles on the start focus; any pan or zoom input skips it. Off-screen wave-call buttons are pulled to the screen edge, so scrolling levels still show every entrance. Fields: Padding, Min Zoom, Pan Speed, Edge Size, Zoom Step, Smoothing. FitToLevel(), Bounds, Framing, IntroPanActive, LeftDragging, VisibleRect(), static FocusPoint(level, area, focus).

By default the whole map is visible and the camera does not move. Scrolling is an opt-in per level for maps larger than the screen.

TDGameSettings: camera inputs – used only in levels whose framing scrolls – cameraPan (master), edgePan (off by default), dragPan (middle mouse), keyboardPan (WASD/arrows), cameraZoom (wheel, +/−), leftDragPan (left drag on the battlefield past a small threshold, not starting over UI; off by default; a press that became a drag is not also a click); speedControls (show the 1×/2×/3× buttons; off resets the speed to 1×); language and textTables (string tables; Texts, SetLanguage, GetLanguages, LanguageChanged); damageNumbers, confirmSell (off: selling is one click), showEarlyCallBonus (off by default), allowDebugOverlay. TDGameSettings.Current returns the scene instance (or a hidden default). Bind these to your options menu.

EllipseRenderer: EllipseRenderer.Create(name, parent, material, sortingOrder, width), then Show(center, range, yScale, lineColor, fillAlpha) / Hide() / SetWidth(width). The shape comes from RangeShape, so what is drawn is exactly what the simulation tests.

docs.title: Sample screenshots
docs.text: Tools > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Capture Sample Screenshot (TDMaker.Editor.SampleScreenshot) plays the Basic sample with a scripted run (builds on every slot, upgrades, calls waves early) and renders the camera with the HUD to a PNG. Batch: -batchmode -executeMethod TDMaker.Editor.SampleScreenshot.Capture without -quit and without -nographics (the editor exits by itself). Options: -tdmSeconds N (default 50), -tdmWidth / -tdmHeight (default 1920×1080), and -tdmOut folder for your chosen output folder. Script errors during capture are counted in the Console log.

docs.title: Language selection and click-area priority
docs.text:
The sample title screen's English and Korean buttons call TDGameSettings.SetLanguage. With Persist Language enabled, the choice is saved in PlayerPrefs. Builds load that choice when present, otherwise use the Inspector language. Ignore Saved Language In Editor is on by default so the current Inspector language controls that Play session; turn it off to test persisted-language loading. Turning off Persist Language stops saving new choices.

The default tower hit area includes its pad rectangle and the body SpriteRenderer's world bounds. Shadows, health bars and feedback decorations are excluded. When View > Click Area > Custom Area is enabled, only the authored rectangle is checked. Heroes keep selection priority; equal-priority overlaps prefer the lower anchor point. While aiming a move, rally point or spell, battlefield clicks remain point attempts.

Before wave 1, the entrance skull button shows the translated Start Wave label. Later, its ring shows the time until automatic wave start, and calling early uses the level's early-call reward rules. Twin Roads uses an early-call gold rate of 2 per second.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: Start with the Maker package to create your own game. The separate Samples add-on provides a reference game and feature examples; it is optional. See Maker and Samples for installation and ownership.

docs.title: Build your first level (about 5 minutes)
docs.text:
1. Open Tools > 2D Tower Defense Maker > New Level (also on the Welcome window, Tools > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Welcome).
  2. Enter a Level Name. The folder follows it (Assets/TDMakerContent/<Name>); change it if you like, but not to a folder inside Assets/TDMaker (the package).
  3. Optional: drop your painted map on Background. The default road and build slots are stretched over it and the camera is framed on it.
  4. Pick the Starter content:
  5. Fresh starter assets – a new enemy (Walker), an archer tower with a level 2 upgrade, a barracks with its soldier and, with Include Hero, a hero, all in the level's Data folder. Include Starter Spell is on by default and adds Reinforcements using the Footman in the same folder. Use Sample Sounds is off by default; enable it only when you want references to Samples/Audio.
  6. Sample kit – the Basic sample's towers, enemies, hero and spells (the level then depends on Samples/Basic).
  7. Set the number of Waves (default 3) and press Create Level.

You get <Folder>/<Name>.unity (open), <Folder>/Data/ with the Level asset, the Wave Set and the units, and the Map Editor open on the Paths tool. Then:

  1. Road. In the Scene view drag the road points where the road should run (Shift+click on the road inserts a point, Ctrl+click deletes). Points run from the entrance (ENTRY) to the exit (EXIT). See Editor Tools.
  2. Build slots. Press B and drag the six pads beside the road, or click to add more. Rally points snap to the nearest road.
  3. Units and waves. Tune the towers and the enemy in the Unit Workshop (Tools > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Unit Workshop) and the waves in the Wave Timeline.
  4. Check. Validate and Dry Run in the Map Editor (or Tools > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Validate Project / Dry Run Level). A sound level is lost without towers and won with a defense.
  5. Spells. Edit the starter spell in Unit Workshop, or create a Spell asset and add it to the Level asset's Spells list.
  6. Play. Build on an empty pad, then click the tower artwork or pad to upgrade it. Start the battle with the entrance skull button labeled Start Wave.

docs.title: Optional: play the Basic sample (1 minute)
docs.text:
Install the optional Samples add-on after the Maker package, then open Tools > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Samples > Browse Samples.

  1. Open Assets/TDMaker/Samples/Basic/BasicSample.unity.
  2. If the scene or its Data folder is missing, run Tools > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Samples > Regenerate Sample Content. It (re)creates all sample assets and the scene in place.
  3. If prompted, import TextMesh Pro Essential Resources (or use Tools > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Import TMP Essential Resources), then press Play.

The sample contains two multi-lane paths, five waves, six wave enemy types (including a shielding healer, a Revenant that returns once and a Gravecaller that raises weak Husks), four tower families (archer, cannon, arcane, garrison/barracks) with branching final tiers and purchasable abilities, the Warden with a Hound companion, two spells and five status effects. Volley Nest can buy Barbed Mines. The scenes use original vector maps, sprites and HUD art, with generated primitives as fallbacks.

docs.title: More samples
docs.text:
Scene What it shows Samples/Crossroads/CrossroadsSample.unity Three entrances whose roads merge before the gate, flying Gliders on a separate air route (dotted line; barracks cannot block them, cannons cannot hit them), a tough Marauder for the barracks, and two heroes – the Warden (skills unlock automatically) and the ranged Ranger (both sample heroes unlock skills automatically). Samples/WindingPass/WindingPassSample.unity One long serpentine road, Ironclads (high armor) and Runeguards (high magic resist) and a Bulwark boss; the Mortar family (minimum range, branches into armor-shredding Siege Mortar or slowing Tar Mortar, each with abilities) and a third spell, Hex Circle, that lowers both resistances. Samples/Demo/DemoSample.unity The playable sample flow: title screen, three save slots (delete with confirmation), the campaign world map (each win opens the next level and keeps the best stars), the three levels, pause menu (Resume / Restart / World Map) and result screen (Restart / World Map). Every action has an on-screen button. The world map also opens the permanent star-upgrade shop. See Campaign.

The three levels share gameplay assets and use separate original vector maps. Use Dry Run to compare undefended, fortified and budget-limited defenses, then play the level to check its pacing and controls.

docs.title: Default controls (PC)
docs.text:
Input Action Left-click an empty build slot Open the build menu; one click on an item builds it Left-click a tower Tower menu: upgrade / branch, buy ability ranks, target priority, sell, set rally (barracks) – each a single click Entrance skull button Before wave 1, the button shows Start Wave. Call later waves early for a bonus, or let the countdown ring finish to start them automatically. II / 1x / 2x / 3x Pause and game speed H, click a hero or its portrait Select a hero, then left-click a point to move it (any battlefield click while the hero is selected is a move) 1–9 or spell buttons Aim a spell; left-click a point to cast (empty ground included), right-click or Esc to cancel Esc / right-click Cancel every selection and aim (Esc with nothing selected pauses; right-click with nothing selected does nothing) Space / P, N, F1 Pause, call the next wave, IMGUI debug overlay Mouse wheel, middle drag, WASD Zoom and pan – only in levels whose Camera Framing scrolls (the samples show the whole map; see Game Settings)

The HUD is the TextMesh Pro/uGUI Game HUD, styled by PaintedHudTheme; see Presentation to restyle or replace it.

docs.title: Under the hood: a level asset by asset
docs.text:
The wizard only creates ordinary assets and components; this is the same level made by hand, useful when you want to know what each part does or build a scene layout of your own.

Create a folder for your content, for example Assets/MyGame/. All assets below are created with right-click in the Project window > Create > 2D Tower Defense Maker > … (also available from Assets > Create > 2D Tower Defense Maker).

docs.title: Step 1 – Enemy
docs.text:
1. Create > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Enemy, name it Enemy_Walker.
  2. Set Health (e.g. 40), Speed (e.g. 1.5), Gold (bounty, e.g. 5), Life Cost (1).
  3. Leave Melee enabled if barracks soldiers should take damage when they block it.

The inspector shows effective HP against different defense values.

docs.title: Step 2 – Tower
docs.text:
1. (Optional) Create > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Projectile, name it Projectile_Arrow, Kind = Homing, Speed = 12. Without a projectile an attack is an instant hit.
  2. Create > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Tower, name it Tower_Archer.
  3. Set Cost (e.g. 70). Under ranged attacks add one entry: Range 3, Cooldown 0.8, damage Physical 4–7, Projectile = Projectile_Arrow.
  4. Optional: create a second tower asset, then add it to the first tower's Upgrades list – or open Tools > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Upgrade Tree with the tower selected and press Add Next Level.

For a barracks, create a Soldier asset and assign it to the tower's Soldier field.

docs.title: Step 3 – Waves
docs.text:
1. Create > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Wave Set, name it Waves_Level1.
  2. Select it and open Tools > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Wave Timeline.
  3. Press + to add a wave. Add a group (path 0), then an entry: Enemy = Enemy_Walker, Count 8, Interval 1.2.
  4. Drag bars on the timeline to adjust delays; drag a bar's right edge to change the interval.

docs.title: Step 4 – Level asset
docs.text:
1. Create > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Level, name it Level1.
  2. Assign Waves = Waves_Level1, add Tower_Archer to Available Towers, set Starting Gold (e.g. 200) and Starting Lives (e.g. 20).

Upgrade tiers, soldiers and projectiles referenced by the available towers are collected automatically.

docs.title: Step 5 – Scene geometry
docs.text:
1. Create a new scene. Make the Main Camera orthographic (size around 6–7) and keep it tagged MainCamera.
  2. Create an empty GameObject Level and add Add Component > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Level Authoring. Assign Level = Level1.
  3. Create a child GameObject Path A with 2D Tower Defense Maker > Path Authoring.
  4. In the Scene view, Shift+click to add points (Shift+click on a segment inserts), drag points to move them, Ctrl+click deletes.
  5. Set Lane Count (e.g. 2) and Lane Spacing. Points run from entry (green, "ENTRY") to exit (red, "EXIT").
  6. Create a few child GameObjects with 2D Tower Defense Maker > Build Slot Authoring next to the path. Drag the Rally handle onto the road (used by barracks).
  7. Assign a Preview Tower to see its range ellipse around the slot.

Level Authoring collects child paths and slots in hierarchy order when its lists are empty. Wave groups refer to paths by index (first path = 0).

docs.title: Step 6 – Runtime objects
docs.text:
Create an empty GameObject 2D Tower Defense Maker and add:

Component (Add Component > 2D Tower Defense Maker > …) Setup Simulation Runner Assign Scene Level = the Level object. Entity View Registry Nothing required; it finds the runner. Level View Nothing required; draws a placeholder ground, path ribbons and slot pads. Game HUD Nothing required; uses Camera.main unless a camera is assigned. Optionally assign a HUD Theme. Damage Numbers, VFX Pool, Audio Cue Player, Game Settings Optional feedback and settings (Presentation).

Add Camera Controller to the camera to fit the level on start.

If the Entity View Registry has no Sprite Material, an unlit sprite material is created at runtime for the placeholder sprites.

docs.title: Step 7 – Check and play
docs.text:
1. Select the Level object and press Validate Bake in the Level Authoring inspector, or run Tools > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Validate Project.
  2. Optional: Tools > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Dry Run Level simulates the level headlessly and logs a report.
  3. Press Play, build towers, and press Start Wave.

docs.title: Sample tips and editor workflow
docs.text:
The complete packaged sample flow is Assets/TDMaker/Samples/Demo/DemoSample.unity.

  • Select English or Korean on the sample title screen. The choice is saved in PlayerPrefs, independently of campaign slots. A build uses the saved language when one exists, otherwise the Inspector language.
  • TD Game Settings > Ignore Saved Language In Editor is on by default so you can test Language = ko directly in Play mode. Disable it only when you want to test saved-language loading. Use the Korean table together with the sample theme's Noto Sans KR fallback.
  • Twin Roads, Crossroads and Winding Pass start with 1,200, 1,300 and 1,400 gold respectively, and each starts with 20 lives. Build a defense before calling wave 1; leaving the map undefended still loses the battle.
  • In Twin Roads, divide archers and arcane towers between the upper and lower roads and use barracks to hold enemies. In Crossroads, defend the merged roads and shared exit, with archers covering the flying route. In Winding Pass, mix arcane towers and mortars on inside bends where they cover several road sections, and buy time with barracks. Tier II upgrades are available before wave 1; heroes and spells are also available.
  • Creating a Unit Workshop asset clears search, type and tag filters, refreshes the list and scrolls to the selected row. The save dialog prefers the current user level's Data folder; otherwise it suggests the last user folder or Assets/TDMakerContent/Units.
  • A Wave Timeline group's + opens an enemy picker. The new entry copies the preceding entry's Count and Interval, so check both values. Double-clicking a group row copies its preceding entry instead.
  • Map Editor results remain above the scroll view. Click the error/warning summary for the complete list. Auto Rally for all slots asks for confirmation and can be undone in one step.

docs.title: Sample gallery
docs.text: The optional Samples add-on includes original vector artwork and four playable sample scenes. Install it after the Maker package, then open Tools > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Samples > Browse Samples. The Maker works without these examples; see Maker and Samples. Import TMP Essential Resources once before playing. These images show the included package samples.

docs.title: Battle HUD
docs.text: Build towers on the marked slots, upgrade them into branches, command the hero and use spells. The sample HUD uses Inter and separate padded text regions for button titles and prices. See Presentation to replace the theme, fonts and artwork.

docs.title: Title and campaign flow
docs.text: Open Assets/TDMaker/Samples/Demo/DemoSample.unity for the title, save slots, campaign map and three battles. The sample is included in the package. See Quick start and Campaigns.

docs.title: Permanent upgrades
docs.text: Spend campaign stars on ordered upgrade tracks, inspect each rank and undo or reset purchases. Configure the content through the upgrade shop assets. See Campaigns and upgrades.

docs.title: Getting help
docs.text:
Start with Quick Start and the FAQ. For content problems, run Tools > 2D Tower Defense Maker > Validate Project and review the first relevant error. Editor Tools explains how to open an issue in its authoring tool.

When contacting the publisher through the support details supplied with your Asset Store purchase, include:

  • Your 2D Tower Defense Maker package version and Unity Editor version.
  • The render pipeline and input backend you use.
  • Clear steps to reproduce the issue, the expected result and the actual result.
  • Relevant Console messages and, when useful, a small reproduction scene or screenshot.

Remove credentials and private project data from shared logs or reproduction projects.

docs.title: Public API reference
docs.text:
The generated API reference documents the public C# types and members in the package's three assemblies:

  • TDMaker.Core — Unity-independent simulation, templates, commands and deterministic rules.
  • TDMaker.Unity — authoring assets, views, HUD, campaigns, localization and runtime integration.
  • TDMaker.Editor — maker tools, validation, sample generation and online documentation entry points.

Start with Core concepts for the data flow or Extending the framework for integration examples. The product name is 2D Tower Defense Maker; the C# namespaces remain TDMaker.*.

The reference is generated from the package code. Unity and .NET types used in signatures belong to their respective platforms. Assembly binaries and the package implementation are not distributed with this documentation site.
